      definition.description + ' Supply exactly one request or complete inputRef; large results are retained as exact complete files.',
      input, ['workspace'], definition));
  return result;
}

# Use a saved pricing decision in merchant accounting

Import the original SF97 pricing report to use its exact payment options, USD
quotes and per-fulfilled costs in the existing merchant accounting engine and
workspace. The import keeps the complete original report and the assumptions
behind the pricing decision.

## Save the pricing decision

Use the [merchant pricing workspace](../sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/WORKSPACE.md)
to review the merchant's current session or retained history, enter the
commercial assumptions, and save a version. Download **Report JSON** from that
saved version, or use its private `versions/VERSION/report/report.json` file.

Select the original report, not `terms.json`. Both pricing files use the SF97
schema name, but the report contains the normalized payment options, source
hashes and calculated route values needed by this import.

## Create the accounting import

From a source checkout:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/pricing-cli.mjs \
  --report /private/merchant/pricing/versions/VERSION/report/report.json \
  --out /private/merchant/pricing-import-2026-10-11
```

Use an absolute path to a new output directory whose parent already exists.
The command validates the entire selection before creating that directory. It
does not replace an existing import. The resulting directory is private
(0700), and each file is private (0600):

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `accounting-terms.json` | Validated original accounting terms, including the pricing source and commercial context |
| `pricing-report.json` | The exact original report bytes, including all option metadata and observation detail |
| `manifest.json` | The original report and generated terms identities, sizes and import summary |

The command prints the generated terms path, original report hash, terms hash,
route and option counts, unknown-cost option count, and selected source range.
Keep the import directory with the pricing and accounting review it supports.

### Preserve a long or descriptive quote basis

Pricing accepts a descriptive quote basis up to 300 characters. The original
accounting format uses a shorter reference: 3–100 letters, numbers, spaces or
`_ . : / -`. If a pricing basis cannot be used directly, provide the accounting
reference explicitly:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/pricing-cli.mjs \
  --report /private/merchant/saved-pricing-report.json \
  --out /private/merchant/pricing-import-2026-10-11 \
  --reference "Approved merchant quote October 2026"
```

The reference applies to the imported options. Every full original route basis
is retained in `pricingProvenance.routes`, and the complete report stays beside
the generated terms. Text is never shortened or silently substituted.

## Use the original accounting workspace

For an existing workspace, open **Sources & imports**, select
`accounting-terms.json` under **Merchant accounting terms**, and choose
**Import & select terms**. Capture a new reconciliation from **Reconcile &
review**. Earlier runs keep their own original terms and source snapshots, so
the existing comparison can show the effect of the changed pricing decision.

For a new workspace:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --outbox /private/merchant/sf98-outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/sf86-results \
  --terms /private/merchant/pricing-import-2026-10-11/accounting-terms.json
```

Reopen that directory with `--workspace` alone. The [accounting workspace
guide](workspace/README.md) covers source selection, reconciliation, review
notes, comparison, retained exports and restart.

The original accounting CLI consumes the same imported terms:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/cli.mjs \
  --outbox /private/merchant/sf98-outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/sf86-results \
  --terms /private/merchant/pricing-import-2026-10-11/accounting-terms.json \
  --out /private/merchant/new-accounting-review
```

## What is mapped

Every original payment option becomes one accounting option in source order.
The original `compileTerms` implementation validates each option and the
complete result.

| Original pricing report | Accounting terms |
| --- | --- |
| `routeId`, `method` | The same route and method |
| `paymentOptions[].network`, `asset`, `payTo` | The same network, asset and recipient |
| `paymentOptions[].atomicAmount` | `amountAtomic`, unchanged as a decimal string |
| `quoteUsd` | `unitPriceUsd`, unchanged |
| `variablePerFulfilledUsd` | `unitCostUsd`, unchanged; unknown remains `null` |
| `priceBasis` or the explicit accounting reference | `priceBasis` |

SF97 applies one commercial quote and fulfillment-cost schedule to all
configured alternatives on that route. The import preserves that scope. It
does not choose the first option, derive an exchange rate, or allocate request
counters to a particular payment option.

The original accounting limits still apply: at most 200 distinct options,
supported Stellar networks and exact payment schemes, accounting-compatible
asset/recipient addresses, and its existing decimal precision and input-size
limits. A rejected option identifies its route and index. Duplicate accounting
identities fail as a complete selection; no option is silently removed.
Nonpayable example asset or recipient markers must be replaced in the
merchant's actual seller configuration before producing an accounting import.

## Retained context

`pricingProvenance` retains the original seller, commercial-terms and observation
hashes; the exact report hash when original bytes are supplied; merchant and
generation identity; session or retained-period range; the full original quote
bases; monthly targets; challenge costs; and shared fixed costs. The original
report file retains the complete source detail.

The retained pricing range describes the pricing observation. The
reconciliation's event scope comes from its selected native journals and
verification inputs.

Only the route quote and per-fulfilled variable cost become unit accounting
terms. Shared monthly costs, payment-challenge costs, monthly demand targets and
HTTP traffic remain pricing context. The existing settlement engine determines
which native events and independent network verifications match the imported
payment terms.

## Application integration

```js
import {
  createAccountingTermsFromPricingReport,
  preparePricingReportImport,
  writePricingReportImport,
} from './merchant-settlement-accounting/pricing.mjs';

// For a parsed original report. No original-byte hash is inferred.
const terms = createAccountingTermsFromPricingReport(report, {
  accountingReference: 'Approved merchant quote October 2026',
});

// For the exact file bytes or UTF-8 JSON received by an operator interface.
const prepared = preparePricingReportImport(originalBytes, {
  accountingReference: 'Approved merchant quote October 2026',
});
// prepared: terms, reportBytes, termsBytes, reportSha256, termsSha256, summary.
// Retain reportBytes and termsBytes together, using the existing private store.

// Complete create-only filesystem import used by the CLI.
const imported = await writePricingReportImport({
  reportFile: '/private/merchant/saved-pricing-report.json',
  outputDirectory: '/private/merchant/new-pricing-import',
});
```

These functions perform no payment or provider operation. The pure mapping
returns a new object without changing the input report. The byte preparation
retains exact source bytes; the filesystem writer adds regular-file, size,
stability and private-output checks. A changed saved report fails before
publication of an import.

# Merchant settlement accounting

This Node 22+ operator CLI and local workspace integrate the original native SF98 merchant delivery outbox and independently collected original SF86 testnet and public-network transfer-verification results. The [retained SF86 collection workflow](../sf86-rpc-transfer-reconcile/BATCH.md) prepares original checkout files, collects and resumes network reads, and produces this same report end to end.

It does not sign, purchase, authorize, retry payments, create invoices, or move assets. Existing SF30/SF98 native processSettlement success events come from `../sf98-merchant-delivery/outbox.mjs`, which is imported directly at runtime. Existing SF86 operator outputs retain the actual `stellar-forge.sf86.rpc-reconciliation.v1` schema and verified network-specific RPC response details.

## Operator workflow

For a complete accountant exchange, use [Accountant handoffs](accountant/README.md): label a completed original reconciliation or saved period close, retain a CSV and offline packet, preview returned bookkeeping references, and save matching changes with full revision history.

For a retained browser workflow with source imports, paginated ledger and exception review, before/after comparisons, named operator notes, and original report downloads, use the [merchant settlement workspace](workspace/README.md). It runs this same accounting engine and report writer directly; the command below remains available for one create-only report.

The workspace also connects the [original recovered-settlement source](RECOVERY.md), reviews and imports retained completed SF31 purchases, and preserves their original response downloads. Pass `--recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered-settlements` to this CLI to include that explicit source in a report. Native and recovered counts, source identities, and time bases remain separate in the original output.

On the original merchant host, retain its private SF98 outbox directory with its native `events.ndjson` and `deliveries.ndjson`. In another private directory retain the original authorized operator's SF86 reconciliation JSON result files. Source instructions for this first-party read-only original verification are at `../sf86-rpc-transfer-reconcile/README.md`. The report can be generated with no SF86 files, in which case all native successes remain unverified.

Prepare a private merchant terms JSON (schema `stellar-forge.merchant-accounting-terms.v1`), with a `routes` array containing one row for **each actual payment option**, up to 200 rows. A resource offering several networks, assets or recipients repeats its `routeId` and `method`. Each row has `routeId`, `method`, `network`, `asset`, `payTo`, `amountAtomic`, `unitPriceUsd`, `unitCostUsd`, and `priceBasis`. These values come from the approved original seller configuration and the merchant's own price records.

| Terms field | Original source |
| --- | --- |
| `routeId`, `method` | Compiled original SF30 route ID and HTTP method |
| `network`, `asset`, `payTo` | The corresponding complete `offer.accepts` entry |
| `amountAtomic` | That option's `amount`, retained as an exact decimal string |
| `unitPriceUsd`, `unitCostUsd` | Merchant-provided USD values, decimal strings to six places or `null` for unknown |
| `priceBasis` | The merchant's description of the approved quote basis |

Both `stellar:testnet` and `stellar:pubnet` terms are accepted. The `asset` is the actual checked C-contract StrKey; `payTo` is the actual checked G-account or C-contract StrKey. Atomic amounts are positive signed-i128 decimal strings, matching the original verifier. No automatic currency conversion occurs. The complete key is route ID, method, network, asset digest, atomic amount and recipient digest. Duplicate complete keys are rejected, including duplicates with conflicting prices. Different actual options on the same resource are retained independently.

From the current original repository root:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/cli.mjs \
  --outbox /private/merchant/sf98-outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/sf86-results \
  --terms /private/merchant/pricing.json \
  --out /private/merchant/new-reconciliation-report
```

The output directory must be absolute, normalized, private, and nonexistent. It is created at mode 0700. Six create-only mode-0600 files are written:

| Output | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `report.json` | Existing ledger, route totals, exceptions and lineage, with additive payment-option groups and mapping metadata |
| `ledger.csv` | Every native event, with original columns retained and selected recipient digest, option ID, mapping result, candidate count and verification scope appended |
| `options.csv` | Each configured payment option, including options with no events, plus separate unconfigured or unresolved native groups |
| `exceptions.csv` | Original event/route/reason columns, followed by method, network, option ID and terms mapping |
| `review.html` | Original route and event views, complete option identity and quote/cost terms, separate per-option atomic totals and operator exceptions |
| `manifest.json` | Exact SHA256 input and output lineage |

HTML is offline, mobile/print friendly, grayscale and script-free. Its event and exception rows link directly to the relevant option section. CSV rows expose opaque event IDs and hashed asset/recipient/transaction/receipt/order references, not original wallet addresses or raw buyer data. Original private source inputs are unchanged.

## Selected option and older journals

New original SF98 events add `recipientDigest`, the SHA256 of the selected native payment requirement's `payTo`. The native event retains its existing `stellar-forge.sf98.delivery-event.v1` schema, event ID and deduplication behavior; existing journal entries are not rewritten. No raw recipient address is added to the journal or these reports.

The accounting report records the following mapping results:

| `termsMatch` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `EXACT_OPTION` | All six recorded identity fields match one configured option |
| `LEGACY_UNIQUE_OPTION` | Recipient was not recorded, and the remaining five fields match exactly one configured option |
| `AMBIGUOUS_LEGACY_OPTIONS` | Recipient was not recorded, and the remaining fields match more than one recipient option; the event remains unverified |
| `MISSING_ROUTE_TERMS` | The route and method have no configured merchant terms |
| `OPTION_TERMS_MISMATCH` | The route exists, but its configured options do not match the event's recorded identity |

`recipientDigest` in the event ledger always represents what the original journal recorded, or `null` when absent. `termsRecipientDigest` separately records the matched merchant term's recipient. This preserves the difference between a recorded recipient and a unique legacy mapping. `termsCandidateCount` shows how many actual options remain. Proof contents never choose a recipient from an ambiguous set, and the first configured option receives no preference. Resolve historical ambiguity using the merchant's original settlement/configuration records.

The opaque `optionId` joins each ledger row to its report/CSV/HTML option group. It is a deterministic hash of the six terms, not a payment receipt. Unresolved legacy rows use a distinct recipient-unknown group and cannot merge into a configured recipient group. Configured options with no events remain visible for comparison.

Each option group reports `nativeAmountAtomic` and `officialMatchedAmountAtomic` as exact integer strings. These sums stay within the same route, method, network, asset, per-event amount and resolved recipient. Route and grand totals retain event counts and verified merchant USD quotes; they never add together atomic units from different options. Unknown legacy recipients are explicitly labeled in their own groups.

## Operational evidence boundary

`NATIVE_SUCCESS_UNVERIFIED` means the original native SDK reported a settlement success, but no matching independent SF86 official transfer proof was provided. It is not financial recognition.

A valid `stellar:pubnet` native event joins its own matching original SF86 public-network proof and receives `verificationScope: OFFICIAL_PUBNET_RPC`. Without matching proof it retains `PUBLIC_NETWORK_PENDING` and the corresponding exception. Testnet rows retain `OFFICIAL_TESTNET_ONLY`. Proof lookup, transaction reuse and unused-proof counts all include the network, so identical fingerprints on different networks remain independent.

`OFFICIAL_TRANSFER_MATCHED` requires the original SF86 network-specific verdict (`CHAIN_TRANSFER_MATCHED_RPC_TESTNET` or `CHAIN_TRANSFER_MATCHED_RPC_PUBNET`), its matching RPC source, one exact SEP-41 transfer, and the same transaction fingerprint, network, asset, recipient and atomic amount as the selected original option. Public-network proof additionally binds the listed provider, canonical passphrase, network/transaction response hashes and event-page hashes. A recorded native recipient digest must agree. The [network contract](../sf86-rpc-transfer-reconcile/NETWORKS.md) describes these fields and legacy testnet compatibility. `LOCAL_RPC_REPLAY_MATCHED` remains excluded. Reused native transaction fingerprints and conflicting proof rows downgrade rather than double count. The transfer stays bound to a seller-reported transaction hash; delivery and financial recognition use the merchant's original records.

`WEBHOOK_ACCEPTED_NOT_FULFILLED` means SF98 received a 2xx webhook acknowledgment, not proof of merchant order fulfillment. Exhausted deliveries are exceptions even if the original transfer matched.

`verifiedQuotedValueUsd` is the independently transfer-matched quantity multiplied by the merchant's *own quoted USD unit price*. It is not realized revenue, an exchange-rate valuation, or a payout. Unknown costs remain unknown. No challenge-only 402 count, successful 2xx response, or unverified event is upgraded into sale or cash evidence.

This module complements existing SF97 merchant forecasting, SF93 support, SF98 delivery notifications, and SF82/SF86 chain reconciliation. The optional local workspace retains operator state on private disk. The original accounting engine and CLI remain usable independently.

## Focused source exercise

The original single-option implementation's local private CLI flow was exercised with native SF98-shaped event journal rows and exact SF86-shaped official/local proof schemas, including distinct official matches, ignored local replay, duplicate transaction guard, exhausted delivery and its original five output files. That developer exercise used an isolated temporary disk-journal adapter, not the authenticated merchant payment host; only the original operator can produce a live signed purchase and genuine official-RPC receipt. Multiple-option reporting retains those original SF86 proof criteria and existing outputs, with the additive option fields and `options.csv` described above.

# Recover a completed native purchase into merchant accounting

Use this workflow when an original SF31 buyer completed a purchase and retained
its native outcome and delivered response, but the seller did not capture an
SF98 settlement event. It recovers that existing transaction into the original
merchant report and keeps the delivered bytes available to the operator.

The recovery CLI reads the original files, calls the original SF86 independent
Stellar RPC verifier, and saves a private entry whose origin is
`RECOVERED_ORIGINAL_SF31_OUTCOME`. The ordinary SF81/SF36 preauthorized buyer path
continues to use its existing reservation record. Recovery does not create that
record, call a buyer or signer, send an SF98 webhook, or contact the merchant.

Use the maintained [native commerce operator guide](../sf66-demo-launcher/OPERATOR.md)
for setup and service operation. The original
[facilitator operating workflow](../native-facilitator/OPERATIONS.md) provides
`--probe`, `/readyz`, shared signer ownership and orderly drain. Recovery consumes
the completed outcome from that lifecycle and can run after its service has
closed, using the same retained transaction and delivered response.

## Retain the actual source files

Use the same Node 22+ installation and installed `@stellar/stellar-sdk` as the
original buyer. The maintained SF88 installation also supplies the existing
SF43 decoder. No additional package is required.

The input directory must contain the actual retained sources. Keep it private
with mode `0700` and each file `0600`.

| File | Required original content |
| --- | --- |
| SF31 outcome | `intentId`, `status`, `resource`, `requirement`, `settlement`, `receipt`, `httpStatus`, and optional `contentType`. The accepted state is `DELIVERED_REPORTED_SETTLED` with a successful native receipt and a successful HTTP response. |
| SF31 request | The complete intent originally supplied to the SF31 `approve(intent)` callback. A retained wrapper containing `intent` is also accepted. It includes the exact URL, method, accepted terms and request body identity. |
| Merchant terms | The existing `stellar-forge.merchant-accounting-terms.v1` file used by this component. One option must match route, method, network, asset, amount and recipient exactly. |
| Saved response, optional | The original response writer's saved bytes, plus its recorded byte count and SHA-256. The importer checks those values before retaining a copy. |

For an in-process integration, retain the original values at their existing
boundaries. The outcome JSON cannot serialize an HTTP `Response` object; retain
the listed scalar outcome fields and the original native requirement/receipt.
The original response writer already provides the saved body identity. Do not
include signer credentials, x402 authorization headers, or private keys.

A source file's authority remains a retained client record. The independent
ledger check establishes the exact transfer; it does not put the HTTP route or
the operator's source-file selection into the blockchain transaction.

### Create the recovery request

Create a private JSON file with this structure, using the actual source paths,
trusted payer, existing merchant route, and original response identity:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-recovery-request.v1",
  "outcomeFile": "/private/purchase/outcome.json",
  "requestFile": "/private/purchase/request.json",
  "termsFile": "/private/merchant/prices.json",
  "routeId": "patch-record",
  "payer": "REPLACE_WITH_THE_ORIGINAL_TRUSTED_G_ADDRESS",
  "rpcEndpoint": "https://soroban-rpc.testnet.stellar.gateway.fm",
  "httpsProxyEnv": "HTTPS_PROXY",
  "response": {
    "file": "/private/purchase/response.json",
    "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_THE_ORIGINAL_RESPONSE_WRITER_SHA256",
    "bytes": 80
  }
}
```

The payer comes from the original wallet owner. The response byte count shown
above is an example field; use the original writer's actual value. Omit
`response` if no body was retained, and always omit it for `HEAD`. A retained
empty body is valid. Saved bodies may be up to 64 MiB.

Omit `httpsProxyEnv` for ordinary direct public HTTPS. If the operator selected
an HTTP CONNECT proxy, name its environment variable explicitly. The existing
SF31 transport pins the selected RPC origin, keeps TLS verification, and does
not follow redirects. It does not read arbitrary proxy variables or persist
the proxy URL. The RPC provider comes from original SF86's declared network
profile; a receipt cannot choose its own provider.

The recorded resource must be HTTPS. An original loopback HTTP resource is also
accepted for a completed `stellar:testnet` development purchase. Recovery never
requests that resource and does not change the production buyer's HTTPS policy.

## Review, import, and reopen

Run commands from the original repository root:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/recovery-cli.mjs review \
  --config /private/purchase/recovery-request.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/recovery-cli.mjs import \
  --config /private/purchase/recovery-request.json \
  --recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/recovery-cli.mjs list \
  --recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered
```

`review` is offline. It checks exact original request/outcome agreement, maps
the complete merchant option using the existing compiler, and hashes the
retained sources. It does not import the SDK or read a signing key.

`import` performs read-only `getNetwork`, `getTransaction` and `getEvents`
through the original SF86 verifier and SF43 SDK event decoder. The network
passphrase, successful transaction, asset contract, actual token payer,
recipient and atomic amount must match. Its public-RPC match is retained
alongside the source files. Testnet and pubnet use their respective original
network profiles. A local RPC replay cannot create a recovered entry.

The importer stores one entry per SHA-256 of `network + "\n" + transaction`.
An identical later import returns `ALREADY_IMPORTED` without another RPC run.
A different route or source binding for that same transaction returns
`RECOVERY_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_BOUND_TO_DIFFERENT_SOURCE` and preserves the
existing entry. Changed retained files are detected when reopening. Successful
imports become visible by one directory rename after their files are synced.

## Open the already-delivered result

Use the recovery ID printed by `import` or `list`:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/recovery-cli.mjs response \
  --recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered \
  --id RECOVERY_SHA256 \
  --out /private/purchase/reopened-response.json
```

This verifies the retained sources and response hash, then creates a new private
file containing the original bytes. The destination must not already exist.
The command does not request the seller again, repeat a mutation, or pay again.

## Use the original merchant report

Keep using the merchant's existing SF98 outbox, SF86 proof directory, and current
merchant terms. Add the recovered source to the original reporting workflow:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/recovery-cli.mjs report \
  --recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered \
  --outbox /private/merchant/sf98 \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/sf86-proofs \
  --terms /private/merchant/prices.json \
  --out /private/merchant/reports/new-reconciliation
```

The command calls the existing accounting CLI and its report writer. It uses
the same option matching, independent proof classification, transaction
deduplication, JSON ledger, CSV tables, HTML review and output manifest.
Recovered entries retain their own origin and do not increase the count of
captured SF98 native events. The accounting engine handles transaction reuse
across both sources in one place. The original journals remain unchanged.

A merchant with no native events can use an existing empty private outbox and
proof directory. The recovered transfer carries its own original SF86 proof.
For a native testnet XLM development purchase, set the merchant's USD price and
cost fields to `null` and use an explicit testnet price basis; recovery does not
create a fiat valuation or identify the native asset as USDC.

## Reusable source contract

`recovery.mjs` exports:

| API | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `reviewRecoveredSettlement({configFile})` | Offline resolved payment option, original request identity, selected RPC and source hashes. |
| `importRecoveredSettlement({configFile,recoveredDir,signal?})` | `IMPORTED` or `ALREADY_IMPORTED`, retained entry and original proof. Trusted integrations may supply the existing verifier's `fetchImpl` and `decodeContractEvent` seams. |
| `readRecoveredSettlements(recoveredDir)` | `{entries,hashes}`; each entry is `{data,fileDigest,proof:{data,fileDigest}}`. Every source and saved response is rechecked. |
| `readRecoveredSettlement({recoveredDir,recoveryId})` | The same validated entry/proof for one recovery, without scanning the store. |
| `readRecoveredResponse({recoveredDir,recoveryId})` | Verified original body bytes, SHA-256 and content type for an existing operator surface. |
| `exportRecoveredResponse({recoveredDir,recoveryId,outputFile})` | Create-only private copy of those bytes and its identity. |

The canonical engine accepts `recoveredDir` as an optional input to
`runOriginalAccounting({outboxDir,proofDir,termsFile,recoveredDir})`. The maintained
accounting workspace can retain that source alongside its ordinary fixed
inputs and keep its existing report, review-note and run-comparison features.

Each entry directory contains `entry.json`, `outcome.json`, `request.json`,
`terms.json`, `proof.json`, and optional `response.bin`. `entry.json` uses schema
`stellar-forge.merchant-recovered-settlement.v1`; it records the actual recovered
origin, import time, complete selected option, transaction, request body
identity, source byte counts/hashes, and saved response identity. The receipt
fingerprint explicitly uses canonical receipt JSON, since the original HTTP
header bytes need not have been retained. It is not presented as an SF98
captured-header fingerprint.

The recovered store is an immutable private source, separate from the SF98
sender queue and original buyer budget ledger. Deleting or editing its contents
is not a refund or a new accounting event. The existing merchant reconciliation
classification remains the authority for reports.

# Accountant handoffs

The **Accountant handoffs** area in the merchant accounting workspace takes a completed reconciliation through an accountant's returned bookkeeping file. Prepare a labeled CSV, retain an offline handoff, preview the accountant's changes, and save the matched references beside the original payment records. Reopen any earlier handoff or return later.

## Open the workspace

Use the existing [merchant workspace command](../workspace/README.md). The maintained distribution exposes the same application:

```sh
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace
```

For a source checkout, run:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace
```

Open the printed local address, enter your operator name, and choose **Accountant handoffs**. Completed reconciliations from the original workspace appear immediately. When recorded-activity periods are installed, saved period closes appear in the same source selector.

## Prepare a handoff

1. **Choose the original source.** Select a completed reconciliation or a saved period close. The source summary shows its original networks, event count, and transfer matches. A period close carries its frozen exception notes and the original period scope.
2. **Add useful account labels.** Each original payment option has separate asset, unit, account code, and account name fields. For example, an XLM option can use `XLM`, `stroops`, and the merchant's clearing-account code. Labels describe the existing amount; the displayed atomic amount keeps its original exact value. Options on different networks or with different assets remain separate.
3. **Name and retain the handoff.** Use a name that the merchant and accountant recognize, such as `October recorded activity — first review`. Saving retains the exact source report, source identifiers, labels, preparation time, and operator.
4. **Download the accountant CSV or complete archive.** The archive includes an offline HTML review, the editable CSV, structured handoff, original report, and a file manifest. A period-based handoff also includes the original period close and frozen review notes.

The original report manifest and input manifest travel with the packet, retaining the source hashes and captured-file references used by the original reconciliation. Individual files remain available in the local workspace.

## Carry refunds and cancellations into the books

Record the later customer operation in the workspace's **Adjustments** area, then prepare the accountant handoff from the original reconciliation. Each payment keeps its original gross amount alongside verified refunds, pending refund requests, remaining amount, and recorded cancellations. The row detail and offline review show the refund's native transfer time separately from the merchant's cancellation effective date.

A handoff freezes the adjustment state that was selected when it was saved. Choosing a saved period close uses that close's original adjustment files; later refunds appear in a newly prepared live handoff. For example, a payment of `50000` atomic units with a verified refund of `12000` remains a gross payment of `50000`, with `12000` returned and `38000` remaining. A cancellation remains a separately dated merchant record. Pending refund requests stay separate from verified returned money.

The complete archive includes `adjustments.json`, the full history in `adjustments.csv`, and an offline `adjustments.html` review. These same original files accompany every returned bookkeeping revision. Their source hash, per-payment amounts, refund status and latest operation dates are protected columns in the accountant CSV. Edit the four bookkeeping columns below and retain the supplied header. To account for a later adjustment, create another handoff from the updated reconciliation.

Structured summaries group exact atomic amounts by network and asset. A verified return above the original gross payment is visible as an over-return and negative remaining amount; it is preserved for review. Older saved handoffs retain their original CSV template and source.

## Return the bookkeeping file

The accountant edits four columns in the supplied CSV:

| Column | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `externalStatus` | `UNREVIEWED`, `REVIEWED`, `BOOKED`, or `EXCLUDED` |
| `externalBookRef` | External journal or transaction reference; required for `BOOKED` |
| `externalAccountCode` | The account used in the external books |
| `externalNote` | Review explanation or follow-up, including multiline text |

Several events can share an external reference when the accountant posts a batch journal. Account labels prepared by the merchant stay in their own protected columns; the accountant's actual account code goes in `externalAccountCode`.

Keep the complete header and the protected source columns. Import numeric-looking source values as text in a spreadsheet so an amount such as `50000` keeps that exact representation. The CSV uses UTF-8 and normal quoted fields. Reordered columns and rows, a UTF-8 byte-order mark, LF or CRLF line endings, and quoted multiline notes are supported.

In the workspace, select the handoff's **Latest retained version**, name the return, choose the CSV, and select **Preview returned file**. The preview reports matched changes, unchanged rows, conflicts, unknown rows, and original events missing from the return. Inspect the per-row results before selecting **Save matched changes**.

An exact, valid row updates its four bookkeeping fields. An omitted row keeps its previous saved assignment. A row with a changed amount, network, option, source identity, or other protected value keeps its previous assignment and appears as a conflict. Duplicate or cross-wired source identities protect every affected original event. Other valid rows in the same file can still be saved. The full returned file and its conflict results stay available with that revision.

For a correction, download the latest accountant CSV, correct the returned fields, and preview it again. Each save adds a revision. Earlier CSVs, returned files, offline reviews, and complete archives remain available through the version selector. If another return was saved while a preview was open, load the latest version and preview again so the new import uses the current assignments.

## Inspect the result

The event table shows each original method, route, network, exact atomic amount, current bookkeeping status, and external reference. Filter by status or search the source and returned fields. Open an event to see its complete original record, the merchant's labels, the accountant's current assignment, and its last change attribution.

The summary distinguishes original event counts from the accountant's `BOOKED`, `REVIEWED`, and `EXCLUDED` statuses. Original testnet or public-network classification remains visible. Merchant USD quotes and unknown costs keep their original meaning and value; labeling an event or attaching a journal reference does not recalculate its amount or valuation.

## Retention and integration

Handoffs and returns live in the original private workspace under `accountant/`. A saved return contains the exact uploaded bytes, its complete current assignment set, per-row outcomes, the parent revision, the original source binding, and updated CSV/HTML/archive downloads. The original workspace's filesystem lease, revision checks, atomic state save, and operator history also govern this workflow. Stable request IDs make a repeated completed save return the same retained result.

The local interface accepts returned CSV files up to 64 MiB. It retains up to 2,000 handoffs and 2,000 returns per handoff, subject to the original workspace's overall state limit. Close the application before backing up the private workspace directory. Reopening the same directory restores the handoffs and all saved versions.

The [engine contract](SCHEMA.md) documents the pure `createHandoff`, `importReturn`, `renderCsv`, `renderHtml`, and inspection APIs. The connected `AccountantWorkspace` uses that engine through these routes:

| Route | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/accountant` | Retained handoffs, original closes, and current workspace revision |
| `GET /api/accountant/source?runId=…` | Prepare a completed original reconciliation; `closeId` selects an original close |
| `POST /api/accountant/handoffs` | Retain a labeled source handoff |
| `GET /api/accountant/handoffs/:id` | Inspect the selected handoff and returned version |
| `GET /api/accountant/handoffs/:id/rows` | Page and filter original events with current assignments |
| `POST /api/accountant/handoffs/:id/preview` | Preview exact returned bytes against the current saved return |
| `POST /api/accountant/handoffs/:id/returns` | Save the reviewed result using its ID, timestamp, digest, parent, and workspace revision |
| `GET /api/accountant/handoffs/:id/download/:name` | Download an immutable retained file |

Inspection and downloads accept `revisionId=initial` or a saved return ID; omitting it selects the latest saved return. Writes use the original local workspace JSON header and operator identity. The original merchant accounting report stays the shared source for the browser, pure engine, and service adapters.

# Accountant handoff and return contract

`engine.mjs` is the accountant adapter for the original merchant settlement accounting workspace. A handoff retains a completed original reconciliation and optional original recorded-activity close. An accountant receives its CSV, adds external book references, statuses, account codes and notes, and returns that same template. Each saved return is a complete immutable revision of those external assignments, including any conflicts and omitted rows.

The original report remains the source for amounts, network, selected payment option, transfer evidence, delivery classification, source time and quoted USD. The adapter reads those records directly. The original period module owns selection and closing; the accountant adapter consumes its saved snapshot and hash.

## Pure API

All functions are synchronous and perform no provider or state-writing operations. The shared reconciliation module loads its original network catalog at import. The existing workspace owns private source capture, request revisions, file persistence, downloads and idempotent save receipts.

```js
import {
  createHandoff, importReturn, inspectHandoff, renderCsv, renderHtml,
  validateHandoff, validateRevision, parseReturnCsv, accountantColumns,
  HANDOFF_SCHEMA, RETURN_SCHEMA, CSV_COLUMNS,
  PROTECTED_COLUMNS, EDITABLE_COLUMNS, EXTERNAL_STATUSES,
} from './engine.mjs';

const handoff = createHandoff({
  id, name, actor, createdAt,
  reportBytes,
  source: {
    runId, reportSha256, manifestSha256, inputManifestSha256,
    // Optional original saved close:
    periodClose: { id: closeId, revision: closeRevision, sha256: closeFileSha256 },
  },
  periodCloseBytes,
  labels: [{ optionId, assetLabel, unitLabel, accountCode, accountName }],
});

const csvBytes = renderCsv(handoff);
const revision = importReturn({
  id: importId, name: importName, actor, createdAt,
  handoff, csvBytes: returnedCsvBytes,
  parentRevision: previousSavedRevision ?? null,
});

const completeCurrentCsv = renderCsv(handoff, revision);
const offlineHtml = renderHtml(handoff, revision);
const inspection = inspectHandoff(handoff, revision);
```

`id` defaults to a new UUID; `createdAt` defaults to the actual current ISO timestamp. Workspace previews pass the same proposed ID and timestamp to the explicit save so the saved revision digest exactly matches the review. `name` is at most 160 characters; `actor` at most 1,000. All source hashes are lowercase SHA256. `reportBytes` and `periodCloseBytes` accept a Buffer, Uint8Array or UTF-8 string; every supplied source is checked against its retained exact-byte hash.

`source.periodClose` may be absent or null; its bytes must then be absent or null. With a close, the original snapshot's ID, revision and hash are required. Its schema must be `stellar-forge.merchant-period-close.v1`; its ID, positive integer revision, run ID, report hash and input-manifest hash must match the selected original source. Its retained `scope` must equal the original report's `period` object. The original export ID, review-notes hash and review-snapshot revision are retained with its original period definition. The workspace retains the original close and review bytes together with the report. This adapter compares those original fields without selecting dates, recalculating period membership or performing another close.

Labels are optional and supplied for actual `optionId` values from the report. Duplicate labels or unknown options are rejected. `assetLabel` is an operator's currency or asset name; `unitLabel` describes the displayed unit. These labels do not set asset precision or exchange rates. Native `amountAtomic` stays an exact string. Account labels on the handoff remain protected; the accountant's returned account code has its own editable column. Changing source labels requires a new handoff.

## Frozen adjustment source

`createHandoff` accepts optional `adjustmentsBytes` (Buffer or Uint8Array) with `source.adjustmentsSha256`. The bytes contain the original `stellar-forge.merchant-adjustment-export.v1` snapshot from `workspace.adjustments.snapshot(runId)`. The adapter checks the exact byte hash, original run/report/manifest/input-manifest identities and complete original report. It rebuilds the event totals from the snapshot's retained adjustment records through the original adjustment engine before accepting them.

A selected period close binds this same source through its saved `adjustmentsSha256`. The connected workspace reads the close's retained JSON, CSV and HTML companions. A live reconciliation captures one current snapshot. Original closes and handoffs without adjustment files retain their previous source contract.

The accepted handoff adds `source.adjustments` containing `schema`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `workspaceRevision`, `exportedAt` and `dateBasis`. Each row adds `adjustments`: exact-string `grossAmountAtomic`, `refundedAmountAtomic`, `pendingRefundAmountAtomic`, `remainingAmountAtomic`, `availableRefundAmountAtomic`, `cancelledAmountAtomic`, `overRefundedAmountAtomic`; `refundStatus`; `adjustmentCount`; and the latest verified `latestRefundTransferAt` and recorded `latestCancellationEffectiveAt`. The gross amount equals the original row. Remaining equals gross minus verified returns; available subtracts pending requests and clamps at zero. External over-returns keep their exact amount and a negative remaining value.

`summary.adjustments` contains adjusted/refunded/cancelled row counts, adjustment count, and exact amount groups keyed by original network and asset identity. It never adds different networks or assets together. Refund dates come from the verified native transfer; cancellation dates come from the retained merchant record. The original report's period and time basis remain their original source fields.

`accountantColumns(handoff)` returns the exact CSV columns for that handoff. It includes `sourceAdjustmentsSha256` and all row adjustment fields when the source has adjustments. `CSV_COLUMNS` remains the original template for legacy callers. `renderCsv` and `importReturn` select the correct template automatically; direct parsing uses `parseReturnCsv(bytes, {columns: accountantColumns(handoff)})`. Every added adjustment field is protected during return matching.

The initial packet and every returned packet carry the exact selected `adjustments.json`, `adjustments.csv` and `adjustments.html`. Later workspace changes therefore leave all saved handoffs and bookkeeping returns tied to their selected source.

## Retained schemas

### Handoff

Schema: `stellar-forge.merchant-accountant-handoff.v1`.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `name`, `actor`, `createdAt` | Handoff identity and preparation record |
| `source` | Exact run/report/input-manifest/report-manifest identity and optional original close-file identity |
| `sourceHashes` | Original reconciliation's input lineage, copied unchanged |
| `sourceAccountingStatus` | Original accounting status, copied unchanged |
| `sourceOptions` | Original report's complete option groups, copied unchanged |
| `labels` | Operator-supplied option labels |
| `rows` | Frozen original ledger rows with handoff row IDs, exact original-row digests and labels |
| `summary` | Source-event, option, network, origin and missing-label counts |
| `integrity.sha256` | SHA256 of canonical JSON for the record excluding `integrity` |

Each `rows` entry is `{rowId,eventId,sourceRowSha256,original,label}`. The complete original ledger row is in `original`. `sourceRowSha256` hashes that entire row's canonical JSON, including original fields beyond those displayed in the CSV. `rowId` hashes the handoff ID, original report hash and event ID. The event's existing `eventId` is preserved independently.

`summary` contains `totalRows`, `optionCount`, `nativeCapturedRows`, `recoveredRows`, `testnetRows`, `publicNetworkRows`, `officialTransferMatches` and `missingLabelRows`. Its optional `adjustments` member groups exact atomic totals by original network and asset identity.

### Returned revision

Schema: `stellar-forge.merchant-accountant-return.v1`.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `handoffId`, `handoffSha256`, `sourceReportSha256` | Exact handoff/source binding |
| `parentRevisionId`, `parentRevisionSha256` | Previous saved immutable return, or null for the first return |
| `createdAt`, `actor`, `name` | Import observation and operator |
| `importSha256`, `importBytes` | Hash and size of the exact returned CSV bytes |
| `assignments` | Complete current external assignments for every original handoff row |
| `results`, `issues` | Row-level outcomes, protected-field conflicts, invalid edits and unmatched rows |
| `missingRows` | Original rows absent from this return, preserving their preceding assignments |
| `summary` | Import outcomes plus complete current assignment counts |
| `integrity.sha256` | Canonical record hash excluding `integrity` |

Each assignment includes `rowId`, `eventId`, the four editable values, and `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`, `revisionId` for its last actual change. A returned row that exactly repeats its preceding assignment is `UNCHANGED`; the preceding assignment's attribution is preserved.

`summary` includes `totalRows`, `returnedRows`, `appliedRows`, `unchangedRows`, `conflictRows`, `unknownRows`, `missingRows`, `ignoredBlankRows`, `unreviewedRows`, `reviewedRows`, `bookedRows`, `excludedRows`, and `outcome`. `outcome` is `CONFLICTS` when any conflicting or unknown return row exists, otherwise `PARTIAL` when source rows were omitted, otherwise `COMPLETE`. COMPLETE describes return coverage; individual external statuses remain visible.

`inspectHandoff(handoff, revision?)` returns metadata in `handoff`, original `source`, `sourceHashes`, `sourceOptions`, source `summary`, optional `revision` metadata/current summary, joined `rows`, `issues` and `missingRows`. Each joined row preserves `original` and `label`, with the current assignment fields alongside them. The workspace pages this view for browser requests. `validateHandoff(handoff)` and `validateRevision(handoff, revision)` return their validated record or throw `AccountantError` with `code`, `message`, `status`, and optional `details`.

## CSV contract

The output is UTF-8, comma separated, with a header, quoted cells and CRLF record endings. Quoted quotes and multiline notes use the normal CSV representation. Import accepts LF or CRLF, a UTF-8 BOM, reordered columns and reordered event rows. Every header must appear exactly once; unknown or missing columns are a file error. Empty data records are ignored. Invalid UTF-8, malformed quoting, oversized inputs and duplicate headers are file errors; the operator can correct the input before previewing again.

Only these columns are editable:

| Column | Accepted values |
| --- | --- |
| `externalStatus` | `UNREVIEWED`, `REVIEWED`, `BOOKED`, `EXCLUDED`; an empty cell means `UNREVIEWED` |
| `externalBookRef` | Up to 200 characters; required for `BOOKED` |
| `externalAccountCode` | Up to 160 characters |
| `externalNote` | Up to 4,000 characters; quoted multiline text is supported |

BOOKED retains the accountant's report of an external entry. Its reference can be shared by several original events when an external book uses a batch journal. The report's original transfer class, asset units, quoted USD and network remain independently visible beside that external status.

All remaining columns are protected: handoff/run/report/close identities, row and original-row hashes; event/option/asset/recipient/amount; transaction, receipt, proof and recovered-response fingerprints; original time/time basis/origin; native transfer, delivery, exception, mapping and verification fields; merchant quote/cost/basis; and operator-supplied labels. `accountantColumns(handoff)` is the maintained exact ordered list for the selected handoff. Numeric-looking native amount strings are compared as strings; a spreadsheet-modified amount such as `50,000`, `5E4` or `50000.0` conflicts with source `50000`.

Spreadsheet formula triggers are escaped reversibly with one leading apostrophe. Literal leading apostrophes and numeric text containing more than 15 digits are escaped as well, so large native amounts retain their complete text when opened in a spreadsheet. The complete original source remains unchanged in `handoff.json`. Import compares protected values to their original text or that reversible exported representation. Editable values emitted by this adapter round-trip without repeated apostrophes. Formula text in a newly returned note is retained as text and escaped when the adapter emits another CSV. HTML exports escape every source and returned value.

## Partial returns and conflicts

The parent revision supplies the starting assignment for every source event; the first import starts with UNREVIEWED and empty external fields. A present, exact-source row supplies all four editable fields, so clearing a field is explicit. Omitted rows preserve their preceding assignments.

A protected-field mismatch, invalid edit, mismatched row/event pair or repeated target leaves every affected original event at its preceding assignment. All occurrences of a duplicated target are conflicts, even if one occurrence looks valid. A cross-wired pair that names two different source events protects both targets. Unknown rows are retained as unmatched outcomes. Other exact, valid rows in the same return can apply, and their complete result is available in the preview before an explicit workspace import.

Row outcomes are `APPLIED`, `UNCHANGED`, `UNKNOWN_ROW`, `DUPLICATE_ROW`, `IDENTITY_CONFLICT`, `PROTECTED_VALUE_CONFLICT`, `INVALID_EDIT`, or `ROW_LENGTH_MISMATCH`. Results preserve CSV record numbers and physical starting line numbers. Protected-field conflicts retain exact expected and received text. Raw CSV bytes remain in the workspace's immutable return packet.

The engine supports up to 22,000 source rows, 50,000 returned records, 128 MB original reports and 64 MiB CSV inputs. The connected workspace uses the same 64 MiB CSV upload limit. These are input bounds; no background polling, third-party booking, source modification or provider submission is performed by the pure adapter.

# Merchant customer statements

This workspace prepares customer purchase and service usage statements from the original merchant accounting ledger and the original SF101 API-pass export. It keeps the original payment once per purchased order, retains actual call outcomes and unit balances, and produces a customer document, purchase CSV, service call CSV and a file manifest.

The desk is available at **Customer statements** in the merchant accounting operator interface, at `/customer-statements/`. It uses the accounting runtime’s existing state, revision control and lease. The standalone entry opens the same original workspace:

```sh
node customer-statements/cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --port 8447
```

## Operator workflow

1. **Create or select a customer.** Save the customer reference, name and optional email/address. These fields form the customer document header. The account note remains an internal workspace field.
2. **Assign original order references.** Paste one original SF101 checkout reference per line, optionally followed by a tab and a customer-facing description. Assignments are explicit; routes, recipients and wallet fingerprints do not identify customers. Bulk assignment supports up to 2,000 orders per operation.
3. **Import original service usage.** Download the complete original API-pass export from the merchant receiver and choose its JSON file. The importer retains the exact source bytes and their SHA-256. A purchase-only statement can use the accounting report without a usage capture.
4. **Choose a completed original accounting run.** Select the customer, run and optional service capture. An optional UTC period selects native purchase capture times, with an inclusive start and exclusive end. Service usage remains cumulative at the source capture time.
5. **Review the prepared statement.** Check original amounts, transfer classification, adjustments, customer orders, service units and any excluded assignments. Each asset/network/selected recipient has its own total. The original merchant USD valuation is shown separately.
6. **Retain the document.** The workspace freezes the reviewed customer profile, original ledger projection, adjustments and usage capture. It allocates a statement number and writes the retained files before committing their references to the existing accounting state.
7. **Deliver the prepared files.** Open the document register to download the print document or CSVs. The HTML is a standalone, script-free document suitable for printing. Delivery stays in the merchant’s existing customer communication workflow.

The original merchant accounting interface remains the entry for collecting native sources, importing official transfer results and running reconciliation. This module consumes those retained results.

### Corrections and withdrawals

Customer profiles and order assignments have explicit versions. A reassignment to a different customer requires the operator’s correction reason and is recorded in the original workspace history. Earlier retained documents keep their original customer snapshot.

Use **Prepare correction** on a current retained document to prepare a replacement for the same customer. Retaining the correction marks the earlier document as superseded and links both document IDs. **Withdraw document from current register** records the operator and reason while retaining the original files. Current filenames include the document’s register status, and `status.json` exports its current status and history.

A document correction changes the customer document register. Original payment, refund and service entitlement changes continue through their existing merchant controllers.

## Original source joins

The statement engine takes a hash-verified completed `stellar-forge.merchant-reconciliation.v1` report from the original accounting workspace. A purchase row joins to a customer only through an explicit order assignment whose SHA-256 equals the original report’s `orderReferenceDigest`.

A service capture joins only when all of these original values agree:

- Raw order reference and its ledger digest.
- Original SF98 event ID.
- Route ID, method and network.
- Exact atomic payment amount and asset digest.
- **Observed recipient digest**, including the original null value for a legacy order.

The comparison follows the original SF101 receiver’s order/event binding. A selected merchant term’s recipient is retained separately as `termsRecipientDigest`; it cannot replace a missing observed recipient in the entitlement join.

Assigned orders with no selected native purchase, more than one matching event, a recovered rather than native source, or a mismatched usage identity remain visible in the excluded-order section. A missing order in an otherwise valid usage capture preserves the original accounting purchase and identifies the missing usage capture for that row.

### Payments, adjustments and usage

The purchase amount is retained in its original atomic units. Totals stay separate by network, asset and selected recipient. Official transfer matches preserve their original testnet or public-network scope. The customer statement keeps the original delivery outcome and reconciliation exception.

Refund and cancellation values come from the existing accounting adjustment functions. Verified refunds, pending refund requests and recorded cancellations remain distinct. The complete validated original adjustment records are used for the calculation; the customer document projects their identifiers, kind, status, amount and times.

A prepaid service order records its original purchase once. Later calls describe how that purchased allowance was used. The usage CSV therefore contains service units and outcomes, while the purchase CSV contains one original payment row per order.

| Original durable call status | Consumed units | Reserved units |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `IN_FLIGHT` or stored `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` | 0 | Original route unit price |
| `COMPLETED` | Original route unit price | 0 |
| `CONSUMED` | Original route unit price | 0 |
| `RELEASED` | 0 | 0 |

The displayed status can show deadline-derived recovery while the stored call remains in flight. The importer uses the original **stored status** for unit arithmetic. A completed application response, including an HTTP error response, retains the unit treatment recorded by the original service core.

Customer records include the response status, content type, byte count and SHA-256 when the original response is retained. Call bodies, bearer tokens, customer account notes and merchant variable costs are outside the customer projection.

## Supported usage imports

### Original installed API-pass export

The primary importer reads `stellar-forge.sf101.api-pass-export.v1` directly from the original [API-pass implementation](../../sf101-merchant-receiver/api-access/). It uses the real native export fields:

| Export field | Statement use |
| --- | --- |
| `pass.native` | Original order, event, payment terms and entitlement time |
| `pass.plan.title` | Purchased service label |
| `pass.planSha256` | Actual canonical plan identity |
| `pass.manifestSha256` | Exact purchased file revision; must equal `pass.native.fileSha256` |
| `pass.usage.allowanceUnits` | Purchased units |
| `pass.usage.consumedUnits` | Used units |
| `pass.usage.reservedUnits` | Reserved units |
| `pass.usage.availableUnits` | Remaining units |
| `calls` | Complete original call history |
| `snapshot.capturedAt` | Actual source capture time |
| `snapshot.stateSha256` | Original durable snapshot revision |
| `snapshot.callCount` and `snapshot.actionCount` | Completeness checks against retained calls/actions |

The native export captures the pass, all calls and operator actions in one original database view. The importer checks the declared capture counts, unique requests, each call’s purchased route/method/path/unit price, durable outcome counts, consumed units, reserved units and the complete allowance balance. An export with remaining pages or a mismatched count is rejected.

The normalized statement keeps `planSha256` and `manifestSha256` separately. Its shared service projection uses the actual canonical plan digest as `planId` and the exact purchased file digest as `planRevision`.

Each native export describes one purchased API pass. To prepare a statement for that pass, select its customer and original purchase record/capture. Other assigned purchases in the selected report remain visible with their own original accounting outcomes.

### Shared service usage capture

The agreed aggregate adapter shape is also supported:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.sf101.service-usage-export.v1",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-11T22:30:49.343Z",
  "revision": "actual-original-snapshot-revision",
  "orders": []
}
```

Each order supplies `orderRef`, original `eventId`, `routeId`, `method`, `network`, `amountAtomic`, `assetDigest`, `recipientDigest`, `entitledAt`, `planId`, `planLabel`, `planRevision`, and exact integer strings `unitsPurchased`, `unitsUsed`, `unitsReserved`, `unitsRemaining`. Used plus reserved plus remaining must equal purchased. An unentitled order carries null event and entitlement time together.

This aggregate shape carries original service totals. The installed native export additionally carries validated full call history.

## Files and state

The module adds `customerStatements` to the original `workspace.json`. It stores customers, explicit order bindings, usage input metadata, document register entries, numbering and operation history. All mutations use `workspace.serial()`, the existing lease, `workspace.expected(revision)` and the original durable commit.

Exact service inputs are stored under:

```text
inputs/customer-usage-<sha256>.json
```

Each retained document uses the existing accounting export directory:

```text
exports/<statement-uuid>/statement.json
exports/<statement-uuid>/statement.csv
exports/<statement-uuid>/usage.csv
exports/<statement-uuid>/statement.html
exports/<statement-uuid>/manifest.json
```

The manifest records exact file byte counts and SHA-256 values. Downloads recheck those hashes and use a fixed filename allowlist. The files and directories use the original workspace’s private storage and are part of its operating-state backup closure.

`status.json` is a current register export generated when requested. It is separate from the immutable document files. Existing document files retain the customer and accounting state at the moment they were retained.

### Retry behavior

A retention request includes a stable `requestId`, the original workspace revision and the reviewed `previewSha256`. A retry of the same request returns its existing retained document before applying a stale-revision check. Reusing that ID for different content produces a conflict. A new request validates the current revision and recomputes the exact preview from the retained report, usage bytes, customer assignments and current original adjustments.

The browser keeps a pending request in session storage when available. If a reply is lost, **Retry same retention** recovers the original document. A saved result remains saved even if a later register refresh fails.

Usage input imports are deduplicated by exact source bytes. CLI exports write new files exclusively and accept an existing output only when its bytes already match.

## CLI operation

The installed Node entry is `customer-statements/cli.mjs`, exporting `customerStatementsMain(argv)` for distribution integration. Run `help` for the full command list.

```sh
node customer-statements/cli.mjs state --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace
node customer-statements/cli.mjs customer-save --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --input customer.json
node customer-statements/cli.mjs orders-assign --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --input assignments.json
node customer-statements/cli.mjs usage-import --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --file original-api-pass-export.json --revision 12 --actor merchant-operator --name "API pass capture"
node customer-statements/cli.mjs preview --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --input selection.json
node customer-statements/cli.mjs retain --workspace /absolute/merchant-accounting-workspace --input retention.json
```

Use the actual revision returned by the current workspace, and the actual IDs returned by the original operations. The example revision above is a command-shape example.

A customer request includes `revision`, `actor`, `reference`, `name` and optional `email`, `address`, `note`. Editing adds the existing `id` and `expectedVersion`.

An assignment request includes `revision`, `actor`, `customerId` and `orders: [{orderRef, label}]`. Explicit cross-customer corrections add `reassign: true` and `reason`.

A selection contains `customerId`, `runId` and optional `usageId`, exact UTC `from`/`until`, and `replacesId`. Retention adds `revision`, `actor`, `requestId` and the returned `previewSha256`.

`show`, `statements`, `bindings`, `export` and `withdraw` expose the same document register and correction workflow. `--input -` accepts one JSON object from standard input; `export --output -` streams the exact retained file.

const statements = new CustomerStatementWorkspace(workspace);
await statements.init();

# Accepted delivery notices in merchant accounting

This operator pane connects accepted SF98 destination notices to the existing merchant settlement accounting workspace. It keeps each original event identity, the accepted request body identity, the prepared accounting source selection and the resulting original reconciliation together.

Open **/delivery-notices/** on the address printed by the [existing accounting server](../workspace/server.mjs). The pane uses that server, its workspace lifecycle, its selected merchant terms and verification sources, and its original reconciliation runner. The links to the settlement workspace and customer statements return to their existing interfaces.

## Start with the accounting destination

Use the original accounting workspace arguments and add the name of its delivery signing environment when incoming notices should be enabled:

~~~sh
node workspace/server.mjs \
  --workspace /private/accounting-workspace \
  --outbox /private/accounting-destination-outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/sf86-results \
  --terms /private/accounting-terms.json \
  --delivery-secret-env ACCOUNTING_SF98_SECRET
~~~

The named environment is supplied to the server process through the existing secret-management path. The browser shows its name and whether a value is available. It does not receive the secret value.

The configured outbox is the accounting destination's **original native-format event directory**. The retained notice must match the exact full original event in that directory. The backend checks that match when accepting the notice and again when the original accounting capture reads the event.

The fixed incoming endpoint is **POST /sf98/accounting-events**. Configure the original SF98 destination sender with its native signing contract. Where a reverse proxy is used, expose this receiver path while keeping the loopback operator routes private. Operator mutations continue through the accounting server's existing Host, Origin and **X-Workspace-Request: 1** checks.

Incoming signing availability governs acceptance of new notices. Previously accepted notices can still be inspected and captured when that environment is temporarily unavailable.

## Complete an operator review

1. Open **Delivery notices** and check the accounting workspace directory and connected destination outbox.
2. Select an accepted delivery. The pane preserves the original event ID, route, network, method, order reference and atomic amount. Acceptance time is distinct from the time recorded in the original event.
3. Review the selected accounting sources in the settlement workspace. Merchant terms, verification-file selections and the recorded-activity period belong to that original workspace.
4. Return to the notice, enter the operator and capture name, then choose **Capture selected sources**. The browser retains the request ID before sending the mutation.
5. Follow the retained capture's original status. **Open reconciliation** selects its actual run in the settlement workspace. Completed runs also expose their existing offline review and full report JSON downloads.
6. Continue customer work through **Customer statements** and the original accounting review/export surfaces.

A capture reconciles the configured destination outbox and the accounting sources selected when its intent is prepared. The result can include other original events from that outbox; it is not restricted to the selected notice. Atomic amounts are displayed without converting them to decimal token amounts or currency.

The page refreshes while it is visible and live refresh is enabled. Active original runs are checked more frequently. A fresh capture is disabled while the selected notice already has a queued or running reconciliation; that run's status and navigation remain available.

## Recover the original capture

Each browser request retains the event ID, UUID, operator, name and revision in session storage before POST. Recovery storage is scoped to the server-owned accounting workspace directory and destination outbox. Refreshing the page or reopening the same tab reuses that original request.

An accepted prepared capture can also be recovered from **Retained capture history** in a fresh browser. **Review recovery** loads its actual retained UUID, name and actor into browser recovery storage. **Recover same request** submits those same values. The original backend finds an existing accounting run before applying a new-request revision check.

A new capture request is identified by a new UUID. Editing the name or actor while reusing a retained UUID is rejected as a conflict. Prepared source selections remain visible in the capture history.

| Observed state or error | Operator behavior |
| --- | --- |
| The POST response was lost or timed out | Recover the retained UUID. The server returns its original capture or run. |
| STALE_WORKSPACE before acceptance | Refresh the exact notice. When GET confirms that the UUID has no accepted capture, retry the same UUID/name/actor with the current revision after reviewing current sources. |
| RUN_IN_PROGRESS | Keep the prepared request and recover it after the other original accounting run finishes. |
| DELIVERY_CAPTURE_SELECTION_CHANGED | Inspect the retained prepared selection and current accounting sources. Use **Use current selection for a new capture** to keep the old request in history and prepare an explicit new request. |
| NOTICE_SOURCE_CHANGED or EXPECTED_NATIVE_EVENT_CHANGED | Restore or inspect the exact original source event and configured outbox before recovering the same capture. |
| CAPTURE_REQUEST_CONFLICT | Compare the retained UUID, event, name and actor. Recovery uses the original values. |
| Accounting maintenance is active | Open the settlement workspace to complete its existing operating recovery, then recover this same capture request. |
| A run is failed or interrupted | Inspect its original run and source records. A later explicit capture can use the operator's newly reviewed source selection. |

The pane preserves unresolved browser request identity when a response is uncertain. The server retains accepted prepared requests and their original source-selection history, including requests superseded by a later operator-selected capture.

## Receiving the original destination

The original destination CLI includes export, inspect and receive:

~~~sh
starforge delivery-destinations export \
  --workspace /private/destinations --to /private/portable

starforge delivery-destinations inspect --workspace /private/portable

mkdir -m 700 /private/accounting-receiving-parent

# Set DELIVERY_FINGERPRINT to the exact fingerprint returned by inspect.
starforge delivery-destinations receive \
  --workspace /private/accounting-receiving-parent/received \
  --from /private/portable --fingerprint "$DELIVERY_FINGERPRINT"

starforge delivery-destinations status \
  --workspace /private/accounting-receiving-parent/received/workspace
~~~

The receiving target must be absent and its existing parent must have mode 0700. The receiver creates the original source under **received/source** and the original destination coordinator under **received/workspace**. Original journal bytes, destination descriptors, cursors and event identifiers are retained. The transferred state starts without an active worker.

Use the outbox path reported for the intended accounting destination by the received coordinator's status. The source outbox and each routed destination retain their own identities.

The accounting workspace itself uses its existing operating backup and recovery workflow, which preserves accounting runs, notices and customer statements. Existing completed accounting captures retain their original immutable source paths. The destination exchange carries native delivery state; original accounting backup/restore controls the accounting workspace and its retained run history.

After receiving the original native destination directory, point the accounting workspace's outbox argument at that directory. Review its current merchant terms, verification files and period in the existing settlement interface. Accepted-notice capture uses the resulting native source identity and original accounting runner.

## HTTP interface used by the pane

| Method and route | Result or input |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/delivery-notices?offset=0&limit=50&state=all | Workspace revision, server-owned source directories, signing availability, totals and the current page of accepted notices. The filter also accepts pending or captured. |
| GET /api/delivery-notices/EVENT_ID | The exact accepted notice and newest-first prepared capture history. |
| POST /api/delivery-notices/EVENT_ID/capture | JSON object containing revision, actor, requestId and name. The original capture UUID is reused for recovery. |
| GET /api/runs/RUN_ID/download/review.html | Existing completed reconciliation's offline review. |
| GET /api/runs/RUN_ID/download/report.json | Existing completed reconciliation's full report. |

The original server returns errors as an error code and a human-readable message. Workspace revisions are passed through unchanged. Event identifiers in URLs are encoded; all provider/source strings inserted into the page are escaped or assigned as text.

The notice view includes receivedAt, occurredAt, routeId, method, network, amountAtomic, orderReference, eventSha256 and bodySha256. Its capture history includes requestId, name, actor, createdAt, preparedRevision, sourceSelection, runId, status and the original error/code. The signing object exposes only environment and available.

The backend limits the retained bridge to 10,000 distinct notices and 5,000 prepared capture requests, alongside the original accounting workspace/run limits.

## Files and composition
