# Recorded-activity periods and retained closes

The **Periods & closes** area adds saved UTC intervals and immutable close
revisions to the existing merchant accounting workspace. It uses the original
accounting engine, exception reviews, comparison, and archive writer. Open the
workspace with the same [merchant-host command](README.md#open-on-the-merchant-host);
the installed distribution's `merchant-accounting-workspace` command includes
this area in the same application.

## Choose the reporting interval

Enter a period name, a UTC start, and a UTC end. The start is included and the end
is excluded. Both fields accept seconds and milliseconds, so adjacent intervals
can share an exact boundary without counting that boundary twice.

| Original source | Timestamp used for period selection |
| --- | --- |
| `SF98_NATIVE_CAPTURE` | The original event's `at`, labeled `NATIVE_SETTLEMENT_CAPTURED_AT` |
| `RECOVERED_ORIGINAL_SF31_OUTCOME` | The retained entry's `importedAt`, labeled `RECOVERY_IMPORTED_AT` |

These are recorded-activity intervals. A recovered outcome enters the interval
containing its import timestamp. Its transaction may have settled earlier; the
workspace does not substitute an inferred ledger timestamp for the retained
source's time basis.

Select **Save & select version** to retain the definition and choose it for future
reconciliations. Editing a saved period creates another definition under the same
period identity. The earlier versions remain selectable. **Copy to editor** uses
a retained version as the starting point for another definition; it leaves the
retained version unchanged. A note can record why the coverage changed.

The current choice appears above every operator area, including pricing and RPC
collections. Select **Use all recorded activity** to restore the original
all-source behavior. Existing workspaces begin with all activity selected when
first opened with this version.

## Capture and inspect the original result

Name a run and select **Capture period sources**, or use the main reconciliation
form with the current period selected. Queueing pins the exact period identity,
version, name, start, and end to that run. Later selection or definition changes
affect future runs.

The capture retains the complete original journal prefixes, selected accounting
terms, verification results, any selected original pricing report, and the
connected recovered collection. Source bytes are never shortened to the period.
The original engine first validates all captured events, resolves payment terms,
classifies proof matches, and checks network-plus-transaction reuse across native
and recovered origins. It then selects rows in `[from, until)` and passes those
rows to its existing route, option, exception, and total summaries.

An outside-period event therefore still participates in conflict and reuse
handling for an inside-period transaction. The following scopes remain explicit:

| Result | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Event ledger, exceptions, route and payment-option totals | Selected recorded-activity interval |
| Configured payment options with zero selected events | Still visible through the original option summarizer |
| Source SHA-256 identities, ignored proof files, unmatched official proof count | Complete captured sources |
| Verification-file and recovered-source browser views | Complete captured inputs |
| `period.sourceCounts`, `period.selectedCounts`, `period.excludedCounts` | Separate counts for every captured, selected, and outside-period record |

Amounts remain the original decimal strings. The recorded interval does not
change an original proof classification, the meaning of a native SDK success,
or the merchant's quoted USD valuation.

## Retain a close revision

Choose a completed period reconciliation, name the close, and record any useful
handoff context. Select whether to include the private captured sources, then
select **Retain close revision**. Open and investigating exceptions are retained
with their original classifications and named review notes.

Each close receives a sequence number within its saved period, including when a
later close uses another definition version. It records the previous close
identity, original run and report identity, period definition, coverage counts,
workspace revision at close, and frozen review counts. A source-inclusive close
also retains the complete original source files and any saved recovered response
bytes in its archive.

**Close history** keeps every revision available. Inspect a close to compare each
frozen note with its current workspace review, including the full note, reviewer,
assignee, status, version, and time. A later review does not change the earlier
close or its download. The source-inclusive checkbox explains when a download
contains the merchant's private original data.

The close uses the same original archive writer as an ordinary review export.
Its TAR contains the original six accounting files, `input-manifest.json`,
`review-notes.json`, `START.txt`, and the additional `period-close.json`.
Source-inclusive archives contain `sources/`. The close metadata binds the
original report, source manifest, and frozen review notes by SHA-256. Downloads
check the retained file or archive identity before returning it.

## Compare and reopen

Choose a retained close and another completed period run in **Compare a close
with another capture**. The existing comparison shows added, removed, and changed
events; new and resolved exceptions; and complete before/after option totals.
Both recorded-activity intervals appear above the result. If the boundaries
changed, added or removed rows may follow from that selection change, and the
interface states it explicitly. The original comparison remains available for
any two completed runs, including an all-activity baseline.

Stop and reopen the same workspace directory to continue. Saved period
definitions, the selected version, pinned runs, close revisions, frozen notes,
and original downloads remain available. Ordinary workspace revision conflicts
retain edited form text and use the existing explicit reload/inspect/reapply
flow. Definition edits also carry the current saved definition version.

## Reproduce the source-inclusive close

Extract the TAR into a private directory. `START.txt` contains the exact selected
UTC bounds and the original command structure. Use the same original checkout:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/cli.mjs \
  --outbox /private/extracted-close/sources/outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/extracted-close/sources/proofs \
  --terms /private/extracted-close/sources/terms.json \
  --out /private/new-period-report \
  --period-from 2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z \
  --period-until 2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z
```

Replace the example bounds with the exact `period.from` and `period.until` in
`report.json` or `period-close.json`. When the captured source manifest includes
a recovered collection, add `--recovered-dir /private/extracted-close/sources/recovered`.
Both period flags are required together. They accept UTC timestamps ending in
`Z`, with seconds and optional three-digit milliseconds. The end must follow the
start. Omit both flags to use the original all-activity engine behavior.

The CLI recomputes the original accounting result from the complete retained
sources. Frozen review notes remain in the separate close archive; they never
change the engine's accounting classifications.

## Existing workspace API

The native engine exports `compileAccountingPeriod({from,until})` and accepts an
optional `period` in `runOriginalAccounting` and `compileLedger`. Omit it or pass
`null` for all activity. Period metadata is included in the original report and
its output manifest.

The existing `openAccountingWorkspace` object exposes `workspace.periods`:

| Method | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `save({revision,id?,expectedVersion?,name,from,until,note,select,actor})` | Retain another immutable definition; `select:true` selects it |
| `select({revision,selection,actor})` | Choose `null` for all activity or `{id,version}` for a saved definition |
| `retainClose({revision,runId,name,note,includeSources,actor})` | Use the original writer to retain a close and its review snapshot |
| `detail(closeId)` | Read the retained close and frozen/current review counts |
| `notes(closeId,{offset,limit,status,search})` | Page through frozen exceptions beside current reviews |
| `file(closeId,name)` | Download `period-close.json` or `review-notes.json` after identity verification |

`workspace.begin` additionally accepts `expectedPeriodSelection` and pins the
selected definition to `run.period`. `workspace.compare` returns `scope` with
the original baseline and current period metadata. Existing `workspace.archive`
serves the retained close TAR using its export identity. The full period state
appears under `workspace.view().periods`.

Same-origin HTTP routes are `GET/POST /api/periods`,
`POST /api/periods/selection`, `POST /api/periods/closes`,
`GET /api/periods/closes/:id`, and `GET /api/periods/closes/:id/notes`.
`GET /api/periods/closes/:id/download` returns the original TAR;
`/download/period-close.json` and `/download/review-notes.json` return its
individual retained metadata files. Writes use the original workspace revision
and request header. No additional account, login, or completion gate is introduced.

Retention uses the same private filesystem lease and durable state. A workspace
supports up to 1,000 saved periods, 1,000 definitions per period, and 5,000 closes,
subject to the existing 32 MB workspace state and 256 MB archive limits.

# Client portfolio operations

The client portfolio joins firm standards, staff capacity, separately held client runbooks, close calendars and complete handovers. The coordinator holds the client relationships and prepared commands. Each client’s original accounting workspace continues to hold its procedures, source files, preparation, reviews and operation results.

Open **Client portfolio** in the installed Applications panel, or start the original native host. The browser desk is at `/portfolio.html`. Each **Open client desk** link opens the same Runbooks interface mounted at `/portfolio/clients/CLIENT_ALIAS/runbooks.html`.

## Select the original workspaces

The host reads the existing `accounting.workspaces` configuration. Add a `portfolioClients` map to the coordinator entry; each value names another workspace already in the same configuration. A coordinator can select up to 15 distinct client workspaces. The complete accounting configuration supports up to 16 workspace aliases. Select original merchant accounting workspaces with client Runbooks for the coordinator and each portfolio client. The same host configuration can retain other buyer workspace aliases for their issued-period operations.

This is an illustrative configuration with host paths to replace with the already-initialized original workspaces and their actual source directories:

```json
{
  "accounting": {
    "workspaces": {
      "firm": {
        "label": "Firm operations",
        "directory": "/private/firm",
        "outboxDir": "/private/firm-outbox",
        "proofDir": "/private/firm-proof",
        "termsFile": "/private/firm-terms.json",
        "portfolioClients": {
          "client-a": "accounting-a",
          "client-b": "accounting-b",
          "client-c": "accounting-c"
        }
      },
      "accounting-a": {
        "directory": "/private/client-a",
        "outboxDir": "/private/client-a-outbox",
        "proofDir": "/private/client-a-proof",
        "termsFile": "/private/client-a-terms.json"
      },
      "accounting-b": {
        "directory": "/private/client-b",
        "outboxDir": "/private/client-b-outbox",
        "proofDir": "/private/client-b-proof",
        "termsFile": "/private/client-b-terms.json"
      },
      "accounting-c": {
        "directory": "/private/client-c",
        "outboxDir": "/private/client-c-outbox",
        "proofDir": "/private/client-c-proof",
        "termsFile": "/private/client-c-terms.json"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Reopen an existing host with:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace \
  --portfolio-config /private/operator.json \
  --portfolio-workspace firm \
  --desk client-portfolio
```

The source command is `node workspace/server.mjs` with the same flags. The native command requires the existing Node runtime and original accounting workspace dependencies. Initialize each accounting workspace through its existing native setup before selecting it.

The read-only `portfolio inspect` command reports the complete selected configuration:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio inspect \
  --config /private/operator.json --coordinator firm
```

Applications retains the exact selection digest and all coordinator/client workspace resources. Native launch rechecks `--expected-portfolio-sha256` and each original workspace/source binding after acquiring the original writer. Aliases cannot select the same directory, return to their own coordinator, or point at an undeclared workspace.

An optional `recovery` object on each existing workspace keeps its original `stateRoot`, `backupRoot`, `passEnv` and `startPaused` settings. The portfolio uses those same maintenance admissions. A paused client remains visible as unavailable until its original maintenance is resumed.

## Commission the firm and each client

First save the firm’s name, close standard, reporting format and cadence, and escalation instructions. Declare the actual people by stable ID and name. Capacity uses whole minutes per day, working weekday numbers (Sunday 0 through Saturday 6), holiday dates, and explicit time-off intervals. Saving a change retains another firm edition.

Prepare the client’s procedure edition and files in its original Runbooks desk. Client-specific instructions and resources stay there. A procedure edition can contain up to 100 tasks, with the original uploaded supporting files, complete notes and HTTPS references.

Return to the portfolio and select a configured client alias. The source panel reads the actual client workspace ID and revision, its saved runbooks and editions, existing periods, files and accountant handoffs.

Save a client commission with:

- Client name and exact runbook/edition.
- Named preparer, a different backup, and reviewer.
- Delivery scope, source gaps, reporting and escalation instructions.
- Readiness note and the operator’s current discovery, ready or active status.

Each commission is an immutable retained edition. Revising it compares the previous selected edition. The client identity, original workspace, source observation, procedure digest and firm edition remain available in that history.

These operator labels describe the working assignment and readiness decision. Accounting judgments and the customer relationship remain with the responsible practice.

## Build the staggered close calendar

Create a calendar with a label, start date and end date, then add one row per client period. Each row selects a commissioning edition and names its period, preparer, backup, reviewer, close date, review date, planned preparation minutes, review minutes and optional backup reserve.

A row can select an existing original period. A new period can select original client files or an exact accountant handoff/revision. Capacity can be planned before the next period’s files arrive; the actual files must be selected before preparing its create-period command.

Preview uses the saved firm capacity and existing latest calendar editions. It allocates work backwards from deadlines across working calendar dates. Review has a constrained interval between the close date and review date. Actual preparation and review take precedence over backup reserve. Staff holidays and time off reduce available minutes. The ordering is deterministic; it does not promise a globally optimal schedule.

The preview reports:

- Every allocation by date, person, client row, role and minutes.
- Available, existing-booked and new-planned minutes for each day/person.
- Work that did not fit by its deadline.
- Existing bookings that exceed subsequently changed capacity.
- Original client, commissioning, procedure and existing-period identities.

When saving the preview, provide a handling note for each displayed capacity conflict. These notes preserve the operator’s actual resourcing decision. The saved calendar includes its complete preview, firm edition, original source observations, allocations and exceptions.

Revising a calendar selects its current latest edition as `previousPlanId`. The superseded edition remains retained; its replacement supplies capacity bookings for new previews. Historical periods and actual native operations remain unchanged.

## Apply work in the original clients

The portfolio prepares a complete native request before dispatch. Preparation uses the current coordinator guard and selected original client identity/revision, a retained native UUID, actual action parameters and optional saved calendar row.

| Action | Result in the original client |
| --- | --- |
| Save | A new edition of the commissioned runbook |
| Create | A new period with its exact procedures and original source |
| Assign | Responsibility/date handover with the complete prepared-work snapshot |
| Work | An actual procedure result, note and selected supporting files |
| Submit | The complete original preparation handed to review |
| Review | Original approve/return decision and explicit accepted open items |

A create-period command linked to a calendar uses that row’s frozen runbook, edition, label, people, close date and previous period. Its remaining source selection comes from the actual client. The original Runbooks controller validates all source and phase requirements at execution.

Select **Execute** for the saved command. Its source workspace and original request are compared again, and the child’s operation journal is read first. A committed original UUID returns its native result immediately.

**Read result** is read-only. It returns the committed original result or reports that the UUID is absent. Connection errors preserve their uncertainty; the saved command stays available.

### Correct an uncommitted command

If the original request was rejected before application, prepare a correction using the current command as `replacesCommandId` and the same original `nativeRequestId`. The old and corrected complete request bytes remain retained.

The correction must select the current end of its replacement chain, the same client, action and target, and an uncommitted child UUID. Once the correction is saved, a historical uncommitted request cannot dispatch through the portfolio. Coordinator execution and correction share the original coordinator serialization; there is one current chain end.

If a native result is already committed, recover that original result before preparing subsequent work. A child UUID committed with different request bytes is reported as a conflict, with its historical command still available.

## Complete a backup handover

Open the current client period and read its current assignment. The assignment observation covers the actual preparer, reviewer, due date, phase, prepared-work digest and previous handover.

Prepare an assignment command with `expectedAssignmentSha256`, the actual changed preparer/reviewer/date, and a complete handover and open-items note. A change is available during draft, changes requested or review.

The native period retains:

- The initial responsibility/date assignment.
- Every later assignment, its operator/time, and previous handover identity.
- Full before/after responsibility and due date.
- Complete work status, notes and selected supporting-file references at takeover.
- Before/after assignment digests and the corresponding original period history.

The current native period uses the receiving person and agreed date. Existing work, submissions and reviews remain intact. Subsequent work and reviews continue through the original Runbooks workflow.

Period packets carry handover snapshots and all their selected files, including files later replaced in active work. The original period print includes the full responsibility and work history.

For the running portfolio, the original Runbooks CLI can target the mounted client:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks cycle \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 --client client-a --id PERIOD_UUID
```

Use its `prepare --action assign`, `execute` and `reconcile` commands for the same retained native request path.

## Capture and receive the complete portfolio

Capture selects the actual clients, current workspace observations and complete period IDs. Include a period using each client’s commissioned procedure edition. A capture contains the full firm and commissioning histories, calendar editions, prepared commands, and exact native period packets.

Each native packet retains its complete original bytes. The portfolio compresses those bytes and records their original and compressed digests and sizes. A native packet received earlier keeps its original authoring workspace and original packet identity.

A complete portable portfolio is at most 64 MiB as JSON; its native packets can expand to at most 256 MiB in aggregate, with the original 64 MiB per-period limit. Large selections can be retained as separate complete portfolio captures. Each capture records exactly which clients/periods it carries.

The receiving workflow is explicit and usable on another configured coordinator:

1. Receive the complete portfolio file. The receiver validates its firm metadata, command digests, exact compressed/original bytes, native period structures and selected files.
2. Open its retained received view. It presents the original firm/client metadata and each complete native period. Download the original complete portfolio again from this view at any time; its bytes stay exact after receiving and reopen.
3. Download each native period and receive it through the appropriate local client’s original Runbooks desk.
4. Adopt the portfolio’s selected clients into the receiving coordinator. Select fresh local client IDs, configured local aliases, and current original workspace observations.
5. Adopt the original firm edition, or map preparer/backup/reviewer IDs to the receiving firm’s declared people.
6. Prepare the next local period from the received procedure edition and actual new local source files.

Adoption verifies that every selected native period has actually been received into the selected local client workspace with the same exact packet bytes. Incoming commands and calendars remain in the retained incoming portfolio. New local commissions and fresh local commands have their own original coordinator identity.

The coordinator uses the original private runbook blob writer and operation journal. Files are complete, immutable and hash-bound. The feature adds no parallel outcome database.

## Command-line operation and original recovery

The portfolio CLI uses either the running loopback host or the stopped original configured workspaces:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio status \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8446

merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio status \
  --config /private/operator.json --coordinator firm
```

Use `preview --input ... --out ...` to retain the complete calendar preview. To save any coordinator change, prepare and retain it first:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio prepare \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --action configure --input /private/firm-input.json \
  --out /private/firm-request.json

merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio execute \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --prepared /private/firm-request.json

merchant-accounting-workspace portfolio reconcile \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --prepared /private/firm-request.json
```

Input JSON contains the actual operator and action fields. Prepare adds the current coordinator identity/revision and one request UUID; its native request digest is retained beside the exact input. Outputs must be new or already contain those exact bytes.

The other prepared actions are `commission`, `schedule`, `prepare-command`, `capture`, `receive` and `adopt`. A received file can be supplied with `prepare --action receive --file ...`.

Use `execute-command --id ... --sha ...` to execute a durably prepared original client request and `result --id ...` to read its original outcome. `packet`, `received-packet`, `client-packet`, `calendar` and `print` write complete retained downloads.

The standalone pool owns only clients that it opened. The installed MCP controller borrows from its existing session registry and holds each original maintenance admission until its accepted callback finishes. Explicitly opened client sessions keep their original owners. Shutdown rejects new admissions, drains accepted callbacks and retains a failed close owner for retry.

# Review pricing and retain its accounting source

The **Pricing decisions** area accepts the original saved merchant pricing
report directly. It calls the existing
[`preparePricingReportImport`](../PRICING.md) converter and keeps the exact
report bytes beside its validated accounting terms in this same workspace.

Open the workspace with the existing [server command](README.md#open-on-the-merchant-host).
Existing workspaces reopen normally; their earlier runs and terms selections
remain available. This feature adds no package dependency or alternate payment
or accounting engine.

## Complete the review

1. Download **Report JSON** from a saved version in the original merchant
   pricing workspace. Choose that report under **Pricing decisions**, name the
   review, and supply a short accounting reference when the original quote
   description needs one. The file can contain a session or retained-history
   observation. The browser uploads the exact file bytes without reparsing or
   serializing the report.
2. Choose **Review and retain pricing**. The original converter validates every
   configured alternative and creates the accounting terms. The review retains
   the original report, generated terms, original source hashes, observation
   range, full quote descriptions, operator, and import time. The current terms
   selection remains in effect while the new review is inspected.
3. Inspect the payment alternatives. Atomic amounts and USD values are displayed
   as their original decimal strings. Unknown unit costs remain `null` in the
   source and **Unknown** in the interface. Selecting an option shows its full
   asset, recipient, original quote description, and accounting reference.
   Download either original file whenever needed.
4. Compare against original source terms or any retained accounting choice.
   The comparison uses the original accounting option identities. It shows
   added, removed, changed, and unchanged alternatives, with exact before/after
   quote, cost, amount, and reference values. Complete source and assumption
   context is available below the table.
5. Choose **Use these accounting terms**, then give the reconciliation a name
   and choose **Reconcile with these terms**. The existing selector and run
   queue own those actions. The run checks that the reviewed terms are still
   selected and captures their original pricing report with the merchant's
   selected journal, verification, and recovery inputs.
6. Open the completed reconciliation. Its **Captured pricing decision** section
   identifies the frozen report and terms and downloads either exact file.
   Existing ledger, exception review, run comparison, and archive operations
   remain available. Select source-inclusive export to include the original
   pricing report in the retained handoff.

The original pricing observation describes the pricing decision's source
range. The accounting event scope comes from the run's captured merchant
inputs. Shared monthly costs, demand targets, and challenge costs remain
pricing context according to the original converter's allocation fields.

Selecting a later review or returning to original source terms affects future
runs. Earlier reconciliations retain their own exact report and accounting
terms. Reopening the application restores the saved reviews and source choice.

## Original file custody

Each saved review records its report and terms SHA-256 values. The generated
terms use the existing immutable terms-import store; an identical prior terms
file is reused. The report is retained at
`inputs/REVIEW_ID.pricing-report.json`. Uploading the same report with the same
accounting reference returns its existing review and preserves the current
selection. A different reference creates a separately retained review.

A reconciliation using reviewed pricing adds these files and metadata:

| Retained item | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sources/pricing-report.json` | Exact original uploaded pricing report |
| `sources/terms.json` | Exact accounting terms selected for this run |
| `input-manifest.json` → `pricing` | Review, operator, source range, file hashes, and original summary |

Downloads check the recorded hashes. A changed or missing retained source
returns an error before it can be selected or captured. Source-inclusive TAR
exports copy the verified frozen report and terms. The original accounting CLI
continues to reproduce the report from `sources/terms.json` and the other
captured inputs; it does not recalculate pricing assumptions during accounting.

Pricing report uploads use the converter's 64 MiB limit. Complete generated
terms and provenance must fit the original 200 KB accounting limit and 200
payment alternatives. The workspace retains up to 2,000 pricing reviews under
its existing 32 MB state/history limit. Archives retain the existing 256 MB
limit. A selected JSON file that the original converter cannot map is reported
with that converter's original reason; no alternative is removed to make it fit.

## Existing application integration

`openAccountingWorkspace` attaches `workspace.pricing`, using the same retained
workspace state, serialized writes, revision check, and history. Its methods
are `review`, `detail`, `select`, `compare`, `file`, and `runFile`. The native
accounting `begin` method additionally accepts `expectedTermsSelection` when a
caller wants the queued run bound to a particular reviewed selection.

| Method and route | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/pricing/reviews` | Retain `reportBase64` original file bytes and converted terms with `revision`, `name`, optional `accountingReference`, and `actor` |
| `GET /api/pricing/reviews/ID` | Original converted options, provenance, saved review, and selection state |
| `POST /api/pricing/reviews/ID/selection` | Select that review's original terms using `revision` and `actor` |
| `GET /api/pricing/reviews/ID/compare?baseline=SELECTION` | Exact comparison with `source` or an existing terms-import ID |
| `GET /api/pricing/reviews/ID/download/report` | Exact original uploaded report |
| `GET /api/pricing/reviews/ID/download/terms` | Exact generated accounting terms |
| `GET /api/runs/RUN/pricing/download/report` | Exact report captured by the completed run |
| `GET /api/runs/RUN/pricing/download/terms` | Exact accounting terms captured by the completed run |

Writes use the same original workspace request header and local-origin rules.
The browser preserves the selected file, name, and reference across a saved-state
refresh. If a revision changed, it keeps the submitted draft and offers the
existing reload, inspect, and reapply controls. Reapply uses the currently
edited file, name, and reference. If the selected terms changed before a run,
select the intended reviewed terms again before reconciling.

# QuickBooks Online: merchant handoff, journal and bookkeeping return

The QuickBooks workflow takes a frozen handoff from the existing merchant accounting workspace, prepares a reviewed native journal, and brings the original QuickBooks posting back into the same accountant history. The operator keeps the source events, company and account mapping, valuation, request, response and resulting accountant return together.

Open **QuickBooks** from the private accounting workspace described in [the workspace guide](./README.md). The application uses the original workspace lease, revision control, serialization and accountant engine. The browser and HTTP API below operate on the same records.

The maintained implementation is [the journal engine](../accountant/qbo.mjs), [native company import](../accountant/qbo-company.mjs), [QuickBooks HTTP client](../accountant/qbo-http.mjs) and [workspace integration](./qbo-workspace.mjs).

## Configure the native company connection

Use the maintained [OAuth-connected QuickBooks setup](../../sf30-seller-sdk/oauth-connections/QUICKBOOKS.md) to authorize the actual company through the original connection manager, review its native account chart, and save the company selection. Its `oauth-connection quickbooks serve` command opens this same workspace with the original token provider, including persisted refresh rotation and revocation. The connection panel displays the selected alias, reviewed grant, company, realm, and environment.

A host with an existing access-token source can configure the original private accounting server directly. Its native client reads the following server settings:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| STARFORGE_QBO_ACCESS_TOKEN | Current access token for the company's authorized accounting scope |
| STARFORGE_QBO_REALM_ID | Exact company realm ID, retained as a numeric string |
| STARFORGE_QBO_ENVIRONMENT | sandbox or production; sandbox is the default |
| STARFORGE_QBO_MINOR_VERSION | Optional native minor-version query value; the original value is frozen with a posting request |

Open **Connected QuickBooks company** to read the configured realm, environment and minor version. **Configured** means the server has its target and token source; **Load company and accounts** performs the actual authorized company reads. The browser receives configuration metadata and company documents. Token values stay in the server's existing credential provider.

An embedding host can give QboWorkspace a QboHttpClient through its client option. QboHttpClient accepts an async tokenProvider receiving {realmId,environment,signal} and returning a current access-token string. The maintained OAuth connection owner can supply that provider and perform token refresh and rotation behind this boundary.

The configured target must equal the retained plan's realm and environment. A resumed posting also uses its original minor version, endpoint, request UUID and exact request bytes. Restore the original connection settings when reopening a retained operation under a differently configured server.

## Complete operating journey

### 1. Choose the original handoff

Complete the merchant reconciliation and prepare an accountant handoff in the existing workspace. Choose that retained handoff in QuickBooks. It can carry the original period close and its frozen refund/cancellation companions.

Review the original event, network, transfer classification, atomic amount and adjustment context. Each handoff row identifies one original payment event. Its protected adjustment fields can include gross, refunded, pending refund, remaining, available refund, cancelled and over-refunded atomic amounts. A later live adjustment does not rewrite an already frozen handoff.

A QuickBooks plan selects between one and 500 of these events. Each selected event receives one reviewed positive home-currency amount and one debit/credit pair. Enter the event's accounting treatment with its frozen adjustment context in view. The amount and posting direction are the accountant's inputs. The original token quantity, a merchant quote and a fiat valuation remain separately identifiable.

Rows already reported as BOOKED or EXCLUDED require the original accountant workflow to resolve their status before a new plan can use them. Once a journal is reviewed, its selected events are reserved against another reviewed/booked journal for the same QuickBooks company and environment.

### 2. Establish the company and accounts

Choose the actual QuickBooks environment, explicit company realm ID, company name and home currency. This profile supports USD, CAD, EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD, with two decimal places.

**Load company and accounts** reads the configured company's current CompanyInfo, Preferences and complete account chart. The page fills the explicit company realm, name, home currency and environment, then offers selectable native Account.Id values in each mapping field. Entered amounts and existing mappings remain available for review. The source capture time and source digests appear alongside the loaded company.

The native account reader requests active and inactive records using SELECT * FROM Account WHERE Active IN (true, false) STARTPOSITION 1 MAXRESULTS 1000, continuing its one-based pages until complete. It checks page position and repeated account IDs. Each original native page is retained with the normalized source snapshot.

**Load company setup from saved QuickBooks exports** provides the same company normalization for documents obtained through the company's existing authorized client. Use the following successful native JSON responses:

| Source | Native operation |
| --- | --- |
| Company identity | GET /v3/company/{realmId}/companyinfo/{realmId}?minorversion={version} |
| Preferences | GET /v3/company/{realmId}/preferences?minorversion={version} |
| Chart selection | POST /v3/company/{realmId}/query?minorversion={version}, with the text body SELECT * FROM Account STARTPOSITION 1 MAXRESULTS 1000 |

The company and preference paths are published in Intuit's [CompanyInfo read request][company-read] and [Preferences read request][preferences-read]. The account query and paging structure appear in Intuit's [accounting collection][native-collection] and [SDK query guide][quickstart]. Retain every original page needed to include the intended account mappings. For multiple account pages, import a JSON array of those original QueryResponse objects. The browser's Account JSON input accepts that array.

The import accepts:

- A native CompanyInfo or Preferences wrapper, the direct entity, or a singleton QueryResponse for that entity.
- A native Account read response, one Account QueryResponse, an array of Account query pages, or an array of direct native Account records.
- JSON objects, exact JSON text, or UTF-8 bytes through the programmatic helper. The HTTP endpoint accepts JSON-compatible values and JSON text.

The explicit realm ID remains part of the source binding. CompanyInfo.Id does not replace that explicit realm input. Any realmId supplied by an imported wrapper must agree.

The preview reads CompanyName (or LegalName), CurrencyPrefs.HomeCurrency.value and the actual boolean MultiCurrencyEnabled. It preserves every imported chart row and displays account name, Id, Active, AccountType and CurrencyRef.

An account is selectable when its imported source supplies an active posting account in the supported home currency without a required customer/vendor mapping. Inactive accounts, foreign or missing account currency, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Non-Posting and unrecognized types remain visible with reasons. Account IDs stay exact numeric strings. Repeated IDs and malformed source fields produce a source error, allowing the operator to correct the original selection before preparing the journal.

The normalized snapshot retains:

- Exact sourceDocuments text for text/byte imports of CompanyInfo, Preferences and accounts. JSON object inputs are retained as canonical JSON text.
- Raw-byte SHA256, canonical JSON SHA256 and byte count for each source.
- All normalized accounts, their eligibility reasons and source/page counts.
- A sealed snapshot whose validation reconstructs the company and eligibility from those original documents.

The current import limit is 8 MiB for the combined original company sources. Supplying the snapshot to a plan binds its company and selected account references to that retained import.

For an independently verified manual mapping, enter the exact native Account.Id values and the reviewed company/home currency directly. Include the actual Active, AccountType and CurrencyRef fields whenever available. Choose different debit and credit accounts for each selected event.

### 3. Enter and preview the journal

Give the journal a meaningful name and record the operator. Select the posting date explicitly. Intuit's TxnDate is the date used for the posting; omitting it at the provider would use the server date, so this workflow always carries the chosen date. [JournalEntry properties][journal-properties]

For every selected event, enter:

- Its frozen rowId.
- A positive home-currency amount, with at most two decimal places and a maximum of 999999999.99.
- The actual debit account and credit account.
- A useful description explaining the valuation and account treatment.

A sale may use a merchant clearing asset account and an income account. A reviewed return may need the opposite treatment. Select the direction that matches the accountant's treatment of that event and its retained adjustments.

The preview shows the selected source and generated journal. Every event contributes equal debit and credit amounts, so the journal balances before export. Amounts are validated in integer minor units. The native payload contains JSON numeric Amount values.

A document number can be provided up to 21 characters. Otherwise the engine derives a stable short reference from the retained plan UUID. PrivateNote carries the full plan and handoff identity, and each line description carries the source row identity.

The environment is part of the plan. Production requires the selected original events to be on stellar:pubnet with OFFICIAL_TRANSFER_MATCHED. The sandbox workflow carries the original testnet context through its review and later accountant note.

### 4. Retain and approve the journal

The preview is read-only. Saving its exact previewSha256 creates a DRAFT journal and freezes its request, source, mappings and original accountant revision. A stable request UUID identifies that operation; repeating it with the same content reopens the original result.

Open the retained draft and review its actual company, date, source, account directions, home amounts and totals. The review operation records the reviewer, note and retained plan digest. It changes the journal to REVIEWED and reserves the selected events for that company/environment.

The reviewed plan enables **Review native posting** and its exact journal-entry.json download. That file is the native JournalEntry create body used by the connected-company workflow. Also retain plan.json and review.html with the accountant's working papers.

The packet includes:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| plan.json | Frozen journal, selected events, mappings, optional company snapshot and integrity |
| journal-entry.json | Exact native JournalEntry create body |
| handoff.json | Original frozen accountant handoff |
| accountant.csv | Original current accountant template at plan preparation |
| accountant-return.json | The existing parent accountant return, when one was present |
| review.html | Standalone human review of the selected source and journal |

### 5. Post to the connected QuickBooks company

In **Journal review**, select **Review native posting**. The preview shows the actual company realm and environment, document number, journal date, operator, debits and credits, original accountant parent, native request UUID and exact request/plan digests. Review the retained lines, confirm that displayed target and choose **Post reviewed journal**.

The preview is read-only. Posting first saves intent.json and the exact request.json under the original plan, then continues one durable native operation. Its UUID is the requestid query parameter on:

POST /v3/company/{realmId}/journalentry?requestid={originalOperationId}&minorversion={originalVersion}

The minorversion parameter is present when it was configured. The production host is https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com and the sandbox host is https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com. The native payload follows Intuit's [JournalEntry create request][journal-create]. The persisted request identity is also visible in the file and attempt history; Intuit's [request field definitions][request-fields] and [retry guidance][batch-retry] describe the provider's request-identity convention.

Before a create or a resumed uncertain write, the workspace pages through the exact DocNumber query, selects the retained private plan identity and reads a matching native JournalEntry.Id. The original response matcher checks the full journal. When an original journal is found, it receives that posting into the same plan. If the lookup finds no matching original journal, the operation continues with its same requestid, original URL and exact reviewed body.

The successful native response passes through the existing accountant response preview, saved response intent and original accountant apply/link. The page opens **Accountant return** when that linked result is BOOKED. The native JournalEntry.Id, SyncToken and original saved return remain attached to the same plan.

Each query, read and create attempt retains its complete response bytes and receipt. **Native request and response history** shows the actual HTTP status, received time, request realm/environment, Intuit trace ID when provided, response size and digests, with exact file downloads. The list is paginated for repeated recovery.

#### Continue an interrupted native operation

Refresh saved state to reopen the retained operation. **Resume original posting** keeps its UUID and reviewed request. A RECEIVED operation uses its saved response to finish the original accountant return locally. Workspace startup also finishes retained native responses and pending accountant returns where their original source still matches.

After a timeout, transport interruption or incomplete response, the operation records the uncertain outcome and resumes the original query/read reconciliation before any repeat of the same create. When the provider requests a pause, the retained retry time remains visible. Refresh at or after that time, then resume the original operation. The client observes the later of its minimum 60-second pause and the provider's Retry-After value, consistent with Intuit's [throttle guidance][native-throttles].

A response showing multiple original journals or changed journal economics appears as a reconciliation state with the actual provider source retained. Inspect that source and the original accountant history, resolve the reported issue, then use **Recheck original journal**. A pending manual response already owns its original accountant return; continue that saved response before starting native posting.

The page keeps the actual native status visible throughout this process. A successful local request that returns RETRYABLE, UNCERTAIN, RECEIVED, FAULT or CONFLICT displays that saved state and its next operation. BOOKED appears when the original accountant return has been saved and linked.

#### Use an existing authorized QuickBooks client

The reviewed request download and original response import remain available for work performed through the company's existing client. Submit the same retained journal-entry.json to the selected company/environment, preserve that client's original request identity and complete native result, then follow step 6 below. A native operation already retained in this workspace continues through its own posting and response history.

The simple journal profile uses explicit home-currency values and reviewed no-tax journal treatment. Currency conversion, tax-code classification, classes, departments, counterparty subledgers and additional fee/reclassification lines belong in the accountant's full journal treatment when required. The original handoff and return remain available for that work.

### 6. Preview the original response and save the return

Native posting runs this step with the retained provider bytes. For a response received through the company's existing authorized client, open the same reviewed plan, select the original response JSON, retain its company realm and preview it. The application reads either a native JournalEntry or a native Fault.

For a successful return, it checks the posting date, document number, retained private plan reference, currency, amounts, account IDs, posting sides and source descriptions. Provider-generated line IDs and display names can vary. Line order is compared by its full semantic composition.

The response must retain the native JournalEntry.Id and SyncToken as strings. SyncToken "0" is a valid initial version. The entity/version pair remains in the resulting accountant note and external reference; later provider updates use their own current version. Intuit describes these entity/version fields in its [JournalEntry model][journal-properties].

Ordinary no-tax/default fields are accepted when they preserve the reviewed treatment. This includes NotApplicable tax calculation and empty/zero tax details, plus false adjustment flags. Deleted/voided entries, conversion, substantive tax classification and changed journal economics require reconciliation against the reviewed source.

A successful preview builds the original accountant CSV return and runs it through the existing accountant preview. Saving it first retains the exact provider response and immutable return intent. The original accountant engine then applies that stable return and the workspace links the same result.

The selected rows receive:

| Accountant field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| externalStatus | BOOKED |
| externalBookRef | QBO:{realmId}:{JournalEntry.Id} |
| externalAccountCode | {debitAccountId}>{creditAccountId} |
| externalNote | Original note, with environment, realm, JournalEntry.Id, SyncToken, reviewed amount and currency appended when it fits |

Protected source columns and all unselected assignments stay with the original accountant engine. The journal becomes BOOKED when that original return has been saved and linked.

A Fault response is retained with its original error codes, messages and details. The journal remains available for the operator to resolve the provider issue and import the correct original posting result.

### 7. Resume, export and reopen

A matched response moves through PENDING while its original accountant return is being applied and linked. Reopening runs recovery for pending responses. The explicit resume operation continues that same response/return ID. Repeating a completed save returns the existing saved response.

If a pending operation reports a stale accountant parent or a source conflict, open its original accountant history and inspect the recorded return/revision before continuing. Its raw provider response, prepared return and stable identity are retained. Keep the existing posting and reconcile that record through the original accountant workflow.

A saved response carries these files:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| response.json | Exact imported provider response bytes |
| result.json | Bound response inspection and proposed original accountant return |
| returned.csv | Exact accountant return content for a matched response |
| return-request.json | Stable original accountant import identity and preview digest |

The workspace retains the final saved accountant return ID and digest in the response record. Download the plan and response files from the same plan detail. The original accounting workspace export and backup should include its qbo directory and workspace state.

A DRAFT or REVIEWED plan can be cancelled after the operator confirms that it has no saved QuickBooks posting and its request will remain unused. Cancellation records the operator's reason and releases the event reservation. For a native operation, cancellation also requires no active run, no observed original journal and no retained matched response; it must be undispatched or have one definite failed first write. An earlier uncertain write remains attached to its original recovery. A matched pending/saved response continues through its existing accountant record.

## State and recovery reference

| Record | State | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Journal | DRAFT | Exact plan and source packet retained; review remains |
| Journal | REVIEWED | Review recorded; selected company/events reserved; native request available |
| Journal | BOOKED | Original accountant return saved and linked |
| Journal | CANCELLED | Operator confirmed the plan unused and recorded cancellation |
| Response | FAULT | Exact native provider error retained |
| Response | PENDING | Matched response and original return intent retained; application/link pending |
| Response | SAVED | Original accountant return linked to this response |
| Native posting | PREPARED | Exact intent and native request packet saved |
| Native posting | RUNNING | Original query, read or posting is in progress |
| Native posting | RETRYABLE | Original operation can resume after its reported issue or retry time |
| Native posting | UNCERTAIN | An earlier write is being reconciled with its original provider identity |
| Native posting | RECEIVED | Exact native response retained; original local accountant completion remains |
| Native posting | BOOKED | Original saved response and accountant return linked |
| Native posting | FAULT | A definite native fault is retained with its attempt files |
| Native posting | CONFLICT | Original journal/source requires the recorded reconciliation |

The workspace revision protects writes against concurrent changes. expectedParentId protects the selected accountant revision. Preview digests bind the actual source and values that were reviewed. Stable IDs support interruption recovery.

All paths are mounted on the existing private accounting server and use that server's established authentication. GET, company fetch and preview operations inspect source. Record-changing POST operations use the original workspace revision and retained identities; native posting additionally performs the reviewed QuickBooks request.

## Common corrections

| Result | Concrete correction |
| --- | --- |
| QBO_CONNECTION_REQUIRED | Configure the current authorized server token or token provider and original realm, then refresh the connection |
| QBO_CONNECTION_CHANGED / QBO_NATIVE_CONNECTION_CHANGED | Restore the retained plan's company, environment and original minor version |
| QBO_NATIVE_POST_EXISTS | Reopen record.nativePost and resume that original operation |
| QBO_NATIVE_THROTTLED | Refresh at or after the retained retryAt, then resume the same operation |
| QBO_NATIVE_MULTIPLE_JOURNALS | Inspect the retained exact query/read responses and reconcile the original native journals |
| QBO_COMPANY_SOURCE_FAULT | Open the provider error and obtain the successful CompanyInfo, Preferences or Account response |
| QBO_COMPANY_ACCOUNT_ACTIVE / REFERENCE / DUPLICATE | Correct the original account source; preserve string IDs and boolean Active, with one record per account |
| Account is visible but unselectable | Read its reason and choose a suitable actual account, or complete the required currency/counterparty treatment in the original accounting workflow |
| QBO_STALE_ACCOUNTANT / QBO_ACCOUNTANT_CHANGED | Reload the original handoff/current accountant revision and review the affected assignments |
| QBO_PREVIEW_CHANGED | Preview the current complete request and use that returned digest |
| QBO_EVENT_RESERVED | Open the original reviewed/booked plan; cancel an unused reviewed plan when appropriate |
| QBO_COMPANY_MISMATCH / QBO_RESPONSE_IDENTITY | Retrieve the original response for the selected company, plan and posting |
| QBO_RESPONSE_MISMATCH | Compare the retained native request with the provider's complete journal before importing |
| QBO_JOURNAL_ALREADY_IMPORTED | Reopen the original retained response/return |
| Pending response with lastError | Inspect the retained accountant history and resume the same return after resolving its specific conflict |

## Primary QuickBooks contract references

The generated journal uses the native JournalEntry line structure and balance rule from Intuit's [journal model][journal-model] and [JournalEntry request][journal-create]. Currency preferences are defined in [CurrencyPrefs][currency-prefs]. Native chart fields come from Intuit's [Account model][account-model]; the [AccountType enum][account-types] gives the exact spellings used by the import.

Regional tax, class, department and counterparty fields are separate native concepts in [JournalEntryLineDetail][journal-line]. The home-currency profile and explicit account selection here are the implemented product contract. The original company settings and accountant's treatment determine the actual posting.
