# Merchant settlement workspace

This local operator application keeps a merchant's reconciliations, imported original verification results, recovered original purchase outcomes, exception reviews, comparisons, and downloads together across restarts. It runs the existing `merchant-settlement-accounting/reconcile.mjs` engine and the existing CLI's report writer directly. The original SF98 journal reader, SF86 proof classifications, explicit recovered-settlement reader, multi-option identity, and exact monetary arithmetic remain the accounting source.

## Buyer-only accounting startup

An operator with an issued SF36 buyer period can initialize this same workspace with `--buyer-source ABS --buyer-operator NAME`. The original file, source context and first-handoff identity are retained inside the native Store. The browser opens its accountant review, Xero and recovery workflow. [Buyer startup, CLI, source binding and complete receiving](BUYER_ACCOUNTING.md#start-with-an-issued-buyer-period) documents the complete path; merchant outbox/proof/terms paths are not part of a buyer source configuration.

## Xero journals

Open **Xero journals** from the Accountant handoff panel to retain an organization and chart of accounts, explicitly value original payments and verified refunds, create balanced native drafts, reconcile returned journals, and apply the original accountant return. The [complete Xero workflow](XERO.md) includes the operator interface, existing distribution subcommand, retained source downloads and original-workspace recovery.

## Open on the merchant host

Use Node 22 or later on Linux, with `flock` and `tar` available. The source checkout supplies all JavaScript modules; this workspace adds no package dependencies. The existing merchant outbox and SF86 result directory must be private directories with mode 0700. Select the original merchant accounting terms JSON described in [the accounting guide](../README.md).

From the repository root:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --outbox /private/merchant/sf98-outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/sf86-results \
  --terms /private/merchant/accounting-terms.json
```

The workspace directory must be separate from its original input directories. It is created at mode 0700, with new retained files at mode 0600. Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:8446` address. Set `--port 8450` to choose a different local port.

The browser has no account creation, login, or token entry. The server binds to loopback and validates its local Host header; writes use same-origin JSON requests with the workspace header. Run it in the merchant's private operating-system session. It is a local application, with filesystem access under the account that starts it.

Reopen the same retained work later:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace
```

Original source paths are retained in the workspace. Import another terms file through the interface when the merchant's approved terms change. Use a separate workspace directory for a different source outbox.

An existing original recovered-settlement collection can also be selected at startup with `--recovered-dir /private/merchant/recovered-settlements`, or connected through the source screen after opening the workspace. The collection must be separate from the workspace, outbox, and verification directories.

## Complete a merchant review

Enter the operator or reviewer name in the sidebar. It is recorded with imports, reconciliation runs, review decisions, and exported handoffs.

1. **Review sources and import original files.** The source screen shows the configured native paths. Import an original `stellar-forge.sf86.rpc-reconciliation.v1` JSON result or `stellar-forge.merchant-accounting-terms.v1` merchant terms. Imported files retain their exact bytes, SHA256, filename, and original verdict. Choose which imports will enter the next reconciliation. The configured SF86 directory is always included; imported terms can be selected or switched back to the original source file.
2. **Capture a reconciliation.** Give it a useful name and select *Reconcile current sources*. The application retains its input bytes and runs the original engine in the background. The run list shows queued, running, completed, failed, or interrupted work. Existing completed results remain available while a new run executes.
3. **Inspect every record.** The event ledger, payment options, exception queue, and verification files are paginated and searchable. Open a row to inspect its full native fields. Atomic amounts and merchant USD values remain exact decimal strings. Configured options with no events remain visible, and each actual option keeps its own atomic totals.
4. **Investigate exceptions.** Add a named review note, assignee, and status of open, investigating, or reviewed. Notes follow the same event and the same exception reason into later reconciliations. A new reason starts its own review. Review status stays separate from the original transfer classification.
5. **Compare retained runs.** Choose the current and baseline run. The comparison reports added, removed, and changed events, resolved and new exceptions, and complete before/after payment-option totals. Event changes include original delivery and verification fields as well as merchant terms, quote, and cost fields. The application displays original exact values side by side.
6. **Create the handoff.** Export a new review download from a completed run. The archive includes the original report files and a snapshot of the named exception notes. Existing exports remain unchanged. Select *Include private captured source files* when the recipient also needs the retained journal, terms, and verification files.

Refresh preserves unsaved form text. If another operator saved the same review or changed the workspace revision, the interface retains the draft and offers an explicit reload and reapply action. Completed background work can also advance the workspace revision. A stale write is never silently substituted for the newer saved state.

## Exchange an accountant handoff

The **Accountant handoffs** area prepares a labeled CSV and offline packet from a completed original reconciliation or recorded-activity close. Preview a returned bookkeeping file, inspect exact source matches and conflicts, and save its references with inherited partial progress and immutable revision history. The original source amounts, networks, transfer classifications, and merchant quotes remain visible beside the accountant's returned fields. Follow the [accountant workflow guide](../accountant/README.md) for the complete exchange and integration routes.

## Exchange merchant attribution with Bitwave

Open **Bitwave Data Fusion** from Accountant handoffs, or `/bitwave.html` on the
same merchant accounting workspace. Select a saved handoff and its original or
returned accountant version to freeze a named Data Fusion plan. Each source
amount, asset identity, network and fingerprint remains an exact string beside
the four editable bookkeeping fields.

The application prepares the native schema and row batches, creates or selects
the customer's exact organization/table, retains each native request and
response, and captures every returned page. Configure `BITWAVE_ACCESS_TOKEN` in
the merchant host environment for native delivery. Original JSON page imports
also support an existing customer-operated API workflow. Review a completed
capture before repairing missing rows after an interrupted upload.

Returned bookkeeping fields are compared with both the frozen export and the
current accountant version. Concurrent edits appear together for review;
matched changes enter the original immutable return history. The complete
download contains original merchant source, native requests/pages, comparisons
and every accepted accountant return with its full CSV and HTML review. A
retained save request reconnects the same return after an interrupted operation.

Follow [the complete Bitwave workflow](BITWAVE_WORKFLOW.md) for source selection,
native setup, interruption recovery, source correction and accountant handover.
The maintained package includes this whole application through its existing
`merchant-accounting-workspace` command; `./merchant/bitwave` and
`./merchant/bitwave-http` expose the pure mapping and native HTTP client.

## Collect verification in the same workspace

The **RPC collections** area retains original reserved payment records and their read-only verification work alongside the accounting inputs. Use the merchant runtime's existing `@stellar/stellar-sdk` event decoder for network collection.

1. **Review original payment files.** Select SF81 record JSON or SF82 checkout evidence and enter the independently known payer account. Each upload retains its exact source bytes and validates the original reservation, receipt and payment terms. The default RPC endpoint comes from the shared network catalog. An optional endpoint must match that network's catalog or the original loopback replay format.
2. **Prepare the selected collection.** Choose the reviewed sources and name the collection. Preparation snapshots their exact bytes through the original SF86 batch API. Sources and prepared collections remain available after reopening.
3. **Collect and resume.** Start read-only verification and follow the per-record result and attempt count. Stop an active operation when necessary; completed original results stay retained. Resume collects only unattempted records. Select unsuccessful records to retry explicitly; earlier attempts remain unchanged. Two collection operations may progress at once, with further operations queued in the same workspace.
4. **Use current results in accounting.** Publish the selected collection's current original results. The workspace retains an immutable original export and imports its files through the existing accounting import API. Repeating publication reuses identical imported files and preserves an operator's inclusion choices. Interrupted publication can be resumed by publishing the current results again.
5. **Capture and export the reconciliation.** Capture current selected sources using the existing accounting workflow. The run includes selected collection results, native journal events and any connected recovered-payment collection. Review the original classifications, then download the original report or source-inclusive review archive. Each collection record also offers its current original verification JSON.

Uploaded sources support 4 MB per file and 2,000 retained sources. Collection input paths and progress live under the existing private workspace; the original batch engine owns its source snapshots and immutable attempts. On process restart, unfinished operations are marked interrupted and their completed attempt files are read through the original inspector. Current progress uses the retained batch results, with an in-memory view while an operation is active. Workspace revisions advance for meaningful operator and operation transitions rather than every network response.

For a host with an explicitly configured HTTPS CONNECT proxy, start or reopen with `--rpc-proxy-env HTTPS_PROXY`. The existing public HTTPS transport reads that environment variable on the host. Enter the variable name at startup; the browser handles the retained records and public account identities.

## Use a saved pricing decision

Open **Pricing decisions** to upload an original saved SF97 pricing report.
The existing converter retains every payment alternative, exact amount, unknown
cost, original quote description, and observation source. Review and compare
its accounting terms, select the approved choice, and capture a reconciliation
that retains both original files. Earlier runs keep their own pricing sources.
The [complete pricing workflow](PRICING.md) covers original downloads, selected
terms, source-inclusive export, revision conflicts, and reopening.

## Recorded-activity periods and closes

Open **Periods & closes** to save an exact UTC interval and retain its definition
versions. The current selection appears above every operator area. Each queued
run pins that definition while capturing the complete original source. The
engine verifies every captured native and recovered record before selecting
rows for the existing summaries. Native rows use capture time; recovered rows
use import time.

Retain a named close from a completed period run, including its open exceptions
and frozen review notes. Compare later captures or definitions through the
original comparison, inspect frozen notes beside current reviews, download the
original source-inclusive archive, and reopen the same retained workspace.
The [complete period workflow](PERIODS.md) covers source scope, immutable close
revisions, exact CLI bounds, and the existing workspace API.

## Recover an already completed purchase

The original recovery module handles a completed SF31 purchase whose native request, outcome, and optional delivered response were retained outside SF98. Its input and source-binding format is documented in [the original recovery guide](../RECOVERY.md). It keeps that origin explicit and uses the original network-specific SF86 verifier.

1. **Connect the recovered collection.** Choose its absolute private directory on the machine running the workspace. A new collection is created at mode 0700. An existing collection is read through the original recovery reader, which checks the retained entries and their source files. The screen records the latest inventory time. Refresh the collection after another original process adds entries; ordinary UI polling reads the saved inventory instead of rereading large response files.
2. **Review the original request.** Select a `stellar-forge.merchant-recovery-request.v1` JSON configuration. Its outcome, request, terms, and optional response paths refer to files on the workspace host. The workspace retains the exact configuration bytes and invokes `reviewRecoveredSettlement`. Review the original route, method, network, selected payment terms, transaction, payer, source hashes, and response identity before importing. This review reads the selected files locally.
3. **Import the reviewed result.** The workspace starts the original `importRecoveredSettlement` operation in the background. The original importer verifies the transfer using the configured official RPC endpoint and retains its canonical entry, proof, and source files. A previously imported identical transaction returns `ALREADY_IMPORTED` and reuses its retained proof. The importer never sends another paid request. Progress and any original error remain in the workspace after navigation or restart.
4. **Continue or cancel an attempt.** An in-progress read-only import can be cancelled. If the original durable import already completed, its completed result is retained. Retry the same reviewed request after cancellation, interruption, or an operational error; native import identity prevents a duplicate entry. If an original file changed after review, review the request again to inspect its current binding.
5. **Reconcile the selected sources.** The next run captures the connected collection alongside its selected native outbox, terms, and verification files. The original engine reports native successes and recovered settlements separately. Recovered rows retain `RECOVERED_ORIGINAL_SF31_OUTCOME`, their import-time basis, original entry/proof identities, and saved-response status. The engine's existing duplicate-transaction handling spans both origins.
6. **Inspect and download the result.** The recovered-source view shows the entries frozen with the selected run. A saved response can be downloaded from the current collection or from a retained run. Downloads return the exact original saved bytes through the original reader. Disconnecting the collection affects future reconciliations; earlier runs, their captured files, and completed import history remain available.

The selected merchant accounting terms still determine the current run's route and payment-option mapping. A retained recovery has its own original terms file for source binding; it does not silently replace the workspace's selected accounting terms.

Recovered response downloads and source-inclusive review archives can contain the original delivered merchant data, request metadata, and public account addresses. Use the source-inclusive option when the recipient needs those originals. The default review archive contains accounting identities and named review notes without those private source bytes.

## Original result classifications

The interface uses the existing engine's result fields without interpreting a review note as payment evidence:

| Original field or classification | Operator meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `OFFICIAL_TRANSFER_MATCHED` | Existing SF86 official proof matched the original recorded network and payment option |
| `NATIVE_SUCCESS_UNVERIFIED` | Native settlement success still needs independent matching verification |
| `PUBLIC_NETWORK_PENDING` | The original engine reports a public-network event awaiting compatible verification |
| `LOCAL_RPC_REPLAY_MATCHED` | Original local replay result remains excluded from official transfer counts |
| `WEBHOOK_ACCEPTED_NOT_FULFILLED` | Native delivery received a webhook acknowledgment |
| `DELIVERY_EXHAUSTED` | The original delivery worker exhausted its attempts |
| `RECOVERED_ORIGINAL_SF31_OUTCOME` | Original retained SF31 outcome imported through the canonical recovery source |
| `RECOVERED_RESPONSE_SAVED` | The original delivered response bytes are retained with this recovered entry |
| `RECOVERED_RESPONSE_NOT_RETAINED` | This recovered entry has no original saved response file |
| Review status `reviewed` | An operator recorded a review note; the original classification remains visible |

Original duplicate-transaction, conflicting-proof, ambiguous legacy-recipient, and unknown-terms behavior is preserved. An identical imported file already present in the original proof directory is captured once; the import remains listed as a duplicate of that original file. Conflicting original files remain available to the original engine's conflict detection.

The original engine's `verifiedQuotedValueUsd` is the merchant's own quote for independently matched units. The UI preserves its label and exact decimal string. Payment-option atomic totals are never combined across different options or networks.

## What a run retains

The workspace captures a completed prefix of `deliveries.ndjson` before a completed prefix of `events.ndjson`. Native delivery records refer to events already appended by the original producer. This order includes the required event for each captured delivery status while allowing the merchant to keep appending new events. Later appends enter the next reconciliation. The two files are a retained capture, rather than a simultaneous global journal instant.

Missing or empty native journals represent an empty outbox. An incomplete trailing append fails the capture with a clear message; start a new reconciliation after the original producer finishes its append. A source file that is truncated during capture also fails the run. Imported choices and source-directory selections are retained with the queued run, and selected source bytes are frozen before the original accounting engine begins.

Each completed run contains:

| Retained path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `sources/outbox/` | Captured native event and delivery journal bytes |
| `sources/proofs/` | Included original verification result bytes |
| `sources/terms.json` | The selected original merchant accounting terms |
| `sources/pricing-report.json` | Original uploaded pricing report for the selected reviewed terms, when present |
| `sources/recovered/` | Connected original recovery entries, proofs, source files, and any saved response bytes |
| `input-manifest.json` | Captured file paths, SHA256 values, original filenames, and verification descriptions |
| `report/` | The original six create-only accounting outputs |

The workspace records original report and manifest hashes. Downloads and exports check the retained original file hashes before returning them. The original CLI writes the same six report files: `report.json`, `ledger.csv`, `options.csv`, `exceptions.csv`, `review.html`, and `manifest.json`. Its ledger and option CSVs include additive original-source, recovery-identity, and recovered-amount columns; existing columns remain in place. The original HTML displays native and recovered counts separately.

## Export and reopen

A review download is a standard TAR archive with the six original accounting files, `review-notes.json`, `input-manifest.json`, and `START.txt`. Source-inclusive exports also contain `sources/`. The review notes are captured at export time; later note edits do not alter earlier archives. The browser also provides individual downloads for all six original accounting files.

To reproduce a source-inclusive export using the same original checkout, extract it into a private directory and run:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/cli.mjs \
  --outbox /private/extracted-review/sources/outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/extracted-review/sources/proofs \
  --terms /private/extracted-review/sources/terms.json \
  --out /private/reproduced-accounting-report
```

The output path must be new. Exported operator notes remain in their separate file; the original engine computes the accounting result from the retained native sources.

If the archive contains `sources/recovered/`, add:

```sh
  --recovered-dir /private/extracted-review/sources/recovered
```

The explicit directory preserves the captured recovery source during reproduction, including an intentionally empty connected collection.

For a period-selected run, also use the exact `--period-from` and `--period-until`
values printed in the archive's `START.txt`. The captured source remains complete;
the original engine selects the interval after full-source verification. A period
close additionally includes `period-close.json` and its immutable review snapshot.

Workspace state is atomically replaced and fsynced under the existing Linux filesystem lease. One server owns a given workspace directory. Stopping and reopening preserves completed runs, imported files, recovery reviews and attempts, review history, and exports. If the process stops during a run, reopening marks that run interrupted and retains any captured files; the operator can capture current sources as a new run. An interrupted recovery import can be retried from its saved review, including a native entry completed immediately before the interruption. Earlier completed results and downloads stay available. The operating backup below also retains the external sources required to continue this workspace.

Limits follow the original accounting engine: up to 20,000 native events, 16 MB per source journal, 200 payment options, and 2,000 combined verification files. An imported SF86 file is limited to 80 KB and terms to 200 KB. The original recovered collection supports up to 2,000 entries, 200 KB per source JSON, and 64 MiB per saved response. The workspace retains up to 2,000 recovery reviews and 5,000 import attempts. Input manifests are limited to 16 MB, individual review archives to 256 MB, and workspace history to 32 MB with up to 5,000 runs. Archive a completed workspace and start another when those retention limits are reached.

## Back up and restore the complete accounting operation

The original `merchant-accounting-workspace` command has `backup`,
`inspect-backup`, `verify-backup`, `restore` and `recovery-status` subcommands.
They invoke the existing SF101 encrypted recovery engine. The original
workspace lease owns each backup and restore; the normal browser and merchant
MCP continue to open the same directory after completion.

### Operate backup and recovery in the browser

The **Backup & recovery** area uses the same server, workspace, original SF101
encryption and complete operating-source selection. Configure it on the
existing launch command:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --recovery-state-root /private/merchant \
  --recovery-backup-root /private/backups/accounting \
  --recovery-pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE
```

The state root must contain the selected workspace and its original inputs.
The backup root is a separate private directory outside those sources. Keep
the recovery passphrase in the named host environment variable. The browser
shows its availability and never accepts or receives the value. Its saved
backup choices are children of this configured backup root.

1. Enter the operator name and select **Pause accounting workspace**. The same
   server remains open while accepted requests drain and the original
   accounting, collection and Bitwave controllers close. The recovery area
   stays available; accounting resumes through the original controllers.
2. Stop other processes writing the merchant outbox and selected source
   directories. Select **Review operating sources**, inspect the exact roots,
   file count and retained workspace revision, then name the backup and
   confirm that those external writers are stopped.
3. Select **Create encrypted backup**. Source identity is checked again during
   capture. Operation progress and the retained outcome appear in the history.
   The completed backup remains in its displayed private host location; keep
   its whole directory and separately retained recovery key together in the
   merchant's established recovery process.
4. Select a retained backup and **Verify encrypted files** to authenticate its
   original manifest and contents. Verification is attached to that exact
   retained manifest. Review the selected backup and original target before
   **Restore selected backup**. Recovery creates missing files and reuses
   matching files. Existing changed or additional files remain preserved and
   are reported by the original engine.
5. Use **Reopen accounting workspace** after successful recovery or a completed
   backup. The same browser reloads original reconciliations, collections,
   periods, accountant handoffs and reviews from the restored workspace.

Every accepted command has a retained identity, named operator, progress and
result. Disconnecting the browser leaves that operation running. If a response
is lost, **Read saved command** finds the original operation and **Retry this
same command** reuses its exact request identity and input. A changed command
cannot reuse that identity. The original server owns cancellation and
recovery; the browser does not launch a second worker.

After a host interruption or when the original workspace is absent, add
`--recovery-start-paused` to the same configured command. The recovery desk
opens independently of the accounting files. Select the original backup,
complete recovery at the same private paths, then reopen accounting. An
interrupted restore displays **Continue recovery from this backup**; its
original recovery marker and matching published files are reused. Capture
and verification can be stopped through their owned operation controls;
pausing and reopening finish their lifecycle transition before another
operation begins.

The latest 50 operations are retained in the desk's working view. The host
keeps the complete operation history, and `/api/maintenance/jobs/:id` reads
an earlier operation by its saved identity. Existing cold CLI backup and
recovery commands below remain available.

### Capture the original operating sources

Stop this workspace and the processes that write its native outbox, verification
directory and recovered-settlement collection. Supply `--quiesced` after they
have stopped. A competing workspace process is rejected by the original Linux
lease. A source file, directory or filename changing during capture makes the
backup fail and removes only that newly created backup directory.

Use a private `--state-root` that contains the workspace and all its configured
inputs. The command selects these exact sources; it does not copy the whole
state root:

| Retained source | What reopening preserves |
| --- | --- |
| Complete original accounting workspace | Reconciliations and their captured inputs, collection sources/plans/results/attempts, pricing imports, period definitions/closes, accountant handoffs/returns, review history and downloads |
| Configured outbox, proof directory and original terms | Native inputs for the next reconciliation |
| Connected original recovered-settlement collection | Existing transfer proofs, receipt identities and exact delivered response bytes |
| Files explicitly referenced by saved original recovery requests | The outcome, approved request, terms and optional response required to reuse a retained recovery review |

Other files elsewhere under the state root are not scanned. Keep signer keys
and host credentials outside these accounting source paths and preserve their
established private operational backup separately. A
source configured outside the selected state root is reported before capture;
select the correct common private ancestor instead of rewriting its saved path.

Set a private passphrase of at least 16 bytes in the named host environment
variable. Obtain it through the host's existing secret manager or an interactive
hidden prompt. Keep it recoverable separately from the encrypted backup. The
command accepts the variable name and never prints the value.

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace backup \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --state-root /private/merchant \
  --out /private/backups/accounting-2026-10-11 \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE \
  --quiesced
```

The output parent must already be private, and the output directory must be
new and outside all captured sources. In a source checkout, replace
`npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace` with
`node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs`.
The existing installed package includes the same source and recovery engine.

Successful capture returns `ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_CREATED`, the encrypted manifest
SHA256, original workspace revision/hash and captured counts. `backup.json`
marks completion; `encrypted/` is the original SF101 bundle. Its authenticated
encryption contains the source mapping and original files. The outer receipt
contains counts and a manifest digest. Preserve the whole completed directory.

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace inspect-backup \
  --bundle /private/backups/accounting-2026-10-11

npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace verify-backup \
  --bundle /private/backups/accounting-2026-10-11 \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE
```

Inspection reports the completion receipt and manifest identity. Verification
authenticates the original manifest and every encrypted file with the private
passphrase, returning `ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_VERIFIED`. Supply
`--expected-sha256` with the saved manifest digest to pin a specific backup in
either command or in restore.

### Restore at the original private paths

Prepare the same absolute state-root path on the merchant host, owned by the
operating account with mode 0700. Stop the original input writers and workspace.
Preserve any surviving original directories until recovery is complete.

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace restore \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --state-root /private/merchant \
  --bundle /private/backups/accounting-2026-10-11 \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE \
  --quiesced
```

Restore authenticates the full original SF101 bundle into private staging before
publishing any operating file. It checks the encrypted mapping against the
original workspace state and its saved recovery requests. The command creates
missing files and reuses existing files only when their exact bytes match.
A changed or additional existing operating file produces
`ACCOUNTING_RECOVERY_DESTINATION_CHANGED`; that data is preserved. Choose the
appropriate retained backup or preserve the surviving state separately before
recovering into its original empty path.

Original absolute paths remain unchanged because collection plans and completed
batch operations retain those paths in their identities. This command does not
rebase completed plans, generate a payment, replay a purchase or call an RPC.

During publication, `recovery-restore.json` records the selected manifest under
the original workspace lease. A signal or crash leaves that record and any
fully published files for the next attempt. Repeating the **same restore
command** authenticates the same backup, clears only its own unfinished file
staging, reuses completed matching files and finishes the remaining work.
The workspace state file is published last. Normal browser/MCP opening reports
`WORKSPACE_RESTORE_INCOMPLETE` until this operation completes.

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-accounting-workspace recovery-status \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace
```

Success returns `ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE_RESTORED` with original revision/hash,
restored/reused file counts and the manifest identity. Reopen the original
workspace command or existing merchant MCP configuration. Original report,
period-close, accountant packet and recovered-response APIs then read their
same retained IDs and verify their same file hashes.

The recovery engine supports up to 10,000 entries, four GiB of plaintext, two
GiB per file and 16 directory levels; this operating wrapper reserves space for
its encrypted source mapping. Reads and encryption stream file contents.
Staging and restored files are private. No dependency installation, hosted job,
payment or network request is part of this operation.

# Client runbooks and period handovers

Client runbooks capture the instructions, supporting material and review decisions needed to hand a recurring close from one operator to another. They use the existing merchant accounting workspace and original writer lease. A period can freeze the client's own close files or an existing accountant handoff.

Open **Client runbooks** from the accounting navigation, or open /runbooks.html on the printed workspace address. Runbooks are also available through the original `merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks` command.

## Complete operating workflow

1. **Publish procedures.** Create a client runbook with a name, client, description and ordered procedures. Each procedure has a stable identifier, title, complete instructions, required flag and selected supporting resources. Resources may be an HTTPS recording/document link, a written note, or an uploaded original file. Publishing a change creates another immutable edition.
2. **Open a period.** Choose the saved edition, period label, preparer, reviewer and due date. Choose original client close files, supply a source label and working note, and select the uploaded originals. Alternatively select an existing accountant handoff and either its original edition or an explicit returned revision. If choosing a period close, use the close already frozen into that handoff. The period retains the chosen procedures and complete close source.
3. **Prepare the work.** Record each procedure as pending, complete, not applicable or an open item. Nonapplicable procedures and open items require an explanation. Upload working files and attach them to the relevant procedure. Work remains editable during preparation and returned corrections.
4. **Hand it to the reviewer.** Required procedures must be completed, explained as nonapplicable, or documented as open items. Submitting retains the full preparation round and its handover note. Review then operates on that unchanged submission.
5. **Return corrections or approve.** Returning requires a correction note. The preparer can amend the same period and submit a further round. Approval requires every required open item to be resolved or explicitly accepted with a review note and follow-up responsibility.
6. **Deliver the close.** Download the printable handover, the procedure/task CSV, and the complete portable JSON packet. The packet contains the frozen edition, current preparation, submission/review history, every selected supporting file and the selected original client files or accountant source revision.
7. **Receive and continue.** Receive the packet in another existing accounting workspace. Its imported period retains the original completed work and files. Start the next local period from the received procedure edition, select the receiving workspace's actual client files or accountant handoff, and optionally select the prior period. The new period begins with fresh pending work.

An edition published after a period opens applies to later selected periods. Existing periods retain their chosen edition. When an imported edition joins a book that already exists locally, it is retained in that book's history without changing its current latest edition.

HTTPS resources retain their original links. Uploaded resources travel as their exact selected files. The printable handover and task CSV can accompany the firm's existing close-management system; the portable packet carries the complete retained working material. Each task CSV row includes the saved Runbook ID, Edition ID, Period ID and Task ID, so a checklist mapping stays exact when titles repeat.

## Local CLI

Use the live server URL while the browser workspace is open:

```bash
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks status --url http://127.0.0.1:8446
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks sources --url http://127.0.0.1:8446
```

For a stopped workspace, replace `--url URL` with `--workspace /private/accounting-workspace`. The command reopens the existing workspace through its original owner and releases it on completion. The direct source entry is `node workspace/server.mjs runbooks`.

### Publish the first edition

Create a private `procedures.json` with the procedure content and actual operator:

```json
{
  "actor": "Close operator",
  "name": "Monthly close preparation",
  "client": "Example client",
  "description": "Prepare the retained settlement source for reviewer handover.",
  "resources": [
    {
      "id": "source-notes",
      "title": "Source selection",
      "kind": "note",
      "text": "Use the handoff selected for this period and document unresolved source questions."
    }
  ],
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "source-review",
      "title": "Review the source and open items",
      "instructions": "Open the period's accountant handoff, review its retained records and attach the working notes used for preparation.",
      "required": true,
      "resourceIds": ["source-notes"]
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks prepare --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --action save --input /private/procedures.json --out /private/publish-procedures.json
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks execute --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --prepared /private/publish-procedures.json
```

The saved response returns `runbookId` and `editionId`. Fetch `book --id RUNBOOK` for the complete edition. To publish a later edition, include that `runbookId` and its current `expectedEditionId` with the full revised content.

### Prepare a request, execute it and recover it

`prepare` supplies a UUID, the original workspace identity and its current revision. It retains the complete POST body, route, target and digest in a private file before sending anything. Input fields `workspaceId`, `requestId` and `revision` belong to that prepared file; action input contains the other documented fields.

Use the same `--prepared` file for execution and reconciliation:

```bash
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks reconcile --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --prepared /private/publish-procedures.json
```

A committed request returns its original compact result and revision. After a transport interruption, retain the request and execute it again if reconciliation has no saved operation. Exact replay resolves before the original workspace revision check. A response with `applied:false` permits correcting the input and preparing a new request. Commit/storage ambiguity retains the exact request for reconciliation.

| Action | Input fields besides actor |
|---|---|
| `save` | `name, client, description, resources, steps`; later editions also `runbookId, expectedEditionId` |
| `attach` | Optional `name, type`; select actual bytes with `--file` |
| `create` | `runbookId, editionId, label, preparer, reviewer, dueDate`; optional `previousCycleId`. For `sourceKind: "files"`, add `sourceLabel, sourceNote, sourceFileIds`. For `sourceKind: "accountant"` (default), add `handoffId, accountantRevisionId` and optional `periodCloseId`. |
| `work --id PERIOD` | `stepId, status, note, fileIds` |
| `submit --id PERIOD` | `note` |
| `review --id PERIOD` | `decision, note, acceptedExceptions` |
| `receive` | Select the complete packet using `--file` |

Dates use `YYYY-MM-DD`. Accountant revision selection is `initial` or a UUID returned by `sources`. Work statuses are `PENDING`, `COMPLETE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE` and `BLOCKED`. Review decisions are `APPROVE` and `RETURN`; `acceptedExceptions` contains selected procedure IDs.

### Deliver files

```bash
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks download --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --id PERIOD --format packet --out /private/client-close.json
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks download --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --id PERIOD --format print --out /private/client-close.html
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks download --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --id PERIOD --format tasks --out /private/client-close-tasks.csv
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace runbooks file --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --id FILE --out /private/original-working-file.pdf
```

Output files use private modes and create-only publication. Repeating a download into an existing path succeeds when its bytes are identical. A changed result needs a new filename.

## HTTP interface

All JSON responses identify the original `workspaceId` and current `revision`. POST requests use JSON and the existing `X-Workspace-Request: 1` header.

| Method and path | Result |
|---|---|
| GET `/api/runbooks` | Books, compact period summaries and retained file metadata |
| GET `/api/runbooks/sources` | Original handoffs, explicit return revisions and frozen closes |
| GET `/api/runbooks/books/:id` | Full book and immutable editions |
| POST `/api/runbooks/books/save` | Publish a complete edition |
| POST `/api/runbooks/files` | Retain base64 `content`, `name` and optional media `type` |
| GET `/api/runbooks/files/:id` | Exact original file |
| POST `/api/runbooks/cycles` | Create period from an explicit edition and original close source |
| GET `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id` | Complete period, work and preparation/review history |
| POST `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/work` | Save one procedure's completed work and files |
| POST `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/submit` | Retain a complete preparation round |
| POST `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/review` | Return corrections or approve the selected round |
| GET `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/packet` | Complete portable JSON handover |
| GET `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/print` | Standalone printable HTML handover |
| GET `/api/runbooks/cycles/:id/tasks.csv` | Task and procedure CSV |
| POST `/api/runbooks/receive` | Receive base64 packet `content` |
| GET `/api/runbooks/operations/:requestId` | Original committed request kind, target, digest and compact result |

Every mutation includes `workspaceId, requestId, revision, actor`. The request digest is SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON of `{kind,target,input}`, with sorted object keys, preserved array order and no final newline. `input` is the entire unchanged POST body. The target is the period ID for work, submit and review; it is `null` for the other actions.

Kinds are `edition_saved, file_retained, cycle_created, procedure_saved, preparation_submitted, review_saved, packet_received`. Accepted results retain IDs and file/receiving metadata. Clients fetch the complete current book or period after a saved or reconciled mutation. This keeps the operation journal proportional to work performed.

## Storage and receiving

Runbooks live in the existing `workspace.json`. Supporting files are content-addressed beneath `runbooks/files`; received complete packets are retained beneath `runbooks/packets`. All state changes use the original serial writer and workspace commit. New bytes are fully written and synchronized before create-only publication.

A portable packet verifies its canonical content, every attachment, each preparation/review join, its complete client-file source or original accountant handoff/return, and any report/manifest/input/close/adjustment bytes selected by those original accountant records. Exact packet replay reuses the received period. The same period ID with different content requires resolving the existing selection.

Operational limits are 8 MiB per supporting upload, 64 MiB per complete portable packet, 100 procedures/resources per edition, 200 runbooks, 200 retained editions per book, 2,000 periods/files and 20,000 compact operation entries. The underlying workspace retains its existing 32 MB state limit. Client-file mode retains the exact source documents without translating their currencies, accounts or accounting system. Keep long recordings at their source URL, retain the working instructions in the procedure, and include the original files needed by the next operator.

The browser keeps procedure, period, work, review and receiving drafts in its local IndexedDB, scoped to the original workspace and selected record. A retained pending request is reconciled against its original kind, target and digest before the browser accepts a committed result. The next operator receives the same complete period and opens the next close from its retained procedures.

## Issued buyer close handoffs

The same source selection accepts an original accountant handoff created from an
issued buyer expense period. The browser identifies the actual buyer workspace
and issued close. Select its exact accountant return in the same way as a
merchant handoff. Its buyer close, source context and native allocations stay in
the frozen source.

Portable receiving carries the complete original-buyer-source.json and recreates
the original handoff through the maintained buyer-aware accountant engine before
accepting it. The recreated handoff must match every retained source field, row,
label and identity. Selected returned CSV bytes and accountant return history
keep their existing validation. A received period can supply its original
procedures for the next locally selected close.

# Company chart source changes

This workflow replaces an unused QuickBooks or Xero accounting plan when the selected company's chart or organization source changes. It runs inside the existing merchant or buyer accounting workspace. Staff compare the original and current source editions, review every mapping and valuation, retain a native successor preview, then explicitly authorize cancellation of the unused predecessor and creation of that exact successor.

The original accounting handoff, economic rows, native plan history, provider identifiers and accountant returns remain in the same workspace. New QuickBooks plans still require the original review before posting or downloading their journal request. New Xero plans still use the original draft, native-response and accountant-return controls. Preparing or applying a source change does not invoke either provider.

## Open the complete workflow

Start or reopen the existing configured accounting application and open **Chart source changes** from the accounting, QuickBooks or Xero page. The direct route is `/source-changes.html`. A buyer-source workspace exposes the same workflow for its original Xero plans.

Use the original Connections page at `/connections.html` for approved QuickBooks company and chart captures. For Xero, retain the new organization/chart context through the existing page at `/xero.html`. Those existing workflows keep provider authorization, company or tenant selection, original source responses and saved source identity.

The source-change page also accepts an existing normalized QuickBooks company snapshot. This is the complete original `stellar-forge.quickbooks-company.v1` object produced by the maintained company normalizer, including its three source-document strings, source digests and integrity. A hand-edited list of account IDs is insufficient.

An older QuickBooks plan without a retained company snapshot remains accessible through its original page. Its missing historical chart cannot be reconstructed by choosing a new chart, so this replacement workflow requires an actual retained baseline.

## Staff workflow

1. **Select the original plan and the target source edition.** Keep the same QuickBooks realm and sandbox/production environment, or the same Xero tenant and demo/books identity. Xero contexts must already be retained in this workspace. QuickBooks source selections come from the original Connections review or a validated original snapshot.
2. **Compare the editions.** Read company name, base currency and account changes. Accounts are matched by their original native IDs. A renamed account or changed Xero account code remains connected to that same ID. The comparison identifies selected accounts that have changed or become unavailable.
3. **Review the successor mappings.** Existing eligible account IDs provide initial suggestions. Missing or ineligible accounts remain unselected. Staff choose the replacement accounts and explicitly review dates, values, descriptions and valuation notes. The workflow does not infer exchange rates. Original economic rows, buyer allocations and exclusions remain fixed.
4. **Retain the review.** Supply a reason, operator, successor name and explicit valuation confirmation. The exact source comparison, both source editions, original plan, complete native successor request and preview are retained before cancellation is possible. Keep the review UUID, successor UUID and original timestamp.
5. **Apply the exact review.** Confirm that the predecessor is unused, that no downloaded request from it was imported externally, and that the mappings are approved. The application retains an application UUID, exact request hash and cancellation intent before calling either original native method.
6. **Inspect the successor in the original provider page.** The source-change receipt links the cancelled predecessor and the successor. Continue normal QuickBooks review/posting or Xero draft/reconciliation/return from that successor. Any external accounting action still belongs to those original controls.
7. **Download the handoff and preserve the operating workspace.** The source-change download includes both source editions and the original retained plan files. The original full operating backup preserves the entire workspace and all other accounting work. Reopen that workspace and inspect the same review and native plan IDs.

The interface retains pending command bodies before dispatch. Large snapshot drafts use a browser database scoped to the current original workspace. The current workspace binding returned by the server controls every new request. The binding stored in an older review remains provenance; it is not permission to replay a pending command into a different workspace.

## Which plans can be replaced

| Provider | Required unused state | Preserved original restrictions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QuickBooks | DRAFT or REVIEWED, no cancellation, no native posting attempt and no received response | Other reviewed or booked plans continue to reserve the same realm/environment event IDs. The new plan remains DRAFT until its original review. |
| Xero | Active plan, all journals READY and unattempted, no native operation, capture, return intent or accountant return | All other active plans continue to reserve tenant/component identities and buyer workspace/economic IDs. The original cancellation also rejects a RUNNING operation. |

An attempted or posted plan can be compared when its original sources remain available. It cannot be replaced through this workflow. Correct it through its existing provider and accountant-return process. Never use a new source-change UUID to bypass an attempted plan's native history.

The implementation preserves the exact selected economic event/component set. It does not remove conflicting plans from the workspace, temporarily cancel them to manufacture a successful preview, release another plan's reservations, or change the original accountant baseline.

## Retained phases and recovery

| Phase | Actual retained state | Continue with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PREPARED | Both editions and the exact successor preview exist; no application intent exists | Review and approve this exact record |
| APPLYING | The original application intent exists; cancellation may already have completed | Inspect the same review, then resume its original application UUID |
| CANCELLED_PENDING_SUCCESSOR | The original predecessor is cancelled; the exact successor still needs confirmation or creation | Resume the same application UUID and successor request |
| COMPLETED | The native successor matches the retained preview and original economic source | Open the original successor or download the handoff |

A lost response is not evidence that an action failed. Keep the original request body and UUID. Read the same review before retrying. If the backend already retained an application intent, use `resume` with its original application UUID. Resume does not allocate a new successor or reverse a completed cancellation.

A known pre-intent application rejection is retained in that same review and in the original workspace history. Its receipt includes the application UUID and canonical request SHA256. Repeating that exact rejected request remains rejected. The browser can return to review only after matching the bound rejection and a fresh copy of that same retained record with no application intent. A generic 400/409, HTML response or network failure cannot release the pending command.

If an initial prepare request has no retained review, the explicit bound `SOURCE_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND` result and a fresh matching catalog allow the original draft to be reviewed again. An unreadable or unrelated 404 is an unknown outcome.

### A save with an uncertain durable outcome

The original accounting Store now marks `WORKSPACE_COMMIT_UNKNOWN` when it cannot confirm a durable save. A rename may have published the new `workspace.json` before a later directory sync failed. All subsequent mutations, including already queued actions from other accounting pages, are rejected until the original workspace closes and reopens. The response includes `outcomeUnknown: true` and `reopenRequired: true`; the normal state view also exposes the retained diagnostic.

Keep the original action and close the application through its existing lifecycle. Reopen the same workspace so the actual saved edition becomes authoritative, then inspect and resume the original review. Do not restore an older backup or delete the original workspace to resolve an uncertain response.

Xero plan creation now uses the original QuickBooks immutable packet pattern. Completed packet members are retained through interruption. A repeat of the same request reuses only files whose byte count and SHA256 match. Partial or conflicting bytes are preserved for diagnosis. A failed save does not delete a possibly committed successor's files. Xero context imports use the same immutable member publication, with an original import intent that preserves the request, creation time and source-observation metadata. An unchanged import UUID resumes those exact retained identities. A complete older context/source pair can be verified and reused; ambiguous partial earlier packets remain preserved.

The full Store history remains retained under its existing limits of 100,000 entries and 32 MB. The interface may show a shorter recent history; cancellation reconciliation uses the original full history and exact native cancellation fields.

## HTTP and typed embedding contract

The existing server's host, origin and `X-Workspace-Request: 1` checks remain in effect. POST bodies use `Content-Type: application/json`. Source-change requests have a 32 MiB whole-body limit; the original QuickBooks normalizer separately limits the combined source responses to 8 MiB.

Every successful JSON result returns:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.accounting-source-change.v1",
  "binding": {
    "workspaceId": "the current original workspace identity",
    "sourcesSha256": "the current configured source identity"
  }
}
```

Additional fields depend on the action. Identifiers in the following table refer to actual retained UUIDs.

| Method and path | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET /api/source-changes | None | Current binding/revision, original plan eligibility, retained Xero contexts and source-change records |
| GET /api/source-changes/sources | offset, limit query values | Paginated original Connections reviews, total and nextOffset |
| POST /api/source-changes/inspect | binding, kind, planId, target | Before/after comparison, actual normalized target accounts, defaults and predecessor eligibility |
| POST /api/source-changes/prepare | Inspection inputs, stable review id, predecessorSha256, comparisonSha256, rationale, valuationConfirmed and successor | The complete retained review and native preview |
| GET /api/source-changes/:id | None | Retained review, original intent/rejections and actual predecessor/successor state |
| POST /api/source-changes/:id/apply | binding, stable application id, previewSha256, current revision, actor, note and all three confirmations | The retained original application outcome |
| POST /api/source-changes/:id/resume | binding and original application id | Continuation of that exact retained intent |
| GET /api/source-changes/:id/download | None | A complete source-change JSON handoff attachment |

The target is one of:

```ts
{ kind: "qbo-review", id: reviewId, sha256: review.previewSha256 }
{ kind: "qbo-snapshot", snapshot: originalNormalizedCompany }
{ kind: "xero-context", id: contextId, sha256: contextSha256 }
```

A prepare request keeps its original `id` and successor identity. The successor contains `id`, canonical ISO `createdAt`, `name` and `actor`, plus:

- QuickBooks: `txnDate`, optional `docNumber`, and every original row as `{rowId,amount,debitAccount:{value},creditAccount:{value},description}`.
- Xero: `valuationBasis` and every included/excluded component. Included rows use `{componentId,decision:"include",date,amount,debitAccountCode,creditAccountCode,valuationNote,description}`. Original excluded rows remain `{componentId,decision:"exclude",reason}`.

The apply confirmations are exactly `unusedConfirmed: true`, `noExternalImport: true` and `mappingConfirmed: true`. Values and mappings are validated again against the current original source and native preview before the cancellation intent is retained.

Bound source-change errors contain `schema`, current `binding`, `reopenRequired`, `error`, `message` and `outcome`. Outcome is `unknown`, `not_found` or `rejected`. A terminal rejection additionally contains `command: {id,requestSha256,state:"rejected",error,message,createdAt}`. Host/body/parser failures outside this handler may lack the source-change binding; clients must treat those as unknown.

Canonical request hashes use recursively key-sorted JSON from the original QuickBooks canonical serializer. They cover the complete request, including binding and revision. Whitespace in a JSON transport is not a new request; changing a parsed field under an existing UUID is rejected.

The installed SDK exports are `./accounting/source-changes` and `./accounting/source-changes/model`, with adjacent TypeScript declarations. A hosting adapter supplies the original leased Store and existing QboWorkspace/XeroWorkspace instances:

```js
const changes = new SourceChangeWorkspace(workspace, {
  qbo: existingQuickBooksController,
  xero: existingXeroController,
  connections: existingConfiguredConnections
});
```

The existing accounting server constructs this once per active original workspace. Close the source-change controller before closing the native controllers and Store so its retained cancellation/create operation drains. It never closes a borrowed connection or starts a new provider engine.

## Downloads, complete backup and reopen

The source-change attachment uses `stellar-forge.accounting-source-change-handoff.v1`. It retains the immutable review bytes, current record, comparison and both original native plan packets. Each embedded file carries its path, byte count, SHA256 and base64 bytes; the handoff itself has a canonical SHA256.

QuickBooks' existing journal-export restriction remains effective. An unreviewed successor or cancelled predecessor does not gain a separate journal-entry download through this page. The handoff explicitly lists withheld native request files and their hashes. Complete private operating backup retains the entire workspace, including those original files.

Use the original **Operating backup and recovery** workflow, or stop the workspace and its original input writers and run the existing commands with a host-configured private passphrase:

```sh
starforge merchant-accounting-workspace backup \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --state-root /private/merchant \
  --out /private/backups/accounting-source-change \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE --quiesced

starforge merchant-accounting-workspace verify-backup \
  --bundle /private/backups/accounting-source-change \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE

starforge merchant-accounting-workspace restore \
  --workspace /private/merchant/accounting-workspace \
  --state-root /private/merchant \
  --bundle /private/backups/accounting-source-change \
  --pass-env STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE --quiesced
```

These are the original encrypted operating recovery APIs. Restore uses the original absolute paths, preserves changed existing files and continues an interrupted restore using the same backup and paths. Buyer-source mode preserves its complete original accounting directory and issued source. The new source-change records and files are inside that directory and therefore join the same backup.

After reopen, read the current catalog, open the same review UUID and verify the original predecessor, successor, preview hash, phase and application intent. Continue from the actual saved state. Provider tokens and authorization stores remain under the original host's separate credential and grant-store custody.

## Commissioning in an existing receiving operation

Use the original accounting receiving owner, workspace and provider transport. Supply an actual unused original plan, its already retained target chart edition, and staff-reviewed successor values. Complete the interface sequence from comparison through original successor review, preserve the exact download, then use the owner's original backup/reopen step and inspect the same IDs.

If the selected receiving plan already has a native attempt or an accountant return, verify its comparison and refusal to replace it, and retain the real reason. That existing plan is not an eligible unused predecessor. A complete replacement needs another actual unused plan selected by the original owner. No provider or application run is implied by source publication.

# Xero journals in the merchant accounting workspace

The original accounting workspace can now carry a frozen payment/refund handoff into a balanced Xero manual-journal plan, retain native draft creation and read responses, and apply the resulting bookkeeping return through the original accountant history.

Open **Xero journals** from the Accountant handoff panel, or open the running workspace's `/xero.html` page. The existing `merchant-accounting-workspace xero` command provides the same lifecycle. The original workspace directory, process lease, maintenance controller, backup, restore and reopen own the source and delivery state.

## Complete operator workflow

1. **Prepare the original accountant handoff.** Choose the retained reconciliation or period close in the existing accounting workspace. Its exact report, payment rows, frozen refund snapshot, review notes and source manifests accompany the Xero plan.
2. **Select the organization.** Read the native Organization and Accounts endpoints with the configured connection, or import their original JSON response files. Supply the Xero tenant UUID. The adapter verifies the returned organization ID, active state, base currency, demo flag, and unique account IDs/codes.
3. **Value each original component.** Every payment and every independently verified native refund appears separately. Choose an explicit journal date, a value in the organization's base currency, a debit account, a credit account, and the valuation source. Excluding a component requires a reason. Original atomic amounts and asset identities remain beside these choices. The adapter does not calculate fiat value from a token amount or a merchant quote.
4. **Review and save the plan.** Each component produces an equal debit and credit pair. Journals group up to 100 components by the chosen date, retain their exact native payloads, and use `DRAFT`, `NoTax` and an explicit cash-basis-report setting. The plan records the operator's valuation and tax-treatment explanation. Active plans reserve the same native payment or refund component within the selected tenant, including across later handoffs and imported context snapshots.
5. **Create drafts or use the retained native payloads.** The connection sends one original manual-journal request per retained journal. Its request and stable idempotency key are written before the native call. The operator can also download the exact native JSON payloads for an existing approved Xero integration.
6. **Read or import the returned journals.** Refresh uses the known native journal UUID, or searches the exact original narration through the terminal empty page. Import accepts original `ManualJournals` JSON response files. Comparison retains every source file and checks journal ID uniqueness, date, narration, tax/cash treatment, debit and credit values, account codes and IDs when returned, and exact descriptions. Warnings and validation errors remain visible.
7. **Preview and apply the original accountant return.** An exact active draft match proposes `REVIEWED`. Posted matches in a merchant-books plan propose `BOOKED`; demo plans remain `REVIEWED`. Payment references point to the native gross journal; separate refund journals are recorded in the note. Later manual accountant edits produce a displayed conflict instead of being overwritten. A later native refresh can advance an earlier Xero draft return to posted status through its recorded original return.
8. **Download and reopen.** The complete archive contains the saved plan, native payloads, original accounting companions, organization/accounts source, every native operation and comparison, linked original accountant returns, current delivery state, and a file manifest. Reopen the same original workspace to continue.

A demo plan requires the native Xero demo-company flag. A merchant-books plan requires a non-demo organization and original independently matched public-network payment/refund source. The selected purpose remains in the source and review.

## Native connection

Set `STARFORGE_XERO_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the original server process environment using the merchant's existing authorized Xero application. The browser and request files contain no access token. The same environment setting applies to direct `--workspace` CLI use.

Before creating drafts, the original operation reads and retains the current native organization and chart once more. The base currency, demo identity, and selected active account IDs/codes must still match the reviewed plan. This also binds imported account source to the selected live tenant before any draft write.

The adapter calls only `https://api.xero.com/api.xro/2.0/` and passes the selected `xero-tenant-id`. It reads `Organisation`, `Accounts`, and `ManualJournals`; draft creation uses **PUT ManualJournals** with `summarizeErrors=false` and the retained `Idempotency-Key`. The application needs the corresponding Xero accounting settings/read and transactions/read/write access for the chosen operations. Obtain and renew the token through that application's existing OAuth connection.

Source: Xero's maintained [Accounting OpenAPI schema](https://github.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI/blob/master/xero_accounting.yaml), [Manual Journals API](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/manualjournals/), [Accounts API](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/accounts/), and [Organization API](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/organisation/).

Bank, receivable/payable control, and other native system accounts that cannot receive manual journals are excluded from the account selectors. Other active accounts retain their native account type and system-account identity. Choose the clearing/asset and income/expense accounts appropriate to the original event; the adapter supplies no automatic accounting classification. See Xero's [locked and system account guidance](https://central.xero.com/0/article/Locked-and-system-accounts-in-your-chart-of-accounts).

Only the original reviewed draft payload is created. Posting, editing or voiding a journal remains a native Xero operation. Refresh brings the resulting native state back into this workspace.

## Retained operation recovery

A process interruption marks the original in-flight operation `INTERRUPTED`; an uncertain sent draft remains an existing attempt. Refresh reads its original exact narration or UUID. The adapter never automatically resends an uncertain creation.

Explicit new creation operations can retry requests rejected before journal creation by the native authentication, routing or rate-limit response. They retain the same journal payload and idempotency key, with a new operation record containing the new response. Provider retry headers are kept with the original response for the operator.

Successful responses from a partially completed native operation remain usable. Its comparison records the exact operation and the journals actually observed; a missing response does not become proof that a native journal is absent.

Accountant application first retains the exact original import request and preview. If the process stops between preparing, applying and linking that original return, **Complete retained accountant return** reuses the same request and original return UUID. The original accountant importer performs the idempotent application.

Unused plans can be cancelled with a recorded reason and confirmation that their downloaded payloads were never imported externally. The original source remains available for review.

## CLI

Use the existing distribution command or the original source entrypoint:

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace xero status --url http://127.0.0.1:8446

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/server.mjs \
  xero --help
```

Use `--url` for a running original workspace. Use `--workspace /private/accounting-workspace` to reopen a stopped one through its original owner. Output files use mode 0600 and must be new.

### Organization source request

`import-context --input context.json` accepts:

```json
{
  "id": "OPERATION_UUID",
  "revision": 12,
  "name": "Merchant organization",
  "actor": "Operator name",
  "tenantId": "NATIVE_ORGANIZATION_UUID",
  "organizationBase64": "BASE64_OF_ORIGINAL_ORGANISATION_RESPONSE",
  "accountsBase64": "BASE64_OF_ORIGINAL_ACCOUNTS_RESPONSE"
}
```

`capture-context` uses the same request without the two file fields. It reads both original native endpoints using the process connection. Use the current workspace revision from `status`.

### Journal request and review

Read `source --handoff HANDOFF_ID --context CONTEXT_ID` to obtain exact component IDs and the current accountant baseline revision. The preview request contains:

```json
{
  "id": "PLAN_UUID",
  "name": "Merchant period journal",
  "actor": "Operator name",
  "handoffId": "ORIGINAL_HANDOFF_UUID",
  "contextId": "RETAINED_CONTEXT_UUID",
  "accountantRevisionId": "initial",
  "purpose": "demo",
  "valuationBasis": "Operator-selected valuation source and NoTax treatment",
  "showOnCashBasisReports": false,
  "entries": [
    {
      "componentId": "EXACT_COMPONENT_SHA256",
      "decision": "include",
      "date": "2026-10-11",
      "amount": "12.34",
      "debitAccountCode": "OPERATOR_SELECTED_CODE",
      "creditAccountCode": "OPERATOR_SELECTED_CODE",
      "valuationNote": "Original rate or valuation reference",
      "description": "Original merchant payment"
    },
    {
      "componentId": "ANOTHER_EXACT_COMPONENT_SHA256",
      "decision": "exclude",
      "reason": "Operator's explicit exclusion reason"
    }
  ]
}
```

Use the returned accountant revision UUID instead of `initial` when selecting an existing returned baseline. The decimal amount is text with at most two fractional digits. Values are converted with integer cents, checked for exact native JSON representation, and paired to an exact zero balance.

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace xero preview --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --input /private/journal-request.json --out /private/journal-preview.json
merchant-accounting-workspace xero save --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --preview /private/journal-preview.json
```

The saved preview contains the stable request, original plan hash and workspace revision. A changed workspace revision requires a fresh preview.

### Native operation

`operate --plan PLAN_ID --input operation.json` accepts `id`, current workspace `revision`, `actor`, `action` (`create-drafts` or `refresh`), and the exact saved `planSha256`. It waits for the retained native operation and prints its result. `operation --plan PLAN_ID --operation OPERATION_ID` reopens that original result.

For original response-file import, `import-response --plan PLAN_ID --input responses.json` accepts:

```json
{
  "id": "CAPTURE_UUID",
  "revision": 17,
  "actor": "Operator name",
  "files": [
    {"name": "native-manual-journals.json", "base64": "BASE64_OF_ORIGINAL_RESPONSE"}
  ]
}
```

### Accountant return and complete archive

The return request contains `id`, `name`, `actor`, and optionally a stable `createdAt` or the expected current `expectedParentId`.

```sh
merchant-accounting-workspace xero preview-return --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --plan PLAN_ID --capture CAPTURE_ID --input /private/return-request.json \
  --out /private/return-preview.json
merchant-accounting-workspace xero apply-return --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --plan PLAN_ID --capture CAPTURE_ID --preview /private/return-preview.json
merchant-accounting-workspace xero download --url http://127.0.0.1:8446 \
  --plan PLAN_ID --file xero-handoff.tar --out /private/merchant-xero-handoff.tar
```

All protected accountant source columns come from the original rendered handoff. The original importer still determines the applied return, retains its source CSV, and writes the original return archive.

## Source and packaging

The implementation adds no package dependency:

- `accountant/xero.mjs`: native source model, exact-valued draft journals, native comparison and original accountant return preparation.
- `accountant/xero-http.mjs`: fixed-origin native Xero transport.
- `workspace/xero-workspace.mjs`: original workspace-owned source custody, operations, recovery, return application and downloads.
- `workspace/xero-cli.mjs`: the same original owner and routes through the existing distribution command.
- `workspace/public/xero.*`: the loopback operator interface.

The existing merchant-accounting-workspace distribution component already includes this original subtree and server entrypoint. Native Xero state is inside the original accounting workspace directory, so the existing encrypted backup and restore includes it with the same maintained owner.
