# Receive and continue a saved support handoff

The Handoffs section receives an existing merchant MCP support export into this same merchant workspace. It shows the retained case identity and original files, resumes an interrupted transfer, and opens the received case in the existing case editor. It uses the original support downloader, completion manifest and case store.

## Configure a receiving workstation

Use the complete repository or current complete distribution and Node 22 or newer. The source merchant MCP must already have the support export you want to receive. Obtain its export ID from that existing operation; receiving does not create another export.

The operator who runs this workstation supplies one private source configuration file. Source URLs, access credentials and local directory paths stay on the host. Each source has a short alias and a label shown in the browser:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.support-handoff-sources.v1",
  "sources": {
    "merchant-operations": {
      "label": "Merchant operations",
      "url": "https://merchant-operations.example/mcp",
      "tokenEnv": "MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN",
      "directory": "/private/stellar-forge/received-handoffs"
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the example URL with the actual MCP endpoint. HTTPS is accepted; literal loopback HTTP is also available for an existing local MCP. URLs with credentials, query strings or fragments are rejected. The token named by `tokenEnv` must already be available in the server process environment; the JSON contains its environment-variable name, not the credential value. A source can still open its completed local files when its credential is absent.

Create the receiving directories before starting the desk. Set the configuration file to mode `0600` and the receiving directories to `0700`. Each source directory must be separate from every other source directory and from the case directory: neither equal paths nor nested roots are accepted. A relative source directory is resolved against the configuration file's parent directory. Keep each source alias, endpoint and directory stable across restarts so existing transfers retain their original binding.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs \
  --cases-dir /private/stellar-forge/merchant-cases \
  --handoff-sources /private/stellar-forge/handoff-sources.json \
  --port 8784
```

Open the printed loopback address on the same workstation. Handoffs appears when this configuration is enabled. The server reads local transfer history on page load; it contacts the source only after an explicit inspection or download action. The browser cannot submit a different endpoint, credential or filesystem path.

## Receive the original export

1. Select the configured source and enter the original export ID.
2. Choose **Inspect source handoff**. Review the source case, revision, creation time, original filenames, sizes and manifest identity. This inspection reads the existing completion manifest.
3. Start the download. The request is bound to the exact inspected manifest. The original downloader saves each received range and checkpoint in the source's private directory. Progress reports saved bytes for each file.
4. Use **Stop** when needed. The current operation stops and retains its completed bytes. Select the same source and export ID and resume; a changed source export is rejected rather than mixed into the retained transfer.
5. After completion, open the received case. The existing case editor retains the original workspace, support sources and metadata. If another case has unsaved changes, its normal keep/discard/save flow appears before switching.

The workstation supports up to two active transfers. A second request for an already active source/export uses the same operation. Transfer history and pagination read the local checkpoints, so operators can find an interrupted export without requesting a new source export. A stopped or restarted browser can return to **View saved transfer** and continue the same work.

## Continue the received case

Use the existing case editor to change ownership, follow-up date, status, notes or workorder terms, then save the case normally. Opening the same completed handoff again returns to that same local case and its current revision. It retains the original imported revision and does not replace later edits.

Opening a completed handoff verifies its original file bytes before importing or reopening it. Original file downloads also verify the retained size and SHA-256 before returning an attachment. Completion history records the original successful transfer; a later file change is detected when it is opened or downloaded.

The complete local handoff remains usable while its source MCP is offline. Open the saved transfer, open the received case, and download its original files from the same workstation. Inspections and resumptions require the configured source to be available again.

## Restart, recovery and retention

Stop the console with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. It cancels its own active transfers and waits for their retained checkpoint work before closing. Restart with the same configuration and case directory, select the saved transfer, and resume. The original download lease also protects the same directory from concurrent CLI and browser writers.

Keep the entire receiving root, including each export's `download-state` directory and completion manifest. Back up that root together with the original case directory and private source configuration. The environment credential is managed separately by the host's existing secret configuration. Removing or moving checkpoints can break the connection to the original imported case.

| Observed condition | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| Source unavailable or credential unavailable | Restore the existing source connection or process credential, then resume the same export. Completed local handoffs can still be opened. |
| Source manifest changed | Confirm the intended retained export with its source owner. Keep the existing local files; use the correct distinct source export ID. |
| Another transfer owns the directory | Return to that existing operation or wait for its owner to finish. Use the original downloader's stopped-writer recovery when applicable. |
| Local file or checkpoint differs | Preserve the retained directory and inspect its original completion/checkpoint with the existing support CLI. Do not replace files from a different export. |
| Receiving disk is full | Make space on the workstation, then resume the same saved transfer. |
| Case revision conflict | Use the original case editor's latest-version or save-separately actions. |

See [case desk operations](CASE_DESK.md) for case backups, conflicts and saved-version recovery, [runtime support](RUNTIME_SUPPORT.md) for the retained sources and workorder flow, and the [merchant MCP support guide](../../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/SUPPORT.md) for source exports and CLI transfer/recovery.

`handoff-store.mjs` supplies host-configured source aliases and a small in-process job registry. `handoff-desk.mjs` renders this section in the original page. # Merchant implementation and receiving

The **Implementation and receiving** desk completes the existing SF74 merchant case after its workorder is prepared. The same saved case carries the customer task, assigned implementation, original deliverables, receiving decisions and measured effort. Browser, HTTP, CLI and MCP operations use one workspace format and the original case writer.

The source/terms preparation in [SF49 source-edition commissioning](../../scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/SOURCE_EDITION_COMMISSIONING.md) and the original [SF77 workorder](../sf77-merchant-workorder/README.md) supply the agreed work. This desk turns those milestones into editable implementation tasks. Existing runtime, incident, payment, merchant-release and buyer operations retain their own saved records; attach their actual output or refer to those records from the implementation.

## Use the complete browser workflow

Start the existing console with its private case directory, or open its configured application from the maintained Applications workspace:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs \
  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \
  --port 8784
~~~

Open the printed local address. Reopen the relevant merchant case, including its original source captures, attached runtime and owner terms.

1. **Generate the original workorder.** Choose the existing diagnostic or attached-runtime source, review its terms, and select **Create workorder**. The implementation panel displays the workorder reference, changed route scope, new milestones and changed source fields.
2. **Use the workorder.** Enter the actual operator in **Recorded by**, review the source changes, and select **Use this workorder**. The exact packet, HTML, acceptance checklist and every supplied original input become a retained edition. Reusing an identical retained edition selects its existing identity.
3. **Describe the useful customer result.** Fill in the customer task, implementation payer, merchant, buyer, original source location, merchant host, consuming application, complete output, repeat trigger, implementation and receiving owners, and support scope. Keep the original commercial record linked here. Draft plan changes are included by **Save case**.
4. **Assign and perform the work.** Give the original milestones owners, due dates, acceptance criteria, prerequisites and implementation notes. Add the actual integration tasks needed for this customer. Status and retirement are explicit operator choices. Task search and paging retain the complete case; they do not truncate it.
5. **Attach original deliverables.** Select the actual files, their purpose, source reference and related tasks. Files keep their original names and bytes. Mark observation files as observations; customer files, source inputs, installation files and guides can form part of the delivered work.
6. **Record receiving.** Select the actual workorder edition, receiving kind, tasks, original deliverables, observation time and result. Enter the receiving operator, record or application reference, and what was observed. Technical receiving and customer receiving have separate totals.
7. **Measure the customer task.** Record a before, installed or later recurring observation using the same task definition, comparison identifier, output and unit. Enter actual input population, quantity, operator time, elapsed time and corrections as available. Keep original measurement files and references attached.
8. **Save and hand over.** **Save case** retains the whole implementation. The existing complete support export carries it to the receiving desk. The implementation section also downloads the readable report, task CSV and complete implementation JSON.

Plan and task edits are part of the case draft immediately. A receiving or measurement form becomes a recorded observation when its **Record** button succeeds; then save the case. Form values survive related attachment/task refreshes. Opening another case uses the existing case desk's draft transition controls.

## Source editions and operator choices

The original workorder reference and milestone key identify a source task. A later workorder with the same reference updates source-owned title and acceptance text when those fields still match the earlier source. Deliberately edited text remains in place, with the new source value displayed for selective adoption.

Owners, due dates, status, prerequisites and notes remain operator work. A milestone missing from the new source receives a visible retirement proposal. The task and its original receiving history stay available. A different workorder reference creates a separate set of source task identities inside the same case; the earlier work can be reviewed and retired deliberately.

The **Workorders, history and handover** section opens the exact earlier packet and inputs. Reviewing and using an earlier edition selects that source for the current workplan. All later source files, deliverables and receiving observations remain retained.

### Receiving is tied to the actual delivered subject

Each receiving record saves a SHA-256 digest and complete subject snapshot containing:

- the selected task titles, acceptance criteria and prerequisites;
- the delivery-relevant customer task, merchant, buyer, source, host, consuming application and output definition;
- the inspected original file IDs and hashes;
- the task-linked deliverable set for that workorder edition.

Current accepted totals include only observations whose subject still matches. Changing the task definition or adding linked delivery files makes the earlier observation historical and increments **Receiving needs updating**. Changing a task's owner, due date, status or work notes leaves its delivery definition intact.

A correction retains the original task scope, delivery definition and delivered file set. It can correct the observed result, time, reference or notes and attach additional observation files. Record a new receiving observation for changed work or new deliverables. The earlier row remains in the history and identifies its correction. The most recent observed receiving result is selected independently for technical and customer receiving.

### Compare actual effort

Measurements retain their original edition, task definition, output, unit, input description, observed time, operator, files and reference. Comparisons select an earlier baseline with the same comparison identifier, exact task definition, output and unit. Corrections supersede the selected earlier measurement while preserving it.

The report shows recorded totals, arithmetic changes and percentages. When quantities differ, it identifies the volume difference and also computes per-unit time and corrections where both quantities are positive. A missing value stays blank, a measured zero stays zero, and a zero baseline has no percentage denominator. Each comparison links its two original measurement records.

## Save, restore and recover

The original case revision is the outer concurrency boundary. Every API or MCP mutation requires the exact current saved case revision. The implementation also carries an integer revision; commands require that current value.

Keep one stable request ID and the exact original command payload. On a lost response, inspect the original case and repeat the same command. Its retained operation is checked before current revision rejection, so a successful original request is returned without applying it again. Reusing an ID for a different payload is a conflict.

The saved-case preparation command also retains its exact compiled edition. Recovery reuses that packet and its original inputs rather than generating a second workorder with another timestamp.

Restoring an older case version applies the selected historical workplan while retaining all later immutable editions, files, receiving records, measurements and operation identities. Later-only tasks remain available as retired tasks so historical references stay usable. The restore creates a new current case version. The browser receives the canonical merged implementation after save. Older clients that omit the optional implementation field preserve the existing saved implementation.

Private case writer ownership, stopped-process recovery and immutable version storage remain the original [case desk](CASE_DESK.md) operations.

## Installed CLI

The source-owned `merchant-implementation` contribution registers the original CLI and both programmatic interfaces. Its complete source is included by the original distribution builder.

~~~sh
starforge registrations --source merchant-implementation
starforge registrations --command merchant-implementation
starforge merchant-implementation --help
~~~

The following paths, IDs and hashes stand for the operator's actual retained values.

Read the current implementation and every requested task page:

~~~sh

  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \

starforge merchant-implementation read \
~~~

A section returns `total` and `nextOffset`. Continue from that returned offset until it is null. Sections are `overview`, `tasks`, `materials`, `receiving`, `measurements`, `events`, `editions`, `files` and `comparisons`. An explicit `--revision` opens a retained historical case.

Prepare the implementation directly from the saved case:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-implementation prepare \
  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \
  --case CASE_UUID --revision CURRENT_CASE_SHA256 \
  --implementation-revision 0 \
  --request-id original-workorder-operation \
  --actor "Actual implementation operator"
~~~

Use the returned case and implementation revisions for the next mutation. Supply `--recorded-at` only when deliberately retaining a specific actual UTC preparation time.

Attach an original private deliverable:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-implementation attach \
  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \
  --case CASE_UUID --revision CURRENT_CASE_SHA256 \
  --implementation-revision CURRENT_INTEGER \
  --request-id original-deliverable-operation \
  --actor "Actual implementation operator" \
  --file /absolute/private/original-deliverable.csv \

~~~

Apply a saved original command file:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-implementation apply \
  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \
  --case CASE_UUID --revision CURRENT_CASE_SHA256 \
  --command-file /absolute/private/original-command.json
~~~

The command document has `type`, `requestId`, integer `expectedRevision`, `actor` and `payload`, plus an optional UTC `recordedAt`. `expectedRevision` inside the document is the implementation revision; the command-line `--revision` is the saved case SHA-256.

Export the complete selected implementation and receiving package:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-implementation export \
  --cases-dir /absolute/private/merchant-cases \
  --case CASE_UUID --revision SELECTED_CASE_SHA256 \
  --out /absolute/private/received-implementation
~~~

The output includes case metadata, the exact workspace, complete implementation JSON, readable HTML, task CSV and every original edition/input/material file. If the selected case has an attached runtime, the same manifest also contains the original complete `merchant-support.json` handoff and `support.html` report. The original `support-export.json` manifest is also included, followed by the complete `implementation-export.json` inventory. Repeating the export verifies matching retained files; different existing bytes are preserved and reported as a conflict.

For the complete automatic receiving flow, export under the configured MCP private exports directory using a matching export ID, then select that original named export in the Handoffs desk. The package includes the same `support-export.json` schema used by MCP; its existing manifest/file reader transfers the exact workspace and case metadata for both diagnostic and runtime cases. `--export-id` sets the original ID; otherwise it is the output directory basename. A runtime case can also import its `merchant-support.json` directly through the existing portable support-file flow.

| Operation | HTTP | MCP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read implementation or a complete selected page | `GET /api/cases/ID/implementation?section=tasks&offset=0&limit=100` | `merchant_case_implementation` |
| Prepare from the exact saved case | `POST /api/cases/ID/implementation/prepare` | `merchant_case_implementation_prepare` |

A prepare body contains `expectedRevision`, `expectedImplementationRevision`, `requestId` and `actor`. An apply body contains `expectedRevision` and `command`. MCP adds the original `id` field to select the case. The request ID and original payload must remain stable when recovering a response.

### Command payloads

| Type | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `update_plan` | Any supplied fields from the implementation plan; omitted fields remain. |
| `save_tasks` | `tasks`: a batch of task IDs and changed title, acceptance, owner, dueOn, status, notes, dependencies or retired values. A new non-source ID creates an operator task. |
| `accept_source_changes` | `changes`: selected `taskId` / `field` pairs currently proposed by the workorder source. |
| `select_workorder` | The retained `editionId` to use for the current workplan. |
| `record_workorder` | The original `result` (`packet`, `html`, `checklist`), exact `inputs` and optional original `sourceCase`. Use saved-case preparation for the ordinary MCP workflow. |
| `add_material` | Stable material `id`, kind, description, taskIds, optional editionId and reference. Inline files use original basename, mediaType and canonical Base64 `data`; native files use the retained `sourceFile` bundle/manifest/path reference. |
| `record_receiving` | Stable `id`, editionId, taskIds, materialIds, kind, outcome, observedAt, reference, notes and optional supersedesId. The shared module captures the exact receiving subject. |
| `record_measurement` | Stable `id`, editionId, phase, taskDefinition, comparisonKey, inputDescription, outputDescription, unit, nullable units/activeMinutes/elapsedMinutes/manualCorrections, observedAt, materialIds, reference, notes and optional supersedesId. |

Task statuses are `planned`, `in_progress`, `ready`, `done` and `retired`. Receiving kinds are `technical` and `customer`. Outcomes are `accepted`, `changes_required`, `not_run` and `not_applicable`.

The existing MCP Support export adds three files when the selected case has an implementation: `merchant-commissioning.json`, `merchant-implementation.html` and `merchant-implementation-tasks.csv`. Its original named export, complete manifest and retained chunk reader deliver those bytes. The workspace and support handoff contain the implementation, inline original files and compact native source references. ## Source and file capacity

Original workorder and material files are SHA-256 addressed and deduplicated within the implementation. An inline file can be up to 48 MiB; the complete implementation JSON can be up to 64 MiB. Larger originals remain in the native SF49 source store and are referenced by their complete manifest/member identity. Its original carrier accepts attachments up to 8 GiB within the native source population allowance; runtime handoff and archive bounds derive from the current original source modules. The surrounding workspace and support handoff have their matching expanded transport budgets. File selection, decoding and full import validate before changing the saved case.

The CLI uses the existing private file reader. Source documents, customer deliverables, observation references and complete handoffs remain in the original private case and export directories. The implementation source and operating guide are distributable application code.

## Native continuation

Continue from the existing completed SF74 support case and its retained original sources. The useful receiving journey is:

1. reopen that exact case and prepare its original workorder;
2. assign the complete source milestones and customer implementation work;
3. attach its actual original output, record the actual receiving observation and save;
4. edit a received task and confirm the current receiving indicator changes with its definition;
5. record a new observation for the changed subject and a correction of an earlier observation;
6. reopen the saved case through MCP and CLI, then export the complete private package;
7. import through the original Support receiving desk and reopen its runtime, metadata, workplan and original files;
8. restore the earlier selected workplan and confirm the later immutable observations and files remain available;
9. recover an exact earlier request and resume useful work from the received case.

Reuse the original completed captures and installation. The saved operation and actual receiving output identify where that continuation has reached.

# Incident sources in the merchant support console

The SF74 console operates the existing SF93 incident stores. Select a registered
source to review its incidents, run or stop a watcher owned by this console,
acknowledge the work, manage its original notification queue, and carry retained
captures into the existing merchant case.

## Connect existing stores

Use Node 22 or newer on Linux with util-linux `flock`. Run the console as the
operating-system user that owns the incident directories and notification
environment. Each source must already be initialized by the original SF93
`incident-cli.mjs init` command. The existing
[incident operating guide](../sf93-seller-support-bundle/INCIDENT_OPERATIONS.md)
covers merchant registration, seller/operations startup, capture retention and
backup.

Create a private configuration outside the repository, for example
`/srv/stellar/operator/incident-sources.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.support-incident-sources.v1",
  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "merchant-operations",
      "label": "Merchant operations",
      "directory": "incidents"
    },
    {
      "id": "partner-operations",
      "label": "Partner operations",
      "directory": "/srv/stellar/partner/incidents"
    }
  ]
}
```

The file must be owned by the console user, be a regular file with no group or
other permissions, and fit within 65,536 bytes. Use mode `0600`; original state
directories use `0700`. Relative directories resolve beside this configuration
file. Each configured directory is checked by the original private store
opener, including its existing state and lock directories.

Configure up to eight sources. IDs start with a lowercase letter or digit and
contain at most 64 lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
`profiles`, `constructor` and `prototype` are reserved. Labels contain at most
120 UTF-8 bytes. Two IDs cannot select the same canonical store directory.
Source IDs remain stable across a console restart; edits to this source list
take effect when the console reopens the configuration.

Start the existing console from the repository root:

```bash
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs \
  --incident-sources /srv/stellar/operator/incident-sources.json \
  --cases-dir /srv/stellar/operator/cases \
  --port 8784
```

Open the printed `127.0.0.1` URL. The Incident sources control lists only the
configured IDs and labels. The browser chooses those IDs; the server resolves
their already configured private directories. A missing `--incident-sources`
option keeps the incident panel disabled.

Supply Slack or webhook values through the console process environment using
the names in the original watcher configuration. The source-list file selects
stores. Their existing watcher configuration selects merchants, thresholds and
notification destinations. The
[Slack operating guide](../sf93-seller-support-bundle/SLACK_OPERATIONS.md)
describes workspace/channel IDs and the token environment reference.

## Operate the original watcher and queue

Opening the console reads retained state. **Start watcher here** starts the
original SF93 watcher against the displayed configuration revision and digest.
An intervening configuration change returns a conflict so the operator can
refresh and select the current registration.

The worker panel identifies a watcher started by this console and displays
the original recorded process, sweep and stop metadata. **Stop this watcher**
aborts and drains the worker that this console started. Closing the server
with SIGINT or SIGTERM also drains its owned watchers. The original kernel
lease decides whether another watcher currently owns a source; a historical
`RUNNING` heartbeat can remain after a crash. An active external watcher can
continue collecting while this console performs acknowledgments, queue
operations and configuration changes.

The list supports search, status, merchant and condition filters through the
API, with a default page of 20 incidents and a maximum of 100. The interface
refreshes active operations every five seconds while visible. Counts include
open and acknowledged incidents, pending deliveries, paused deliveries,
exhausted deliveries and the original notification capacity counter.

Open an incident to see its retained observations, before/after capture
references, acknowledgment and notification history. Notification rows use
the original sanitized status projection and retain accepted Slack message
and thread timestamps. The original queue owns the attempt identity,
destination, retry body, provider cooldown and acceptance receipt.

**Acknowledge incident** uses the incident revision that was displayed, records
the named operator and note, and queues the original acknowledgment transition.
If the source recovers or another operator changes the incident first, refresh
the current record before acting again.

**Send an operator reminder** selects the current configured destination through
the original queue. The console sends both the displayed incident revision and
latest notification ID. The original `remindIncident` transaction checks both
before queuing another event. Repeating a request after a lost response cannot
silently create another reminder against the same displayed selection.
Existing CLI callers that omit the additional notification expectation retain
their original behavior.

Use **Retry delivery** for a paused or exhausted event at its retained destination.
Use **Cancel delivery** for an unfinished event that no longer needs delivery.
Both operations use the displayed attempt count and named operator. The original
queue rejects changes to in-flight or completed events. A new configured
destination is selected with an operator reminder; existing queued events keep
their retained destination binding.

**Apply configuration** delegates to the original configuration compiler and
revision check. The original model handles registration changes, incident
retirement and notification scope. **Verify Slack workspace** invokes the
original read-only actor/workspace check and displays its current result;
channel message acceptance appears separately in actual delivery receipts.

## Continue an incident as a merchant case

Load or edit the current merchant workspace and choose the advertised route
from the incident's original capture choices. Each choice records its original
route ID and method, its path when provided by the original packet, and the
before/after side where it appeared. Choose a route whose method matches the
current workspace and that exists in every capture being attached.

The route choices are obtained through the original `inspectRuntimeFiles`
parser. Successful projections are cached by immutable capture hash, with a
maximum of 64 entries per source, so routine detail refreshes reuse already
validated route metadata. A damaged or unavailable retained capture is shown
as a capture problem while incident ownership and delivery history remain
available.

**Prepare incident case** holds the original read-only state transaction while
selecting the displayed incident revision and reading its exact retained
capture files. It then uses the original runtime support parser and handoff
exporter with the current serialized workspace and explicit route mapping.
Capture content hashes are checked again during preparation. Original before
and after sessions retain their own identities and comparison behavior.

Download the original support handoff and readable review, or select
**Open prepared case**. The existing case desk imports the original handoff's
workspace, support text and metadata. Incident ID, registration, condition,
timestamps and acknowledgment travel in the original case notes. Use
**Save case** to retain the continued work in the existing case directory.

## Embedded backend contract

`openIncidentSources({configPath, environment})` exposes the operations below.
HTTP routes belong to the existing local console server, which checks its exact
loopback Host, same-origin requests, route syntax and bounded JSON bodies.

| Method | Arguments after source ID | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles()` | None | Source-list schema and `sources: [{id,label}]` |
| `list(sourceId, filters)` | `q,status,merchant,kind,offset,limit` | Source, directory/config revisions, config digest/config, worker, counters, merchants, filters, page, incident summaries |
| `view(sourceId, incidentId)` | Original incident UUID | Original incident, sanitized event history, latest notification ID, worker, revisions, route choices and per-side capture problems |
| `configure(sourceId, input)` | `config,expectedConfigRevision` | Original new configuration revision/digest |
| `acknowledge(sourceId, incidentId, input)` | `expectedRevision,by,notes` | Original updated incident |
| `notify(sourceId, incidentId, input)` | `expectedRevision,expectedNotificationId` | Original incident/event ID and event status |
| `notification(sourceId, eventId, input)` | `expectedAttempts,action,by` | Original event status and attempt counters |
| `inspectDestination(sourceId, input)` | `expectedConfigRevision` | Original destination inspection plus source and observed configuration identity |
| `start(sourceId, input)` | `expectedConfigRevision,expectedConfigHash` | Source and current worker state after the original watcher becomes ready |
| `stop(sourceId)` | None | Source and worker state after this console's worker drains |
| `prepareCase(sourceId, incidentId, input)` | `expectedRevision,workspaceText,routeId` | `source,incidentId,revision,handoff,html,report` |
| `close()` | None | Idempotent promise that drains all console-owned workers |

The `expectedNotificationId` property is required by the console method.
Use the latest displayed event UUID, or explicit `null` when the incident has
no retained event. Configuration revisions and incident revisions are distinct
from the frequently changing whole-directory revision.

Worker results have `ownership` (`console`, `external`, or `none`),
`status` (`STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `STOPPING`, `STOPPED`, or `FAILED`),
`canStart`, `canStop`, original `recorded` metadata and a stable `error` code.
Route results have `id,method,path?,sides`; `captureProblems` is keyed by
`before` or `after` and contains stable `error,detail` fields.

`incidentProblem(error)` returns `{status,error,detail}` for the local API.
Input errors use 400 or 422, missing selections use 404, stale revisions and
original ownership/queue conflicts use 409, and unavailable storage uses 503.
Refresh a stale selection, correct the indicated input or storage condition,
then continue the same original incident operation.

# Merchant workspace

Keep a merchant case queue, diagnose each route, inspect its runtime and delivery outcomes, review repairs, and prepare internal workorders in one local workspace. The same original captures move through each stage. The optional case desk retains multiple merchant drafts, follow-up ownership and dates, original runtime support files or usage periods, search, work status and saved versions across restarts.

The [Implementation and receiving desk](IMPLEMENTATION.md) continues the same workorder through assigned tasks, original deliverables, technical and customer receiving, measured effort, source updates and complete case handover. The browser, installed `merchant-implementation` CLI and original merchant MCP share the same retained case.

## Open the workspace

From the repository root, with Node 22 or newer:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs
```

For a durable merchant queue, add `--cases-dir "$HOME/.local/share/stellar-forge/merchant-cases" --port 8784`. Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` address. No package installation, account, database or hosted service is required. Nothing is probed on page load. [Case desk operations](CASE_DESK.md) covers the complete save, reopen, follow-up, concurrent-tab and version-recovery flow.

The optional [Handoffs desk](HANDOFF_DESK.md) receives an existing merchant MCP support export, resumes its original saved transfer and opens the received case in this same editor. Configure private host-side source aliases with `--handoff-sources` alongside `--cases-dir`; the browser receives no endpoint credentials or local paths. Completed handoffs and their later case edits remain usable after restart or while the source is offline.

The [runtime support flow](RUNTIME_SUPPORT.md) accepts an original SF93 process packet or the original SF30 `history.json` plus matching SF97 `report.json`. It retains exact sources, method/path variants, saved session coverage and optional native journal reconciliation through case save/reopen and complete private handoff. HEAD is available alongside the other five original seller methods; the maintained diagnostic still performs only its existing unpaid GET/OPTIONS work when original catalog evidence supports GET.

The existing workorder stage accepts either the selected diagnostic captures or **Attached runtime case**. Owner-entered scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria and commercial terms are saved with the case. The same SF77 packet, readable workorder and checklist retain the original source review; a runtime-only case can proceed directly to this handoff. [Runtime workorders](RUNTIME_SUPPORT.md#prepare-a-workorder-from-this-case) covers source selection, reopening and the complete-handoff CLI.

## Diagnose → review → prepare

1. **Diagnose a route.** Enter the actual seller resource, facilitator catalog, buyer origin, Stellar network, public payment recipient and advertised buyer method. Set the credentialed-browser option to match the intended buyer, confirm authorization, then choose **Run diagnosis**. Review the findings and captured scope.
2. **Check browser access when needed.** A POST capture offers a separate **Check browser access** action. Review the displayed seller, origin and credential mode, then authorize its OPTIONS-only check. The original eligibility gate may decline an unsuitable capture without making a request. It never sends a POST.
3. **Keep the before capture.** Choose **Use as before**. Its exact diagnosis bytes and any displayed browser check remain selected in the tab. After the separately agreed repair, run the same diagnosis and optional browser check, then choose **Use as after**. Selected captures survive the next diagnosis. **Save before**, **Save after** and **Save browser check** preserve these original files whenever you need them.
4. **Review changes.** Choose **Compare changes**. The result explains remaining, new and no-longer-observed findings, including incomplete coverage and unconfirmed credential policy. Original CLI captures can instead be opened in the same file slots. Optional POST browser checks must be supplied as a pair, each bound to its unchanged diagnosis.
5. **Prepare workorder.** The selected captures are already available here. Enter the actual workorder reference, seller and relationship owner. Record existing seller permission and the owner-approved proposal price only when you have their records. Delivery cost is optional: leave it blank when unknown, and enter zero only for a recorded zero. The form and packet display a known adverse margin without changing the approved fee. Safe defaults leave permission unrecorded and price withheld. A before capture alone is sufficient; select **Use only the before diagnosis** to deliberately omit an available repair comparison.
6. **Create and save.** Choose **Create workorder**, then download the readable HTML workorder, Markdown handoff checklist and JSON. Open the HTML locally for review. Nothing is sent. Use **Reuse saved owner terms** to import or save the form as JSON for another session.

The three stages also work with existing files: you can open a before capture and prepare a workorder without running a diagnosis or comparison first. A workorder with an after capture computes its review through the original comparator automatically.

Changing a selected capture clears any comparison and workorder made from it. Replacing a diagnosis also clears that side’s browser check. Changing owner terms, selecting an import, or changing baseline-only mode clears prior workorder downloads; failed imports leave the existing form values intact and require a fresh workorder. Late responses cannot restore outdated results.

This is an unpaid diagnostic and internal workorder workflow. Seller acceptance, delivery approval, commercial contact, invoices and payments remain separate owner decisions. No consent, price or acceptance is inferred from a technical result.

## Save the source files

With `--cases-dir`, **Save case** explicitly stores the original workspace plus case metadata. Reopening resets transient probe authorization and regenerates derived comparison/workorder views from the retained inputs. Without that option, state lives in the current tab and process. Portable workspace files remain available in either mode. There is no localStorage, telemetry or automatic saving.

Current captures use **Save diagnosis** and **Save browser check**. Retained selections have their own save buttons, so an earlier capture remains downloadable after a new diagnosis. These exact bytes also feed comparison and workorder generation. Do not reformat a diagnosis after generating its browser check: that check contains the SHA-256 of the original file.

Human result titles appear in the workspace; original schema names, states, hashes, nested observations and limits remain in expandable **Source details** and downloaded JSON. A file hash identifies bytes; it does not independently authenticate an observation or establish seller permission.

## Existing modules and boundaries

SF74 is the local UI and HTTP adapter. It imports the existing engines without copying their decision logic:

| Operation | Original implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Route diagnosis | SF70 `parseArgs` / `capture`, using SF52 and SF68 |
| POST browser check | SF72 `evaluate` and its original eligibility gate |
| Before/after comparison | SF76 `compare` |
| Workorder, HTML and checklist | SF77 `buildPacket`, `renderHtml`, `renderChecklist` |

`server.mjs` serves the static native HTML/CSS/ES modules and same-origin API. `console.mjs` owns transient selections, cancellation and explicit downloads. `terms-editor.mjs` owns only the form fields; the original SF77 builder remains authoritative for terms, economics and acceptance.

`case-desk.mjs` adds the original page's merchant queue and case lifecycle. `case-store.mjs` persists byte-exact v1 workspaces and compact workflow metadata under a process-selected private directory. It uses revision checks and atomic head selection to preserve concurrent edits; the original diagnostics remain unchanged.

- The server binds to literal 127.0.0.1 and rejects unexpected Host or Origin. CSP blocks external page content. No third-party JavaScript, wallet or database is used. Optional handoff sources use host-provisioned MCP credentials, which remain outside the browser.
- Only **Run diagnosis** and the separately authorized browser check invoke diagnostic network operations. The network gate permits one intake or preflight at a time.
- The credentialed-browser option checks the stricter policy without sending cookies or authorization. Before and after must retain the same mode. Unknown legacy mode remains unconfirmed and cannot establish the technical milestone or cleared findings.
- Comparison and workorder generation are offline and in memory. Each uploaded source or terms file is limited to 2,000,000 bytes. Exact file bytes are transported as base64, decoded and hashed before parsing; no server filesystem path is accepted.
- `POST /api/workorder` takes `before`, `terms`, optional `after`, and optional paired `postBefore` / `postAfter` original file bytes. It returns the original `packet`, `html` and `checklist`. HTML is downloaded as a document, never inserted into the workspace DOM. A precomputed comparison verdict cannot substitute for source captures.
- Workorders preserve the original HTTPS scope requirement. `--allow-loopback` exists only for explicit local diagnostic fixtures; HTTP fixture captures are not commercial workorder inputs.
- Use public recipient addresses and authorized endpoints. Do not enter private keys or tokens.

For the original seller-side operation workflow, see [seller pilot](../sf82-seller-pilot/README.md). Commercial ownership and account submission remain with their existing owners.

# Runtime support in the merchant case desk

The existing SF74 case carries a merchant's original runtime packet or retained usage period, its repair follow-up, native delivery reconciliation and operator ownership. The original SF30 history producer, SF93 collector and SF97 analyzer/reconciler remain responsible for their source products. SF74 imports their exact files and connects them to its saved case lifecycle.

## Collect from the existing seller

Use the seller and operations addresses printed by the original SF30 or native commerce launcher. The existing collector reads only the original health, offers, snapshot and metrics endpoints:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/bundle.mjs \
  --seller http://127.0.0.1:8423 --ops http://127.0.0.1:8424 \
  --out /private/support/merchant-before
```

The parent directory must exist; the output directory is create-only. Keep all four resulting files together: `bundle.json`, `operator-brief.md`, `metrics.prom` and `manifest.json`. For a follow-up, use a new output directory. An existing retained packet can be imported without collecting again.

Start the same merchant case desk with Node 22 or newer:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs \
  --cases-dir /private/merchant-cases --port 8784
```

## Attach, review, save and resume

1. Open the merchant case or start a new one. Enter the actual route and buyer settings in **Diagnose**, and record the owner, next action and follow-up in **Cases**. You can use runtime support without running a diagnosis.
2. In **Runtime**, select the four original packet files together. Choose **Inspect selected files**. SF74 checks original file hashes, manifest/session agreement and the original runtime structure before offering its advertised routes.
3. Select the route matching the current case method and choose **Attach to case**. This explicitly maps an operator-provided packet to the current case. The packet does not contain or independently establish the public merchant origin. The mapping retains the exact case inputs; subsequent input changes visibly separate the saved capture from the current case.
4. Review selected-route HTTP outcomes and the original runtime alerts. For a repair follow-up, select **After / follow-up** and import a new original packet. The interval view subtracts cumulative counters only within the same observer session, start time, seller mode and unchanged case mapping, in chronological order with no counter regression. A restarted seller has a separate window. Observer errors or detachment remain visible. Starts and finishes in an interval can belong to different requests.
5. Choose **Save case**. The original bytes and mapping are saved under the same revision as the workspace and follow-up metadata. An interrupted or stale save preserves the existing case and browser draft. Selected files must be attached or explicitly cleared before saving so they cannot be silently omitted.
6. Reopen the case after restart, or open an earlier **Saved version**. Runtime source checks and the original native reconciler run again on the retained files. Opening an earlier version creates a draft; saving it retains all intervening history.

Each attached capture has original-file downloads. **Remove before/after** removes a capture from the current draft only; a later save preserves the old capture in prior versions. No journal writer or merchant control is opened by intake, save, reopen or review.

## Optional original native delivery records

Attach all three optional files to a runtime capture:

| File | Original source |
| --- | --- |
| `report.json` | SF97 `analyze.mjs` report from the same original seller session and configuration |
| `events.ndjson` | Copied original SF98 native-success event journal |
| `deliveries.ndjson` | Copied original SF98 delivery-state journal |

Use a coherent retained journal pair. Empty journals are permitted; incomplete final records, conflicting event IDs, orphan delivery records and invalid original states are rejected by the original native reconciler. SF74 does not open the live outbox to obtain these files or synthesize a revenue report from the smaller SF93 packet.

The integration calls the original `sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/native-reconcile.mjs` **reconcile(report, events, deliveries)**. Original method, network, asset, amount, recipient-option matching and delivery outcomes stay intact. The UI shows the selected route's native notices, inbox acceptance, pending/exhausted delivery, event assignments and original repair flags. The complete original files remain retained for wider accounting review.

A same-session SF97 report can have a different capture time. Its own window is displayed; an exact source-snapshot match is distinguished from a separate snapshot in that session. HTTP counters are never assigned to a payment option, callback acceptance is not treated as customer fulfillment, and the case workflow status is not changed by a diagnostic result.

## Support a merchant across restarts

Use **Retained period across restarts** when a case needs the original saved usage history rather than one process snapshot. Obtain `history.json` from the existing operations console or its `/history.json?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` endpoint. Its optional `routeId` selects one original route. Keep the export unchanged and create the matching original SF97 report:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/analyze.mjs \
  --config /private/merchant/seller.json \
  --terms /private/merchant/pricing.json \
  --history /private/captures/history.json \

```

The original [SF97 period guide](../sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/README.md#review-a-retained-period-across-seller-restarts) covers history retention, live selection and merchant pricing. A saved pricing-workspace version also provides its original `history.json` and `report.json` downloads. The case desk does not rebuild a pricing report from counters or create a replacement support packet.

1. Set the case's actual method and resource. In **Runtime**, choose **Retained period across restarts** and the baseline or follow-up position.
2. Select `history.json` and its matching `report.json` together. Optionally choose both copied original SF98 journals. Journals are a pair; omitting them means native delivery was not supplied, while supplying two empty files represents an actual empty source pair.
3. **Inspect selected files** checks the exact history SHA-256 in the SF97 report, normalizes both original history representations, and calls the existing native reconciler for its report, route and complete payment-option checks. A report created from a different export is rejected even when the date labels or totals look alike. Original seller/terms hashes remain attached; the case mapping itself does not authenticate a public merchant.
4. Select the exact retained method and path. Current configured routes, older path/method variants and removed routes remain distinct. A current route with no saved observations is explicitly labeled; its absence is not measured zero traffic. Changing a path or case mapping never silently moves observations to a current quote.
5. Attach and review. The case shows original UTC days, saved session states and intervals, selected-route membership, all retained variants for the route, original payment-option identities, native event decisions and excluded-event reasons. Per-day starts and completions may belong to different requests. P95 is the original aggregate histogram bound.
6. Save the case, reopen it or an earlier saved version, and prepare the same complete support handoff. The original history, report and optional journal bytes remain downloadable and accompany the existing notes, owner and follow-up. You can remove a draft attachment while keeping earlier saved versions.

The original history validator checks retained day/route/session structure and aggregate conservation; SF74 does not create another history writer. Modern history exports carry exact per-session UTC day/route membership. Earlier original exports remain supported with their coarser session/day coverage. Interrupted checkpoints end at their saved capture times; quiet gaps between sessions remain gaps. An active session's retained counters also stop at its captured checkpoint. Reopening a case reads its saved files without polling a merchant.

### Compare a repair over time

Two period attachments for the same case inputs and exact method/path show their independent observed counts and response shares. When the first selected UTC period ends before the second starts and both retain the selected route, the view also shows changes in percentage points for 2xx, 402, 5xx and disconnected shares. HTTP shares use actual response counts; disconnect share uses completed outcomes. Empty denominators remain unknown. Differences do not establish that a repair caused a change in traffic.

Overlapping or reversed selections display both original periods without subtracting totals or claiming a rate change. They may include the same requests or native events. Different method/path variants, case mappings, or a process packet paired with a period retain separate views. The existing same-session SF93 before/after counter subtraction is unchanged.

For a current selected route, native assignment uses the original SF97 complete option and recipient identity together with actual saved session/day/route coverage. The existing reconciler leaves events in session gaps, outside the selected dates/route, or without saved route coverage out of its option totals. Older or ambiguous route variants remain unassigned. A case mapped to a historical path can inspect those event decisions; current saved payment-option outcomes are labeled as current reference data. Atomic quantities remain separate for every native option. No report total is summed across the two attachments.

### Original incident handoff

The existing SF93 incident operator can continue importing its unchanged four-file packets through `inspectRuntimeFiles` and `exportRuntimeHandoff`. Its incident ID, registered merchant ID, acknowledgment, status and timestamps belong in the original handoff metadata notes and next action. This case can then retain the incident packet beside a separately selected period or follow-up capture. Incident collection, acknowledgment, notifications and recovery remain with the original SF93 service; the case does not operate a second watcher.

## Prepare a workorder from this case

The **Prepare a merchant workorder** stage can use **Attached runtime case** directly. A runtime incident or retained period does not need a separate SF70 diagnosis. The same original SF77 builder owns the commercial terms and generates the workorder JSON, readable HTML and acceptance checklist.

1. Attach and review the original runtime sources. The latest attached capture's saved merchant mapping must match the current case; an earlier baseline may retain its distinct mapping and comparison result. Save the prepared intent in the Service case before executing it. Then use `refund_review` to ACCEPT or REJECT the returned packet. ACCEPT either binds a matching original `purchase_item_id`, or explicitly requests `register_original_purchase:true` when the original native proof supports it. Those two choices are mutually exclusive.

The original buyer records its purchase, credits and source packet. It retains every native adjustment status, including outcomes that have not become verified credits.

### 3. Code the purchase and returns

Use the original cost center and asset label controls. `state.labels` is an array; saving labels supplies the complete selected `assets` array. Labels change presentation and declared native scales, not the original amounts.

Set an explicit operator recognition date. It is not a claimed transfer or settlement date. Choose the original nonoverlapping period covering that date.

Purchase and credit allocation amounts are exact native base-unit strings. The original validators require purchase allocations to equal the original settled purchase and credit allocations to respect the remaining original dimensions. No JavaScript floating-point currency calculation or assumed exchange rate is introduced.

An existing current purchase coding is preserved. When the purchase has several dimensions, supply explicit credit allocations. A single original dimension can receive the exact verified credit amount with that same center, project and account code.

A closed original period requires a named operator and reason before it can be reopened. Source or coding changes continue through that original period; earlier closes remain retained.

### 4. Review and issue the period

Read the actual native period report. Each `issues[]` entry carries:

```js
{
  code, item_id, request_id, source_name, description, source_capture,
  basis, allowed_kinds, resolved, disposition, group
}
```

Render each issue's own `allowed_kinds`. Some issues permit carry-forward or exclusion; duplicate-event groups have different original choices. The current `basis` must accompany an explicit disposition. Do not invent an enum or automatically exclude an unresolved payment.

A READY review captures the exact period context. Close uses that specific review ID and the original version checks. The issued source includes the selected accepted merchant capture and complete native outcome history.

### 5. Deliver and receive the accountant's return

The delivery action captures four native files from one selected buyer revision:

| File | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `issued-buyer-accountant-source.json` | Complete original issued period and its source identities |
| `buyer-expense-accountant-edition.zip` | Original accountant period packet |
| `buyer-bookkeeping-complete-period.zip` | Complete native period and bookkeeping history at the selected revision |
| `buyer-expense-complete-project.zip` | Portable original application source, project database and retained files |

`accountant_create` consumes the exact issued source bytes from that saved delivery outcome. Its original handoff ID and request remain stable. The outcome retains all files emitted by the original AccountantWorkspace, with exact names, bytes, hashes and base64.

Staff can edit the original accountant CSV using its existing editable fields, preview it in the original accountant application, and save its original return. The generated `buyer-return.json` carries that native handoff and return chain.

In Support, upload that full original JSON file and call the return-preview operation before saving. Show the native match, previous return, overlaps and current preview hash. The save includes every explicitly selected overlapping `other_handoffs[].return_id` in `supersedes`; a reason is required when superseding. Empty supersedes is valid only when no overlap needs replacement. Accepted bookkeeping changes do not rewrite issued amounts.

## Recovery and concurrent work

Prepare writes the complete native intent before dispatch and keeps the first selected revision and bytes. Execute requires that same prepared intent to be present in the original case.

For buyer mutations, execute first reads the original native request journal. Only an actual `REQUEST_NOT_COMMITTED` result permits initial dispatch. If the mutation response is lost, the same journal can recover its committed result. Other failed reads preserve uncertainty. The original native fingerprint binds method, path, payload and expected revision.

If the request is definitely uncommitted and the live revision changed, staff refresh and make a new explicit decision. They retain the old intent. A stale request is never silently rebased.

The accountant's original create/apply methods also check retained request IDs before current revision. Existing matching results are reused. A changed body under the same ID is rejected.

Case-save uncertainty is separate from native mutation uncertainty. Read the case for the exact accepted material before another save. A case conflict can be composed against the new case revision while retaining the unchanged native material and peer fields. It does not justify replaying a different payment or buyer request.

Original files are immutable operation artifacts. Their full descriptor, base64 and hashes remain in the selected outcome, case export and receiving outputs. A changed alias or workspace identity is rejected. Later live buyer or case activity does not change an already issued delivery.

**Retain first service edition** adds the complete reviewed terms to this case. To change them, select an existing edition and use **Open edition to revise**. ### Continuous and business calendars

The calendar controls define when target minutes accrue:

- **24 hours, every day** uses continuous local calendar days.
- **Local business calendar** uses the selected weekday windows.
- **Holidays and special dates** replace the normal windows for that exact local date in either calendar mode.

Enter local times as 09:00-12:00, 13:00-17:00. A blank weekday or special-date window is closed. An ending time of 24:00 is allowed. Split overnight coverage at midnight across the two relevant dates. Daily windows must be ordered without overlaps after normalization.

The time zone is an installed IANA name such as America/New_York. Reporting month dates use this time zone; the original incident and capture timestamps remain UTC. Daylight-saving transitions are resolved by the model’s retained clock policy: an ambiguous boundary uses the earliest start and latest end, and a skipped local boundary advances to its next actual minute. The resulting service time counts actual elapsed minutes inside those windows.

An agreement can retain up to 1,000 special-date rows. Empty unfinished rows remain in the case draft until completed or removed; retaining the actual terms edition validates every date and window.

### Agreement history in a report

Select the latest agreement edition that belongs in the report. Its earlier editions remain part of the original terms history. Each incident uses its governing edition at the original opening, then that edition’s effective end, source and merchant binding. Later changes preserve the target associated with an earlier opening. An ended or rebound edition continues to govern its period and prevents earlier open-ended coverage from reappearing.

The calculation merges overlapping excluded intervals and subtracts their overlap with actual service windows. It reports calendar minutes before exclusion, excluded minutes and service minutes after exclusion separately.

## Review and retain the monthly report

Select the service edition and complete reporting month. The month is inclusive local calendar dates in the selected service time zone. Set an explicit UTC report cutoff. Retaining a new compatible incident snapshot defaults this cutoff to its actual capture time.

Select all source snapshots needed for the month’s original chronology. The desk identifies captures outside the selected agreement history. Relevant snapshots may carry historical incident bindings even when the merchant’s current registration has changed. Original incident identity and revision checks reconcile repeated incidents across the selected snapshots.

Select each reviewed exclusion that should apply, then choose **Review monthly report**. Changing the month, cutoff, service edition, capture list or exclusion list requires a new review.

The report contains the full selected terms history, source identities, exclusions and original incident details. ### Read the clocks

| Report field or state | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Actual elapsed minutes | Wall-clock time from opening through the observed completion or cutoff. |
| Calendar minutes | Actual minutes inside the applicable service windows before exclusions. |
| Excluded minutes | Overlap removed by the explicitly selected reviewed exclusions. |
| Service minutes | Calendar minutes remaining after those exclusions. |
| MET | The original recorded acknowledgment or recovery completed within its target. |
| MISSED | The relevant service-clock target was exceeded. |
| OPEN | The target clock is still open and within its target at the evaluated cutoff. |
| RETIRED | The registration was retired while the remaining clock was within target. |
| UNACKNOWLEDGED | The incident recovered within the response target without a recorded human acknowledgment. |
| Evaluated cutoff | The earlier of the explicit report cutoff and that incident’s actual selected capture time. |

The response clock uses the original human acknowledgment. Recovery uses the original recovered transition. An over-target clock remains missed when the registration is later retired. The table keeps the original owner, capture, agreement edition and follow-up alongside each result.

Additional source incidents appear with their selection reason when the chosen terms do not cover their opening, binding or condition, or the retained capture predates the reporting period. The preview also identifies selected exclusions that did not apply to the report’s incidents.
